title: Avocado Brioche Sourdough Bread
text: avocado brioche sourdough bread source: wellandgood.com ingredients - 10 grams sourdough starter - 30 grams water - 60 grams bread flour - 300 grams bread flour - 150 grams ripe avocado - 5ml lemon juice - 100 grams sweetened condensed milk - 1 large egg - 30 grams milk - 15 grams sugar (optional) - 30 grams soft butter - 60 grams stiff starter - 6 grams salt - 0.5 grams dry yeast (optional, to reduce sourness) instructions 1. at 10pm, add starter to the water and whisk together, add flour, mix well, and form a ball. 2. roll it into a tight roll, place in jar, cover with water, and let sit at room temperature 23°c to 26°c until it increases in size and starts to float on the top of the water. 3. in about 8 to 10 hours, the top of the starter will dry and the bottom will start to melt in water; use the center part of it. 4. keeping stiff starter in the water will help to reduce its acidity and sourness of the final product. 5. at 8am on day 2, cut fresh ripe avocado and add it to the food processor along with lemon juice, sweetened condensed milk, regular milk, and an egg, then purée together. 6. if using dry yeast, add it to the food processor as well. 7. add purée, stiff sourdough starter, and sugar to flour and mix on low speed for 2 to 3 minutes until well incorporated. 8. add salt and mix for a couple more minutes until the dough forms a ball and seems stiff. 9. add soft butter and mix for 10 more minutes until the dough is well incorporated and comes together. 10. cover and let it proof for 3 to 4 hours at 24°c to 27°c. 11. during that time, perform two stretches and folds; the dough should become slightly puffy. 12. at 12pm to 1pm, transfer the dough to the fridge for cold fermentation for 8 to 9 hours. 13. at 10pm, remove the dough from the fridge. 14. shape as desired into a loaf pan or divide into 3 or 4 pieces and braid. 15. put a sheet of parchment paper on the bottom of your loaf pan. 16. transfer the shaped loaf into the loaf pan. 17. cover the dough and let it proof overnight for 8 to 9 hours at 21°c to 22°c until it doubles in volume. 18. sprinkle some flour on top of your loaf or egg wash it. 19. preheat the oven to 191°c. 20. bake for 35 to 40 minutes until golden brown. 21. enjoy your avocado brioche sourdough loaf.

title: Banana Peel Flour
text: banana peel flour ingredients - ripe banana peels, washed and dried instructions 1. wash and dry the banana peels. 2. cut the peels into small pieces. 3. spread the peel pieces on a dehydrator tray or a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. 4. dehydrate the peels in a dehydrator at 57°c (57°c) for 8-12 hours or in an oven at the lowest setting for 4-6 hours, until the peels are dry and crisp. 5. grind the dried peels in a blender or food processor until they become a fine powder. 6. sift the powder through a fine-mesh sieve to remove any large pieces. 7. store the banana peel flour in an airtight container in a cool, dry place.

title: Bazlama Turkish Pita
text: bazlama turkish pita ingredients - 500 g (454g) flour - 150 ml (5 fl. oz) warm milk - 150 ml (5 fl. oz) warm water - 5ml salt - 30ml dry yeast - 45ml olive oil - chopped parsley - chili flakes instructions 1. whisk flour with salt and yeast. 2. add warm water and milk and knead just until liquids absorb. 3. add olive oil and knead until smooth dough forms, around 10 minutes. 4. form the dough into a ball, cover with vegetable oil and set aside in a warm place for 1 hour or until doubled in size. 5. when the dough is done rising, cut it into 6 pieces and roll each piece into a ball. 6. roll out each flatbread and place on a pan preheated on medium-high heat. 7. cook for 5-6 minutes, 2.5-3 minutes on each side, flipping until the flatbread rises up to make a pocket in the middle. 8. brush each hot flatbread with oil, then top with parsley and chili flakes.

title: Beef Pot Pie
text: beef pot pie source: gooddinnermom.com ingredients - 907g boneless beef chuck-eye roast, trimmed and cut into ¾ inch pieces - salt and pepper - 45ml olive oil or avocado oil, divided - 113g baby bella mushrooms, trimmed and quartered - 1 onion, finely chopped - 3 carrots, peeled and cut into ½ inch pieces - 30ml tomato paste - 4 garlic cloves, minced - 120ml dry red wine or 120ml water - 45ml all-purpose flour - 480ml beef broth - 15ml soy sauce - 15ml worcestershire sauce - 1 bay leaf - 240ml frozen peas - 8ml chopped fresh thyme, divided - 1 large egg, lightly beaten - 1 9-inch store-bought pie dough round instructions 1. adjust oven rack to the lower-middle position and heat oven to 177°c. 2. pat beef cubes dry with paper towels and season generously with salt and pepper. 3. heat 22ml oil in a dutch oven over medium-high heat and add half of the beef, cooking until well browned on all sides, about 7 minutes. 4. transfer browned beef to a bowl or plate and add the remaining uncooked beef to the same bowl. 5. reduce heat to medium, add the remaining 22ml oil to the pot, and stir in mushrooms, onion, and carrots, cooking until lightly browned, about 5 minutes. 6. add tomato paste and garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds. 7. stir in wine or water and cook until mostly evaporated, about 2 minutes. 8. sprinkle flour over the vegetables and stir for 1 minute. 9. slowly add broth, soy sauce, worcestershire sauce, and bay leaf, scraping the bottom of the pot to release flavor. 10. return all beef to the pot, bring to a simmer, cover, and transfer to the oven. 11. bake until beef is tender, about 1 hour 15 minutes, testing a piece and adding 60ml water and returning to oven for 20–30 minutes if still chewy. 12. remove from oven and increase oven temperature to 204°c. 13. if filling looks dry, transfer meat to a bowl, add ¼–120ml water to the pot, and scrape up browned bits to create a rich sauce, then stir back into the meat mixture. 14. discard bay leaf and stir in thyme and peas, then taste and season with more salt and pepper as needed. 15. spray a 9-inch deep-dish pie plate with cooking spray and add beef filling. 16. brush the rim of the dish with beaten egg, place pie dough over the top so it slightly overhangs the edges, fold excess dough inward, and crimp edges with your fingers. 17. cut a ½-inch hole in the center of the crust and cut six small slits around it to vent steam. 18. brush the crust with remaining egg and sprinkle lightly with salt, pepper, and thyme. 19. place pie on a rimmed baking sheet and bake until golden brown, 20–30 minutes. 20. let pie cool on a rack for 15 minutes before serving.

title: Beer Batter Fish Made Great
text: beer batter fish made great source: allrecipes.com ingredients - 2 quarts vegetable oil for frying - 8 (113g) fillets cod - salt and pepper to taste - 240ml all-purpose flour - 30ml garlic powder or to taste - 30ml paprika or to taste - 10ml salt or to taste - 10ml ground black pepper or to taste - 1 large egg, beaten - 1 (340g) can or bottle beer, extra cold instructions 1. heat oil in a deep fryer to 185°c. 2. rinse cod fillets and pat dry, then season with salt and pepper. 3. mix flour, garlic powder, paprika, salt, and pepper in a large bowl, add the beaten egg and stir well to combine. 4. gradually mix in enough beer to make a thin batter. 5. dip cod fillets into the batter to coat thoroughly. 6. carefully lower fillets one at a time into the hot oil, frying several at a time without crowding the vessel. 7. fry the fillets, turning once, until cooked through and golden brown, about 2 minutes per side. 8. drain the fried fillets on paper towels and serve warm.

title: Beer Battered Onion Rings
text: beer battered onion rings source: melissassouthernstylekitchen.com ingredients - sweet onions such as vidalia onions, sliced into 1/2-inch thick rings - one 340g bottle or can of beer (lager or stout) - all purpose flour - buttermilk - hot sauce - seasoned salt - seafood seasoning (seafood magic, old bay, or similar) - onion powder - garlic powder - smoked paprika - ground cumin - peanut oil or vegetable oil for frying - mayonnaise (for dipping sauce) - chili sauce (for dipping sauce) - green onion (for dipping sauce) - roasted red pepper (for dipping sauce) - garlic cloves (for dipping sauce) - lemon juice (for dipping sauce) - creole or cajun seasoning (for dipping sauce) - prepared horseradish (for dipping sauce) instructions instructions not provided in source text.

title: Best Basic Pizza Dough Recipe
text: best basic pizza dough recipe source: foodrepublic.com ingredients - 1 packet active dry yeast - 30ml olive oil - 5ml kosher salt - 720ml all- purpose flour - 240ml slightly warm water instructions 1. in the bowl of a mixer fitted with a dough hook, pour the warm water in and sprinkle with yeast. let stand until foamy, about 5 minutes. do not use hot water or it will kill the yeast and your dough will not rise. 2. add the sugar, oil, and salt into yeast mixture. 3. with the mixer on low, slowly add the flour and mix until a dough ball forms. you may want to transfer to a floured work surface and knead by hand until a smooth ball comes together. transfer dough to an oiled bowl and brush top with oil. cover bowl with plastic wrap and set aside in a warm area for about an hour. the dough should double in size. 4. cut the dough in half. place both pieces on a floured work surface and gently knead. you can roll one piece out now into a 12- inch round. 5. to cook now, top with your favorite toppings. brush the exposed dough with olive oil and place in a 450 degree oven on a pizza stone (if you have one) for 12 to 15 minutes until the dough is golden brown. 6. to freeze the second piece, wrap the dough in plastic and place it in a resealable freezer bag for up to 3 months. 7. pizza 8. grilled blt pizza recipe 9. tarte flambée recipe

title: Best Brownies
text: best brownies ingredients - 2½ sticks unsalted butter, plus more softened for greasing - 227g good-quality semisweet chocolate (225 g), or bittersweet chocolate 60-70% cacao, roughly chopped - 180ml unsweetened dutch process cocoa powder (90 g), divided - 15ml espresso powder - 480ml granulated sugar (400 g) - 120ml dark brown sugar (110 g), packed - 10ml vanilla extract - 10ml kosher salt - 6 large eggs - 240ml all-purpose flour (125 g) - flaky sea salt for sprinkling instructions 1. grease a 9x13-inch dark metal pan with softened butter, then line with parchment paper, leaving overhang on all sides, and grease the parchment with softened butter. 2. combine the chopped chocolate, 60ml of cocoa powder, and espresso powder in a heatproof bowl and set aside. 3. add the butter to a small saucepan over medium heat and cook until it just comes to a vigorous simmer, about 5 minutes, swirling occasionally. 4. pour the hot butter over the chocolate mixture and let sit for 2 minutes, then whisk until completely smooth and melted. 5. combine the granulated sugar, brown sugar, vanilla extract, salt, and eggs in a large bowl and beat with an electric mixer on high speed until light and fluffy, about 10 minutes. 6. pour the slightly cooled chocolate and butter mixture into the egg mixture with the mixer on and blend until smooth. 7. position a rack in the middle of the oven and preheat to 177°c. 8. sift in the flour and remaining cocoa powder and gently fold with a rubber spatula until just combined. 9. pour the batter into the prepared pan and smooth the top with a spatula. 10. bake until lightly puffed on top, about 20 minutes. 11. remove the pan from the oven and lightly drop it on a flat surface 1-2 times until the brownies deflate slightly, then sprinkle with flaky sea salt. 12. return the pan to the oven and bake until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out fudgy but the edges look cooked through, about 20 minutes more. 13. set the brownies on a cooling rack and cool completely in the pan. 14. use the parchment paper to lift the cooled brownies out of the pan, cut into 24 bars, and serve.

title: Best Sourdough Pizza Crust (No Steel or Stone!)
text: best sourdough pizza crust (no steel or stone!) source: the clever carrot ingredients - 50 g active sourdough starter - 250 g water - 360 g bread flour - 7 g fine sea salt - 240 g pizza sauce (quick no-cook, sicilian tomato sauce, or pomodoro sauce) - fine sea salt - black pepper - handful fresh basil - freshly grated parmesan cheese - olive oil - 226 g whole-milk mozzarella block cheese, shredded (about 600ml) instructions 1. in the evening, combine the sourdough starter and water in a large mixing bowl and mix with a fork. 2. add the flour and salt and continue mixing, then finish by hand to fully incorporate the flour. 3. cover with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let rest for 30 minutes at room temperature. 4. return to the bowl and fold the dough over itself several times to create a rough ball. 5. transfer the dough to a lightly oiled 2 quart dough tub, cover, and let rise overnight at room temperature (about 20°c) for 10-12+ hours until it has almost doubled in size. 6. coat a non-stick 9x13-inch baking pan with 15ml of olive oil and rub the bottom and sides. 7. remove the dough directly into the pan and with oiled fingertips, gently dimple and stretch the dough to reach the corners and sides of the pan. 8. cover the pan with an inverted baking sheet and rest in a warm spot (such as a proofing box set to 26°c or a turned off oven with the light on) for 30 minutes. 9. return to the pan and dimple the dough again, gently lifting and stretching it as you go, then cover and rest for another 30 minutes while preheating the oven to 232°c. 10. place the baking pan on the bottom rack and bake the dough at 232°c for 15-18 minutes, or until the surface is set and the bottom crust is light golden brown. 11. top the par-baked pizza crust with tomato sauce spread over the entire surface including the crust. 12. season with salt and pepper, add fresh basil leaves, a fresh grating of parmesan cheese, and drizzle with olive oil. 13. sprinkle with mozzarella cheese, taking it to the corners and sides for crispy edges, and tuck any remaining cheese cubes into the corners. 14. bake at 232°c on the middle or top rack until the cheese is melted and broiled in some spots, about 12-15 minutes, or place under the broiler to crisp it up further.

title: Bim's Sourdough Pizza
text: bim's sourdough pizza ingredients - 1000 g bread flour (or 35% wholewheat and 65% bread flour) - 200 g active starter - 700 g water - 20 g olive oil - 20 g lard (or additional olive oil as substitute) - 20 g salt - 30 g honey, sugar, or maple syrup - extra flour for dusting - 30ml pizza sauce per pizza - mozzarella cheese - pizza toppings of choice instructions 1. in a large bowl, add starter, water, sugar, and flour and mix until everything is combined well. 2. rest the dough for 30 minutes. 3. add olive oil, lard, and salt, then mix well and ensure all salt is combined evenly in the flour. 4. rest the dough in a controlled temperature of 25 degrees celsius for 30 minutes. 5. perform a stretch and fold, then rest for 30 minutes. 6. use coil folds evenly for 30 minutes and repeat this step 3 more times for a total of 4 sets. 7. proof the dough for 2 to 4 hours in a controlled temperature. 8. after 2 to 3 hours when the dough has doubled in size, separate it into small balls of 250 to 300 g each. 9. brush olive oil all over the inside of small plastic round containers and shape the dough into balls. 10. place the dough balls in containers and cover the lids after brushing them with oil as well. 11. rest the dough in the refrigerator overnight or freeze for up to 2 months. 12. defrost in the refrigerator for 6 to 8 hours for slow defrosting, or leave on the counter for 2 to 3 hours. 13. dust the top of the dough with bread flour and pour the dough out from the container. 14. use your hands to spread the dough and form the edges to create a unique sourdough pizza crust, shaping it into a nice circle of about 10 inches. 15. heat a pan on the stovetop until it is hot and place the pizza dough in it. 16. immediately add 30ml of pizza sauce in the middle and use the back of a spoon to spread it evenly. 17. top with your favorite pizza toppings and a generous amount of mozzarella cheese. 18. let the pizza cook in the pan for 3 to 4 minutes until the crust begins to create bubbles. 19. transfer the pizza to a hot preheated oven with the top heat set to 250 degrees celsius for 5 minutes. 20. check frequently to ensure the pizza does not burn while the cheese melts and turns golden brown. 21. serve the pizza while hot.

title: Biscotti Mandelbrot with Chocolate, Hazelnuts and Orange
text: biscotti mandelbrot with chocolate, hazelnuts and orange ingredients - 250g plain flour - 240g caster sugar - 2 large eggs or 3 small ones - 2 oranges, zested - 10ml fennel seeds - 200g hazelnuts (almonds or pistachios) - 150g dark chocolate - 5ml baking powder - icing sugar - a pinch of salt instructions 1. toast the nuts at 200°c until gently golden brown, then crush and chop into smaller pieces. 2. bash the fennel seeds with a bit of the sugar in a pestle and mortar then chop up the chocolate. 3. combine all the ingredients in a bowl and mix thoroughly. 4. split the mixture into two and roll out into logs on a bed of icing sugar to stop them sticking. 5. lay the logs on baking trays with parchment paper and bake at 200°c for 20 minutes. 6. remove from the oven, leave to cool a little, then chop into biscuits at an angle while still warm. 7. lay the biscotti out on the trays and bake again at 150°c for another 20 minutes or more, turning halfway through until they are dry but not too hard. 8. store in a jar when cooled and they will last for ages.

title: Black Bean And Chocolate Chili
text: black bean and chocolate chili source: geniuskitchen.com ingredients 29.58ml olive oil 354.88ml chopped onions 4 garlic cloves, minced 1 stalk celery, sliced 1-2 jalapeno chile, minced 14.79 ml cumin 9.85 ml oregano 2.46 ml cinnamon 0.25 ml ground cloves 4.92 ml ground coriander 14.79 ml chili powder 2.46 ml ground black pepper, to taste 2.46 ml salt, to taste 354.88 ml chopped bell peppers (red and green are nice) 2 (822.13 g) can black beans, rinsed and drained 411.06 g can diced tomatoes 14.79 ml fresh lime juice (optional) 14.79 ml soy sauce 42.52 g semisweet chocolate (about 60ml) tofu sour cream or scallion, for serving instructions in a large skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat. add onions and garlic and sauté until onions become soft and translucent, about 10 minutes. add the celery and chile, cover and cook for another five minutes more. reduce the heat and stir in spices, (cumin, oregano, cinnamon, cloves, coriander, chili powder, black pepper, salt) along with the bell peppers. cover again and cook for another five minutes. stir often to keep the spices from burning. if the pan gets too dry add a little liquid from the diced tomatoes, or some water. next, add the black beans, tomatoes, lime juice (if using) and soy sauce. let the chili simmer on low for 5 to 10 minutes, until it thickens slightly and flavors combine. stir in the chocolate. when chocolate has melted, taste to adjust the salt and pepper. serve with topping of your choice. i like a bit of vegan cheese, sour "cream" and scallions. chili can also makes a great filling to serve wrapped in flour tortillas, or in taco shells if you prefer. recipe content not provided.

title: Black Bean Brownies
text: black bean brownies ingredients - 260g cooked black beans - 50g rolled oats - 60g ghee, melted - 75g brown sugar - 3 large eggs - 55g unsweetened cocoa powder - 2ml baking powder - 1ml salt - 5ml vanilla extract - 15ml chia seeds - 30ml milk - 80g dark chocolate chips (56%) - 15ml cocoa nibs - 25g dried cranberries, chopped - 35g chopped walnuts instructions 1. rinse dried black beans and remove any debris. 2. quick soak by boiling for 2 minutes then letting sit for 1 hour, or overnight soak in plenty of water for 8 hours. 3. drain soaking water and add fresh water (about 720ml per 120ml of dried beans), then simmer for 60–90 minutes until tender, adding salt near the end of cooking. 4. preheat oven to 175°c (177°c) and line a square pan (20x20 cm) with parchment. 5. soak chia seeds in 30ml milk until gelled, and soak cranberries briefly in warm water if firm. 6. blend beans, oats, sugar, eggs, cocoa powder, baking powder, salt, vanilla, and chia gel in a food processor until smooth. 7. add melted ghee and half the melted chocolate chips, then pulse lightly to combine. 8. stir in cranberries, walnuts, and cocoa nibs by hand. 9. pour batter into pan and sprinkle with remaining chocolate chips. 10. bake for 22–26 minutes until edges look set but center is still slightly soft. 11. cool for at least 30 minutes before slicing.

title: Black Bean Brownies
text: black bean brownies ingredients - 260g cooked black beans - 35g almond flour - 15g quinoa flour - 80g butter, melted - 75g brown sugar - 3 large eggs - 55g unsweetened cocoa powder - 2ml baking powder - 1ml salt - 5ml vanilla extract - 15ml chia seeds - 30ml milk - 80g dark chocolate chips (56%) - 15ml cocoa nibs - 25g dried cranberries, chopped - 35g chopped walnuts instructions 1. rinse dried black beans and remove any debris. 2. quick soak the beans by boiling for 2 minutes then letting sit for 1 hour, or overnight soak in plenty of water for 8 hours. 3. drain the soaking water and add fresh water (about 720ml per 120ml of dried beans), then simmer for 60–90 minutes until tender, adding salt near the end of cooking. 4. preheat oven to 170°c and line a 20x20 cm square pan with parchment paper. 5. soak chia seeds in milk until gelled and soak cranberries briefly in warm water if they are firm. 6. in a food processor, blend the cooked beans, sugar, eggs, cocoa powder, baking powder, salt, vanilla, milk, and chia gel until smooth. 7. add melted butter and half the chocolate chips melted, then pulse lightly to combine. 8. stir in cranberries, walnuts, and cocoa nibs by hand. 9. pour the batter into the prepared pan and sprinkle with remaining chocolate chips. 10. bake for 18–22 minutes until the edges look set but the center is still slightly soft. 11. let cool for at least 30 minutes before slicing.

title: Black Radish, Endive and Apple Salad
text: black radish, endive and apple salad source: washingtonpost.com ingredients - 319ml apple cider vinegar - 60ml honey - 90ml fresh lemon juice (from 2 lemons) - 2 3-inch cinnamon sticks - 90ml olive oil - 4ml coarse sea salt - freshly ground black pepper - 3 or 4 small cox or pink lady apples - 8 belgian endive (trimmed and cored), leaves separated - 8 to 10 small black radishes, sliced very thin on a mandoline (may substitute 4 tender young turnips) - leaves from 0.5 bunches flat-leaf parsley, torn instructions step 1 combine the vinegar, honey, lemon juice and cinnamon sticks in a small saucepan over medium-high heat. once the mixture comes to a boil, cook for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it has reduced to a syrupy 6 to 105ml. remove from the heat; let cool completely, then discard the cinnamon sticks. step 2 whisk in the oil, along with the salt and a good pinch of pepper. step 3 just before serving, cut the apples horizontally into very thin slices, discarding any seeds. place them in a large serving bowl along with the endive, radish and parsley. pour the dressing over and toss gently to coat. step 4 serve right away.

title: Brandy Snaps
text: brandy snaps source: food52 ingredients - 240ml butter - 240ml granulated sugar - 160ml dark molasses - 5ml cinnamon - 2ml ginger - 480ml all-purpose flour - 20ml brandy - heavy whipping cream (optional) instructions 1. preheat oven to 163°c. 2. stir butter, sugar, molasses, cinnamon, and ginger together over low heat until melted. 3. remove from heat and add flour and brandy, then chill the dough until firm enough to shape, about 20 minutes. 4. roll dough into 3/4-inch balls and place on a baking sheet, leaving room for them to spread. 5. bake for approximately 12 to 13 minutes on a silpat- or parchment paper-lined cookie sheet. 6. when the cookies have cooled enough that you can touch them but they are still warm (about 5 minutes), use a spatula to pull them from the sheet and quickly roll them around a pencil to form tubes, using rubber gloves to prevent your fingers from burning. 7. if desired and serving immediately, whip up some heavy whipping cream and dot each end of the rolled cookies with it.

title: Brazilian Cheese Puffs Recipe
text: brazilian cheese puffs recipe source: rasamalaysia.com ingredients - 240ml whole milk - 120ml vegetable oil - 5ml salt - 284g (280g) tapioca flour - 2 large eggs - 360ml grated parmesan cheese instructions 1. preheat the oven to 177°c (176°c). line 2 baking sheets with parchment paper. place the milk, oil, and salt in a medium saucepan and bring to a gentle boil over medium heat, stirring occasionally. remove from heat as soon as large bubbles start to form in the milk. 2. add the tapioca flour and stir with a wooden spoon until well combined. transfer the dough to the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment. beat the dough for a few minutes at medium speed until it smooths out and cools down. 3. with the mixer on medium speed, add the eggs to the dough one at a time, waiting until the first egg is fully incorporated before adding the second. scrape down the sides of the bowl, then beat in the cheese until the dough becomes very sticky. 4. scoop the dough with a small ice cream scoop, spacing the dough 2 inches apart (12 per baking sheet). dip the scoop in water between scoops to prevent sticking. 5. bake for 15 minutes, then rotate the baking sheets from front to back. continue baking for another 10 to 15 minutes, until the puffs have puffed up and the bottoms turn golden brown.

title: Seeded Sourdough Bread
text: seeded sourdough bread source: marygracebread.substack.com ingredients - 70g sourdough starter - 8g salt - 40g sunflower seeds - 20g flax seeds, plus more for the crust - 30g pumpkin seeds - 300g filtered water - 130g wholemeal flour - 270g strong white flour instructions no instructions provided in source material.

title: Brine Calculator - Brine Salt to Water Ratio
text: brine calculator - brine salt to water ratio source: myfermentedfoods.com this is a tool page rather than a recipe. the content explains how to use a brine calculator to determine the correct salt-to-water ratio for fermenting vegetables, and provides reference information about brine percentages for different vegetables and the role of salt in fermentation. brine percentage guide for common vegetables: | vegetable | brine percentage | |-----------|------------------| | broccoli | 2% – 2.5% | | cauliflower | 2% | | celery | 1% – 2% | | cucumber | 3.5% – 5% | | garlic | 3% | | green beans | 2% | | onions | 5% | | potatoes | 2% | | radish | 5% | | tomatoes | 2% | | olives | 10% | general rule of thumb: for vegetable ferments, use 1-45ml of salt per quart of water.

title: Brioche Sourdough Buns
text: brioche sourdough buns ingredients - 30 g active sourdough starter - 40 g all-purpose flour - 40 g whole milk, cold from the fridge - 10 g sugar - 140 g whole milk - 35 g all-purpose flour - 460 g bread flour - 30 g sugar - 250 g eggs (approximately 5 eggs) - 12 g salt - 150 g unsalted butter, softened, in cubes - 1 egg - splash of water instructions 1. add all levain ingredients to a small mixing bowl and mix until just combined, then cover and let rise in a warm spot at 78-27°c for four hours, or until doubled in size. 2. add milk and flour to a small pot and heat over medium heat while stirring with a whisk until thickened and the mixture reaches 66°c. 3. transfer the tangzhong to a clean bowl, cover with plastic wrap touching the entire surface, and cool to room temperature. 4. add all main dough ingredients except salt and butter to the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a dough hook and mix until just combined. 5. rest and autolyse the dough for 30 minutes. 6. add the salt and knead on medium speed for 5–10 minutes. 7. slowly add the cubed softened butter one cube at a time, then scrape down the sides and continue mixing at medium-high speed until the dough passes the windowpane test. 8. transfer to a clean, lightly oiled bowl and proof for 3 hours at 24°c. 9. transfer to the fridge and cold-proof for 8–15 hours. 10. line two baking trays with parchment paper. 11. take the dough out of the fridge and divide into 12 equal pieces of approximately 90 g each. 12. roll each piece into a seamless round and arrange on the trays with space between them, then cover lightly with plastic wrap. 13. proof for 6–10 hours at 75-26°c until doubled in size. 14. preheat oven to 182°c. 15. brush the tops with egg wash. 16. bake for 15–20 minutes until golden brown and cool completely on a rack before slicing.

title: Brisket Rub
text: brisket rub ingredients - brown sugar 80ml - paprika 30ml - smoked paprika 15ml - freshly ground black pepper 12ml - freshly ground sea salt 15ml - garlic powder 15ml - onion powder 15ml - mustard powder 4ml - cayenne pepper 1ml - cumin 5ml - coriander 5ml instructions no instructions provided.

title: British Fish and Chips Recipe - The Daring Gourmet
text: british fish and chips recipe - the daring gourmet < https://www.daringgourmet.com/fish\-and\-chips/ fish and chips (british pub style) by kimberly killebrew no need to go down to your local pub, chippy or restaurant for the best beer-battered fish and chips. this recipe produces that perfectly crispy, flavorful result you're craving. recreate the perfect beer-battered fish and chips right at home! prep time 30minutes mins cook time 15minutes mins total time 1hour hr servings 4 servings ingredients 125 g all-purpose flour 5ml baking powder 5ml salt 295.74 ml light beer , very cold see note extra flour for dredging , chilled 680.39 g fresh cod, haddock or halibut , (or other firm-fleshed white fish), cut into 4 pieces and patted dry (important for enabling the batter to adhere) oil for frying use beef tallow instead of oil for the best traditional flavor (click link for recipe – it's super easy to make!) for the chips: 4 large russet potatoes or other high starch/low moisture potato , peeled, sliced thickly and put in a large bowl of cold water until ready to fry salt for sprinkling oil for frying quality british malt vinegar , for serving instructions to make the chips: heat the oven to 93°c. heat the oil in a deep fryer or a large heavy pan or dutch oven until the temperature reaches over high heat until it reaches 163°c (i use this instant read thermometer). thoroughly drain the sliced potatoes and blot them with paper towels to remove excess water. once the oil is 163°c carefully fry the potatoes in small batches to avoid overcrowding and fry for 2-3 minutes until pale and softened. use a slotted spoon to remove them from the oil and let them cool to room temperature. increase the temperature to 191°c. carefully add the fries again, frying in small batches, until they are golden, another 2-3 minutes. remove with a slotted spoon, place them on a baking sheet or roasting rack, sprinkle with salt while they're still very hot, and place them in the warmed oven while you're frying the fish. to make the fried fish: combine the flour, baking powder and salt in a large flat bowl. pour in the cold beer and whisk until smooth (use the batter immediately, do not let it rest for a while). in another large flat bowl add some extra flour for dredging. blot the fish with paper towels to remove excess moisture. thoroughly dredge all sides of the fish in the flour and shake off the excess. dip the fish into the beer batter to thoroughly coat all sides, allowing some of the excess batter to drip off (but not too much!) if you prefer an extra thick coating you can repeat the process of dredging the fish in flour followed by the batter. to fry the fish: you can either use a deep fryer or you can use a medium-sized skillet and fill it with oil to a depth of at least an inch. heat the oil to between 177°c and 191°c, using a candy thermometer. carefully lower the fish into the oil, waiting a few seconds before releasing it to prevent it from sticking to the bottom. fry the fish in the deep fryer for 5-8 minutes or until nicely golden. if using a frying pan fry the fish for about 2 minutes on each side or until nicely golden. remove the fish with a slotted spoon, letting the oil drop off, then place the fried fish on paper towels for a few seconds and serve immediately. (if you wait too long to serve the batter will lose its crispiness.) serve with the chips, a sprinkling of quality british malt vinegar and if desired a serving of authentic british mushy peas. though not traditional in the uk, you can also eat the fish with our homemade tartar sauce.

title: Butternut Squash Soup with Garlic Bread
text: butternut squash soup with garlic bread source: mobkitchen.co.uk ingredients - 2 butternut squash - 2 carrot - 1 onion - 10g fresh ginger - 600ml vegetable stock - 2clove garlic - 1bunch parsley - 400g ciabatta - salt - black pepper - olive oil instructions 1. preheat your oven to 180°c/180°c. 2. halve and peel your butternut squash, scoop out the seeds and cut it into cubes. place the cubes on a baking tray and season with a few cracks of black pepper, a pinch of salt and a drizzle of olive oil. toss the butternut squash to season on all sides and whack the tray in the oven for 50 minutes. 3. finely dice your carrots and onion. finely chop the garlic and ginger. pour a large drizzle of olive oil into a frying pan on medium-high heat. add your carrots and onion and sauté for 10 minutes, until the carrots have softened and the onions are translucent. add the chopped ginger and give it all a stir. 4. squash time! add the roasted butternut squash to your pan and stir to combine (leave the oven on for your garlic bread). pour in the vegetable stock and season with a few cracks of pepper. leave to simmer for 15 minutes. blitz the soup in the pan with a stick blender until silky smooth, or your desired consistency. 5. now for the garlic bread. slice your ciabatta in half down the middle and place on a baking tray. finely chop a large handful of parsley, leaving a third for later. in a bowl, mix together 45ml of olive oil, the chopped garlic, two thirds of the parsley, a pinch of salt, and a few grinds of pepper. give it a mix and spread over the ciabatta. pop in the oven for 20 minutes. 6. serve the soup with a drizzle of olive oil, a pinch of parsley, a crack of black pepper and your garlic bread. dig in and enjoy!

title: Carrot Cake
text: carrot cake ingredients - 480ml sugar - 360ml oil - 4 large eggs - 480ml flour - 240ml chopped walnuts - 5ml salt - 10ml cinnamon - 720ml grated carrots - 10ml soda - 227g package cream cheese - 1 stick soft margarine - 10ml vanilla - confectioners sugar instructions 1. mix eggs, sugar and oil together. 2. beat until creamy. 3. add flour, soda, salt and cinnamon. 4. mix well and add carrots and nuts. 5. pour into a 9 x 13 sheet pan. 6. bake for 45 minutes at 350 degrees. 7. beat cream cheese and margarine together. 8. add vanilla and gradually beat in confectioners sugar until sweet and creamy. 9. spread icing on cooled cake.

title: Cabbage Manchurian
text: cabbage manchurian ingredients - 720ml cabbage finely chopped - 5ml chilli powder - 2ml pepper powder - 2ml salt - 5ml ginger garlic paste - 60ml maida - 30ml corn flour - oil for frying - 30ml oil - 1 chilli chopped - 5 clove garlic chopped - 1 inch ginger chopped - ½ onion chopped - 30ml spring onion chopped - ½ capsicum chopped - 30ml tomato sauce - 30ml vinegar - 30ml soy sauce - 15ml chilli sauce - 120ml water - 5ml corn flour instructions 1. in a large bowl take 720ml cabbage, 5ml chilli powder, 2ml pepper powder, 2ml salt and 5ml ginger garlic paste. 2. squeeze and mix well making sure everything is well combined. 3. add 60ml maida and 30ml corn flour and mix well forming a dough without adding any extra water. 4. grease the hand with oil and prepare small ball-sized balls. 5. deep fry in hot oil on medium flame, stirring occasionally until the manchurian balls turn golden brown and crisp. 6. drain off to remove excess oil and keep aside. 7. heat 30ml oil, add 1 chilli, 5 clove garlic, 1 inch ginger and stir fry on high flame. 8. add ½ onion, 30ml spring onion and ½ capsicum and stir fry on high flame. 9. add 30ml tomato sauce, 30ml vinegar, 30ml soy sauce, 15ml chilli sauce, 2ml salt and 2ml chilli powder. 10. stir and mix well until all the sauces are combined and add 60ml water to prevent the sauce from burning. 11. prepare a corn flour slurry by mixing 5ml corn flour in 60ml water and pour into the sauce. 12. mix well and cook until the sauce turns glossy. 13. add fried cabbage balls and 30ml spring onion and mix gently coating the sauce uniformly. 14. serve cabbage manchurian with tomato sauce.

title: Cabbage Rolls II
text: cabbage rolls ii source: allrecipes.com ingredients - 12 leaves cabbage - 454g extra-lean ground beef - 240ml cooked white rice - 1 egg, beaten - 60ml milk - 60ml minced onion - 6ml salt - 6ml ground black pepper - 1 (227g) can tomato sauce - 15ml brown sugar - 15ml lemon juice - 5ml worcestershire sauce instructions 1. bring a large pot of water to a boil and boil cabbage leaves for 2 minutes, then drain. 2. combine ground beef, cooked rice, egg, milk, onion, salt, and pepper in a large bowl and spoon about 30ml of mixture onto each cabbage leaf. 3. bring one end of the cabbage leaf over the mixture, rolling and tucking in the ends to prevent filling from falling out, and arrange rolls in a single layer in the slow cooker. 4. mix tomato sauce, brown sugar, lemon juice, and worcestershire sauce together in a small bowl until combined and pour over cabbage rolls. 5. cover and cook on low for 8 to 9 hours.

title: Caramelized Apple Cake
text: caramelized apple cake source: erasmus recipes ingredients - 5 green apples - 250g butter - 250g white sugar - 5 eggs - 250g flour - 5ml cinnamon - 5ml baking powder instructions 1. peel all five apples and clean them by removing the seeds, then dice the apples. 2. put 50g of white sugar in a dry pan and let it caramelize, watching carefully so it does not burn. 3. when the sugar dissolves completely, add the diced apples and stir well, ensuring they are coated with caramelized sugar and turn golden brown, but do not cook them completely. 4. finish with some butter and cinnamon on top of the caramelized apples for extra depth of flavor. 5. soften the butter in the microwave for a couple of minutes. 6. add 200g of white sugar and mix until homogeneous and creamy. 7. add five whole eggs and mix well until everything is combined, ensuring eggs are at room temperature. 8. add the flour, cinnamon, and baking powder and mix well until everything is combined. 9. add the caramelized apples to the cake mix once they have cooled down and give a final good mix. 10. cover an 18-20cm baking tin generously with butter so the cake will not stick. 11. bake in a preheated oven at 170°c until the surface becomes golden brown and a knife inserted comes out clean, approximately 45 minutes.

title: Cardamom Sourdough Bread with Amaretto Soaked Raisins
text: cardamom sourdough bread with amaretto soaked raisins source: healthfully rooted home ingredients - 113g sourdough starter, active or discard - 360g all-purpose flour - 10ml baking powder - 15ml coconut sugar - 6ml salt - 1 large egg - 75ml butter, softened - 180g warm water - 80ml coconut sugar - 5ml cardamom - 2ml cinnamon - 10ml flour - 1 egg, beaten - 240ml raisins - 240ml amaretto or filtered water instructions 1. soak your raisins in amaretto or filtered water and set aside. 2. combine all of the dough ingredients in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the dough hook attachment. 3. knead until the dough becomes soft and smooth. 4. place the dough in a lightly greased glass or ceramic bowl and allow it to rise for about 2 hours until it has doubled in size. 5. meanwhile, make the filling by stirring together the coconut sugar, cardamom, cinnamon, and flour. 6. once the dough is done rising, gently deflate it and transfer it to a lightly greased counter. 7. flatten the dough into a rectangle about 6 inches by 18 inches. 8. brush the dough with egg wash and sprinkle the filling evenly over it, then top with the soaked raisins, leaving a bare strip about 1 inch wide along one short edge. 9. starting with the short end that is covered with filling, roll the dough into a log and pinch the ends and long seam closed. 10. transfer the log, seam-side down, to a lightly greased 9 by 5 inch loaf pan, cover, and allow it to rise for about 1 hour. 11. while the dough is rising, preheat the oven to 177°c. 12. bake the bread for 40 to 45 minutes, tenting it lightly with foil after 15 to 20 minutes to prevent burning. 13. remove the bread from the oven, gently loosen the edges, turn it out of the pan, and brush the top surface with butter. 14. allow the bread to cool completely before slicing.

title: Carrot Cake with Ginger Cream Cheese Frosting
text: carrot cake with ginger cream cheese frosting source: foodnetwork.com ingredients - cooking spray - 660ml chopped walnuts - 600ml all-purpose flour - 10ml baking powder - 5ml baking soda - 10ml ground ginger - 5ml ground cinnamon - 1ml ground allspice - 1ml ground nutmeg - 1ml salt - 360ml granulated sugar - 120ml packed light brown sugar - 300ml vegetable oil - 4 large eggs - 120ml smooth applesauce - finely grated zest of 1 orange - 5ml pure vanilla extract - 480ml grated carrots (about 4 medium) - 1 4-inch piece ginger - 15ml fresh orange juice - 2ml pure vanilla extract - 2 8-ounce packages cream cheese, at room temperature - 1 stick unsalted butter, at room temperature - 720ml confectioners' sugar, sifted instructions 1. make the cake: preheat the oven to 177°c. coat two 9-inch-round cake pans with cooking spray; line the bottoms with parchment paper. spread the walnuts on a rimmed baking sheet and bake until lightly toasted, about 5 minutes. let cool, then finely chop. 2. sift the flour, baking powder, baking soda, ground ginger, cinnamon, allspice, nutmeg and salt onto a large piece of parchment (or into a medium bowl). beat the granulated sugar, brown sugar and vegetable oil in a large bowl with a mixer on medium speed until smooth, about 1 minute. increase the speed to medium high and add the eggs, one at a time; beat until light and smooth, about 2 minutes. reduce the mixer speed to low; add the applesauce, orange zest and vanilla and beat until just smooth. gradually add the flour mixture and beat until just combined. add the carrots and 180ml walnuts and beat until just combined. 3. divide the batter between the prepared pans. bake until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, about 35 minutes. transfer to a rack and let cool 10 minutes in the pans, then remove to the rack to cool completely; remove the parchment. (the cake layers can be made a day ahead; let cool completely, then wrap in plastic wrap.) 4. make the frosting: peel the ginger and grate onto a piece of cheesecloth. wrap in the cheesecloth and squeeze the juice into a small bowl (you should get about 15ml). add the orange juice and vanilla to the bowl. beat the cream cheese and butter in a large bowl with a mixer on medium-high speed until smooth, about 2 minutes. beat in the juice mixture. reduce the mixer speed to low and gradually beat in the confectioners' sugar. increase the mixer speed to high and beat until smooth, about 2 more minutes. 5. place 1 cake layer on a platter, rounded-side down. spread with 240ml frosting, then top with the second cake layer, rounded-side down. cover the top and sides with the remaining frosting. press the remaining walnuts into the sides of the cake. refrigerate at least 1 hour before serving.

title: Cast Iron Sourdough Focaccia w/ Apples and Rosemary
text: cast iron sourdough focaccia w/ apples and rosemary source: breadbyelise.com ingredients - 10 g active sourdough starter (white, 100% hydration) - 25 g water (at around 26°c/26°c) - 25 g all-purpose flour - 320 g tipo 0 flour - 250 g water (at around 26°c/26°c) - 65 g levain - 7 g salt - 10 g olive oil (extra virgin) - olive oil (extra virgin) - thinly sliced apples - fresh rosemary - flaky sea salt - honey instructions 1. add all the ingredients to a small mixing bowl and stir to combine. cover and proof in a warm spot (around 26°c/26°c) for 5-6 hours or until the levain has doubled/tripled in size. 2. 3,5 hours after you prepared the levain: add the flour and water to a large mixing bowl. mix to combine using your hands or a rubber spatula. cover the bowl and autolyse/rest for 1,5 hours. 3. after 1,5 hours, add the levain to the main dough and mix by hand or with a stand mixer (with dough hook attachment) for 3-4 minutes. add salt, and continue mixing for 2 minutes or until you can't feel any noticeable salt in the dough. add about half of the olive oil, mix for 2 minutes, add the rest, and mix for 2-3 minutes until the dough is smooth. 4. place the dough in a clean, lightly oiled bowl. 5. proof the dough for 5 hours at around 24°c/24°c. coil fold the dough every 30 minutes for the first 2 hours, then leave it alone to proof for the remaining 3 hours. 6. after 5 hours, the dough should have nearly doubled in size. transfer it to the fridge to cold-proof overnight (or up to 24 hours). 7. line the bottom of your cast iron with parchment paper. add about a tbsp olive oil to the top of the parchment and use a pastry brush to evenly spread it around the pan, especially on the sides of the pan, to prevent the dough from sticking. take the dough out of the fridge and dump it into the pan. 8. gently stretch the dough to even it out in the pan. 9. cover the cast iron pan and proof at 24°c/24°c-26°c/26°c until doubled in size. the second proof typically takes 2-3 hours, but please look less on the clock and more on how the dough looks. 10. preheat your oven to 260°c/260°c 30-45 minutes before you plan to bake the focaccia. 11. when the focaccia has doubled in size: drizzle a generous amount of olive oil over the dough's surface. use your fingers to poke dents all over the dough. add thinly sliced apples, fresh rosemary, and flaky sea salt on top. 12. bake for 10 minutes with the lid on, then take the lid off, turn down the heat to 221°c/220°c, and bake for another 10-15 minutes until deep golden brown. remove from the oven, drizzle honey on top, and let it cool for about 15 minutes before serving.

title: Masala Chai Recipe (Indian Masala Tea)
text: masala chai recipe (indian masala tea) source: indianhealthyrecipes.com ingredients - 4 green cardamoms ((elaichi or 1ml ground)) - 2 cloves ((3 for stronger flavor or 1ml ground)) - ½ to ¾ inch cinnamon piece ((cassia or ceylon or 1ml ground cinnamon)) - 2 pepper corn ((or a pinch of ground pepper, optional)) - 1½ cups water - 240ml full fat milk ((adjust to taste, refer notes)) - 2½ to 15ml black tea leaves (or 1¼ to 1½ teaspoon tea powder (dust) (or 3 to 4 tea bags, refer notes)) - 2 to 15ml sugar (or as needed) - 2ml (½ inch) ginger ( chopped or crushed (optional)) - 5ml green cardamoms ((5 grams skinned) (elaichi)) - 2ml cloves ((2 grams) ) - 2½ to 3 grams cinnamon ((cassia or ceylon)) - 1ml fennel seeds ((1½ grams) (saunf)) - ¼ to 2ml black pepper corn ((2ml ground pepper)) - 2ml nutmeg (grated or ⅓ of large nutmeg) - 2 petals star flower ((star anise) (chakri phool)) instructions 1. add cloves, cardamom, cinnamon stick & black pepper to a mortar pestle or a spice grinder. crush or grind them to a powder. 2. heat water in a pot. add the ground spices, crushed/chopped ginger and tea. (start with lower amount of tea and if required you may add more after adding milk) 3. bring this to a rolling boil and reduce the heat to medium. boil for 3 mins until the decoction turns dark. 4. pour milk and add sugar. bring it to a boil on a medium high heat. (if using tea bags remove them at this stage and keep aside.) 5. reduce the heat and simmer until the chai (tea) becomes dark, for about 2 mins. 6. when the masala tea is ready, you will see a layer of cream on top and also the milk flavor is gone. 7. optionally aerate or pull your masala chai for the same chaiwallah taste. take a soup ladle and aerate the masala chai or simply pour some chai to a measuring cup. pour the hot tea in a slow stream, back to the chai pot from a height of 1 to 1½ feet. 8. repeat this step of pulling hot masala chai from the pot to the cup, a few times (4 to 5 times). this breaks down the layer of cream and incorporates it back to the masala chai making it more tasty and thick. 9. strain the masala chai to serving cups & serve with any breakfast, snack or biscuits. 10. clean all the spices and add to a blender jar. powder finely. store it in an airtight glass jar. 11. use about ½ to 4ml or more to make 2 servings of tea. for stronger tea you can use about 4ml.

title: Chantal's New York Cheesecake
text: chantal's new york cheesecake source: allrecipes.com ingredients - 15 graham crackers, crushed - 30ml butter, melted - 4 (227g) packages cream cheese - 360ml white sugar - 180ml milk - 4 large eggs - 240ml sour cream - 60ml all-purpose flour - 15ml vanilla extract instructions 1. preheat the oven to 177°c (175 degrees c) and grease a 9-inch springform pan. 2. mix graham cracker crumbs and melted butter together in a medium bowl until well combined. 3. press the mixture onto the bottom of the prepared pan to make a packed crust. 4. mix cream cheese and sugar together in a large bowl until smooth, then blend in milk and mix in eggs one at a time until just combined. 5. add sour cream, flour, and vanilla and mix until smooth. 6. pour the filling onto the prepared crust and bake in the preheated oven for 1 hour. 7. turn the oven off and let the cheesecake cool in the oven with the door closed for 5 to 6 hours to prevent cracking, then chill in the refrigerator until serving.

title: Cheesy Italian Oatmeal Pan Bread
text: cheesy italian oatmeal pan bread ingredients - 480ml water - 240ml rolled oats - 45ml butter - 4-1200ml all-purpose flour, divided - 60ml sugar - 10ml salt - 2 (7g) packages active dry yeast - 1 large egg - 240ml shredded mozzarella cheese - 15ml grated parmesan cheese - 2ml dried basil leaves - 1ml dried oregano - 2ml garlic powder - 60ml butter, melted instructions 1. spray a 13x9 inch baking pan with non-stick spray. 2. bring water to a boil in a medium saucepan and stir in rolled oats and 45ml butter. 3. cool the oatmeal mixture to 100-43°c. 4. combine 360ml flour, sugar, salt, and yeast in a large mixing bowl and blend well. 5. add the cooled oats mixture and egg, then blend at low speed of an electric mixer until moistened. 6. beat at medium speed for 3 minutes. 7. by hand, stir in 1 3/4 to 600ml flour and mozzarella cheese to form a stiff dough. 8. knead in 1/2 to 180ml flour on a floured surface until the dough is smooth and elastic, about 5 minutes. 9. shape the dough into a ball and cover with a large bowl, then let rest 15 minutes. 10. punch down the dough and press it into the prepared pan. 11. using a very sharp knife, cut diagonal lines 1 1/2 inches apart, cutting completely through the dough, then repeat in the opposite direction to create a diamond pattern. 12. cover loosely with greased plastic wrap and a cloth towel, then let rise in a warm place (80-29°c) until light and doubled in size, about 45 minutes. 13. heat the oven to 191°c and uncover the dough. 14. redefine the diamond pattern by cutting in an up and down motion through to the bottom of the pan with a sharp knife. 15. combine parmesan cheese, basil, oregano, and garlic powder in a small bowl and set aside. 16. spoon 30ml of melted butter over the cut dough. 17. bake for 15 minutes. 18. brush the remaining 30ml of butter over the partially baked bread. 19. sprinkle the parmesan mixture over the bread. 20. bake for an additional 10 to 15 minutes or until golden brown, then serve warm or cool.

title: Chestnut Liquor
text: chestnut liquor ingredients - chestnuts - sugar - neutral spirit instructions 1. roast the chestnuts until the outer shell is blackened and the nut inside is tender. 2. remove the shells and skins from the chestnuts and chop the nuts into small pieces. 3. combine the chestnuts, sugar, and neutral spirit in a large jar or bottle. 4. seal the jar or bottle and store it in a cool, dark place for at least 2 weeks. 5. shake the mixture every day to help the sugar dissolve. 6. after 2 weeks, strain the liquid through a fine mesh strainer or cheesecloth to remove the chestnut solids. 7. bottle the chestnut liquor and enjoy it neat or in cocktails.

title: Chestnut Paste
text: chestnut paste ingredients - 1440ml (907g 227g) chestnuts - 480ml (454g) extra fine granulated sugar - 240ml (227g) water - 10ml vanilla bean paste or vanilla instructions 1. cut an x into the flat side of each chestnut using a knife. 2. place a batch of chestnuts in a non-reactive pot and cover completely with water. 3. bring the water to a boil. 4. boil for 7-8 minutes and remove the chestnuts using a slotted spoon. 5. peel away the outer skin and brown skin from the chestnuts. 6. repeat the boiling and peeling process with the remaining chestnuts in batches. 7. place all peeled chestnuts in fresh water and bring to a boil. 8. reduce heat to simmer and cook for 15 minutes until the chestnuts feel al dente. 9. drain the chestnuts and place them in a food processor. 10. place the sugar in a small saucepan and add 240ml of water, stirring to a boil. 11. brush away any sugar crystals stuck to the side of the pan with a clean wet brush. 12. cook the sugar syrup without stirring to 116°c (116°c). 13. remove from heat and mix in the processed chestnuts. 14. stir the mixture for 5 minutes on medium heat. 15. add the vanilla and combine well. 16. store in a well-sealed container in the refrigerator or freezer.

title: Chewy Chocolate Peanut Butter Bars
text: chewy chocolate peanut butter bars source: half baked harvest ingredients - 120ml honey - 60ml pure maple syrup - 60ml creamy peanut butter (just peanuts and salt) - 15ml coconut oil - 1440ml brown rice krispies - 300ml creamy peanut butter (just peanuts and salt) - 80ml pure maple syrup - 60ml plus 15ml coconut oil - 10ml vanilla extract - sea salt - 340g dark chocolate, chopped instructions 1. line a 9x13 inch baking dish with parchment paper. 2. add the brown rice krispies to a large bowl. 3. in a medium pot, combine the honey, maple syrup, peanut butter, and coconut oil, bring to a gentle boil over medium heat while stirring constantly, cook for 2 minutes, then remove from heat and pour the mix over the brown rice krispies. 4. stir well to combine and spread the mix onto the prepared pan, packing it in tightly, then place in the freezer. 5. in a medium pot, mix the peanut butter, maple syrup, and 60ml coconut oil and bring to a gentle boil over medium heat while stirring constantly. 6. cook for 2 minutes, then remove from heat and stir in the vanilla and salt. 7. pour the peanut mixture over the krispies layer and freeze for 30 minutes until firm. 8. melt together the chocolate and 15ml coconut oil in the microwave, let cool for 5 minutes, and spread over the peanut butter layer. 9. return to the fridge to set for about 10 minutes, then slice and keep in the fridge.

title: Chewy Oatmeal Raisin Cookies Without Butter
text: chewy oatmeal raisin cookies without butter ingredients - 160ml maple syrup (or 120ml brown sugar & 30ml maple syrup) - 2 eggs - 45ml water - 2ml vanilla extract - 1¾ cup oatmeal - 180ml all purpose flour - 180ml raisins - 2ml salt instructions 1. mix maple syrup, water and egg in a bowl using a wooden spoon. 2. add vanilla and mix again. 3. add flour and oatmeal and mix well until everything is combined and the dough starts to come together. 4. add raisins and mix well. 5. let the dough stay in the refrigerator for one hour. 6. preheat the oven to 180°c (177°c) and line baking sheets with parchment paper. 7. take the dough out of the refrigerator and using a spoon or an ice cream scoop, make small balls of cookie dough on the baking sheets. 8. bake the cookies for 16 minutes until their bottoms are light brown. 9. let cool completely before serving.

title: Chicken Liver Pâté
text: chicken liver pâté ingredients - 227g chicken livers, well-trimmed - 1/2 small onion, thinly sliced - 1 small garlic clove, smashed and peeled - 1 bay leaf - 1ml thyme leaves - kosher salt - 120ml water - 1 1/2 sticks unsalted butter, at room temperature - 10ml cognac or scotch whisky - freshly ground pepper - toasted baguette slices, for serving instructions 1. in a medium saucepan, combine the chicken livers, onion, garlic, bay leaf, thyme and 2ml of salt. 2. add the water and bring to a simmer. 3. cover, reduce the heat to low and cook, stirring occasionally, until the livers are barely pink inside, about 3 minutes. 4. remove from the heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. 5. discard the bay leaf and transfer the livers, onion and garlic to a food processor using a slotted spoon. 6. process until coarsely pureed. 7. with the machine on, add the butter 30ml at a time until incorporated. 8. add the cognac, season with salt and pepper and process until completely smooth. 9. scrape the pâté into 2 or 3 large ramekins. 10. press a piece of plastic wrap directly onto the surface of the pâté and refrigerate until firm. 11. serve chilled.

title: Chicken Breast Marinade
text: chicken breast marinade ingredients - 180ml balsamic vinegar - 120ml water - 5ml dried minced onion - 2ml crushed red pepper flakes - 2ml dried minced garlic - 1ml salt - 1ml ground black pepper - 1ml paprika - 1ml crushed dried rosemary - 1ml dried parsley flakes - 1ml chili powder - 1ml dried oregano - 4 (170g) skinless, boneless chicken breast halves instructions 1. whisk together the balsamic vinegar, water, onion, red pepper flakes, garlic, salt, pepper, paprika, rosemary, parsley, chili powder, and oregano in a bowl, and pour into a resealable plastic bag. 2. add the chicken breasts, coat with the marinade, squeeze out excess air, and seal the bag. 3. marinate in the refrigerator 30 minutes to overnight. 4. preheat oven to 204°c (200 degrees c) and line a baking sheet with aluminum foil or lightly grease a broiler pan. 5. remove the chicken breasts from the marinade, shake off excess, discard the remaining marinade, and place the chicken breasts onto the baking sheet. 6. bake in the preheated oven until the chicken breasts are golden brown and no longer pink in the center, 30 to 40 minutes, until an instant-read thermometer inserted into the center reaches 74°c (74 degrees c).

title: Chimichurri Sauce
text: chimichurri sauce ingredients - 1 small bunch flat leaf parsley - 1 small bunch cilantro - 60ml fresh oregano leaves - 15ml. capers - 1 small shallot, minced - 4 large cloves of garlic, minced - 1 small chili pepper, minced (optional) - 30ml. sherry or red wine vinegar - 30ml. lemon juice - 160ml flavorful olive oil - salt and pepper, to taste instructions 1. trim the bottoms off the parsley and cilantro. 2. use a chef's knife with a rocking motion to finely mince the herbs, stems and all. 3. add the oregano leaves and capers to the pile and mince into the rest of the herbs, then move them all to a mixing bowl. 4. stir in shallot, garlic, chili if using, vinegar, lemon juice, and olive oil. 5. add salt and pepper to taste, then allow to rest for at least 15 minutes, preferably longer. 6. taste again and adjust with more salt, pepper, herbs, or acid as you see fit. 7. refrigerate in a glass jar or tightly sealed plastic container for up to three days.

title: Asian Vinaigrette Salad Dressing
text: asian vinaigrette salad dressing source: food.com ingredients - 45ml rice wine vinegar - 15ml sugar - 45ml soy sauce, preferably low-sodium - 15ml fresh grated ginger - 2ml fresh minced garlic - 30ml sesame oil - 120ml peanut oil or 120ml grapeseed oil - 15ml lightly toasted sesame seeds - 15ml chopped scallion (green onions) instructions 1. mix the first five ingredients in a bowl or food processor. 2. if using a bowl, slowly drizzle in the sesame and peanut oil while whisking constantly so that the dressing will emulsify. 3. if using a food processor, leave it running while you drizzle in the oil. 4. when the dressing is well combined, add sesame seeds and scallions. 5. serve immediately or refrigerate and use within a week.

title: Chocolate Frosting
text: chocolate frosting <https://www.simplyrecipes.com/hersheys-busy-day-cocoa-icing-review-8665547 ingredients the busy day cocoa icing recipe ingredients: 90ml boiling water 60ml (1/2 stick or 60ml) butter 10ml vanilla 120ml hershey’s cocoa 720ml powdered sugar instructions the steps couldn’t be simpler. pour the boiling water over the butter, and immediately add the vanilla and cocoa. beat until well blended. then, add the powdered sugar. beat until creamy, adding more water if necessary, until the icing is thin enough to spread. spread on a warm cake (more on that later). the recipe is perfect for a generously frosted 8 or 9-inch round cake or a 9x13-inch sheet cake.

title: Chocolate Mousse Cake
text: chocolate mousse cake source: ricardocuisine.com ingredients - 120ml (75 g) unbleached all-purpose flour - 60ml (55 g) sugar - 30ml cocoa powder, sifted - 1ml baking soda - 80ml (75 ml) water - 30ml (30 ml) canola oil - 5ml (5 ml) white vinegar - 198g (200 g) dark chocolate, chopped - 5ml gelatin - 30ml (30 ml) water - 120ml (105 g) sugar - 480ml (500 ml) 35% whipping cream - 85g (85 g) dark chocolate, chopped - 80ml (75 ml) 35% whipping cream instructions 1. with the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 177°c (180°c). butter an 8-inch (20 cm) springform pan and line the bottom with parchment paper. 2. in a bowl, combine the dry ingredients. stir in the water, oil and vinegar with a whisk until smooth. spoon into the prepared pan. 3. bake for 10 to 12 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the centre of the cake comes out clean. let cool on a wire rack. do not unmould. 4. in a bowl placed over a pot of simmering water or in the microwave oven, melt the chocolate. let cool slightly. 5. in a small bowl, sprinkle the gelatin over the water and let bloom for 5 minutes. 6. in a small saucepan over medium heat, heat cup (60 ml) of the cream with the sugar until the sugar has dissolved. remove from the heat and stir in the gelatin until completely dissolved. add the cream mixture to the melted chocolate and stir to combine. 7. in another bowl, whip the remaining cream (420ml / 430 ml) with an electric mixer until stiff peaks form. combine one-quarter of the whipped cream with the chocolate mixture. with a spatula, gently fold in the remaining cream. spoon onto the cake in an even layer. refrigerate for 4 hours or freeze. 8. unmould the cake and place on a serving platter. if frozen, leave the cake at room temperature for 1 hour. 9. place the chocolate in a bowl. set aside. 10. in the microwave oven or in a small saucepan, bring the cream to a boil. add to the chocolate and let melt for 1 minute. with a spatula, stir the ganache until smooth. pour over the cake, letting it run over the sides.

title: Chocolate Mousse
text: chocolate mousse source: recipetineats.com ingredients - 3 eggs ((55g/57g each)) - 125g / 128g 70% cocoa chocolate or bittersweet chocolate, (, break or cut into small 1 cm / 0.2" pieces (note 1)) - 10g / 9g unsalted butter - 120ml cream (, full fat (note 2)) - 45ml caster sugar ((superfine white sugar)) - more whipped cream - chocolate shavings ((note 3)) instructions 1. for reliable results, work at a steady pace so your whipped egg whites and cream do not get too warm! 2. separate eggs and yolks while eggs are cold. place whites in a large bowl and yolks in a small bowl. leave whites while you prepare other ingredients. (note 4) 3. whisk yolks until uniform. 4. melt chocolate and butter - place chocolate in a microwave-proof bowl with the butter. melt in the microwave in 20 second bursts, stirring in between, until smooth. (stir in optional flavourings at this point, but read note 6 first). set aside to cool slightly while you proceed with other steps - we want it at room temperature but still pourable. 5. whip cream - beat cream until stiff peaks form, being careful not to over-whip (see video). 6. whip whites - clean the whisks. add sugar into the egg whites bowl. beat until firm peaks form. goal - flopping "elf hat"! (see video and note 5 for what this means). 7. yolks and cream - fold egg yolks into cream using a rubber spatula - 8 folds max. some streaks is fine. 8. check chocolate temperature - the chocolate should be cooled to room temperature but still runny (minimum 35°c / 35°c; ideal 40°c / 40°c). if too cool or thick, microwave in burst of 5 seconds at a time until runny. 9. chocolate into cream - pour chocolate into cream yolk mixture. fold through - 8 folds max. some streaks here are ok. 10. fold in egg whites - add 1/4 of beaten egg whites into chocolate mixture. fold through until incorporated - "smear" the spatular across surface to blend white lumps in - aim for 10 folds. 11. pour chocolate mixture into egg whites. fold through until incorporated and no more white lumps remain - aim for 12 folds max, but ensure there are no obvious egg white patches. 12. chill in fridge - divide mixture between 4 small glasses or pots. refrigerate for at least 6 hours, preferably overnight. 13. to serve, garnish with cream and chocolate shavings. raspberries and a tiny sprig of mint for colour would also be lovely!

title: Sourdough Stiff Babka (50% Hydration Starter)
text: sourdough stiff babka (50% hydration starter) yield: 1 large loaf | prep time: 24 hours | bake time: 45 minutes ingredients 1. the sweet stiff levain - 75g active 50% hydration sourdough starter - 105g all-purpose flour - 55g water - 20g sugar 2. the final dough - 375g bread flour - 105g milk (lukewarm) - 80g water (lukewarm) - 2 large eggs (room temperature) - 50g sugar - 8g fine sea salt - 85g unsalted butter (softened to room temperature) 3. the chocolate filling - 95g semi-dark chocolate (chopped) - 70g unsalted butter - 65g powdered sugar - 18g unsweetened cocoa powder - 1 pinch salt 4. the sugar syrup (optional finisher) - 50g water - 50g sugar instructions step 1: build the levain 1. combine the 50% starter, flour, water, and sugar in a small bowl. 2. knead briefly by hand until smooth. it will be dense like a stiff dough. 3. cover tightly and let ferment at room temperature (23°c–26°c) for 10–12 hours, or until it triples in volume and dome peaks. step 2: mix and knead the dough 1. tear the active levain into small pieces and place them into a stand mixer bowl. 2. add the bread flour, milk, water, eggs, sugar, and salt. 3. mix on low speed with the dough hook attachment for 5 minutes until a cohesive dough forms. let it rest for 10 minutes. 4. turn the mixer to medium-low speed. add the softened butter one tablespoon at a time, letting each piece absorb before adding the next. 5. knead for 10–15 minutes until the dough pulls away from the sides, clears the bottom of the bowl, and passes the windowpane test. step 3: bulk fermentation & cold proof 1. place the dough into a lightly greased bowl and cover it. 2. let it rise at a warm room temperature for 6–8 hours until puffy. 3. transfer the covered bowl to the refrigerator for 12–16 hours overnight. this chills the butter and makes shaping much easier. step 4: make the filling & shape 1. melt the chocolate and butter together in a double boiler or microwave. stir in the powdered sugar, cocoa powder, and salt until smooth. let it cool slightly to a spreadable consistency. 2. roll the chilled dough on a lightly floured surface into a 30×40cm rectangle. 3. spread the chocolate filling evenly across the dough, leaving a 1cm border. 4. roll the dough into a tight log, starting from the long side. 5. cut the log completely in half lengthwise using a sharp knife to expose the inner layers. 6. twist the two strands over each other to form a braid. tuck the ends under and lift it into a greased 23×13cm loaf pan lined with parchment paper. step 5: final rise & bake 1. cover and let the babka rise for 4–6 hours at a warm room temperature (around 27°c) until it fills out the pan and looks swollen. 2. preheat your oven to 190°c. 3. bake for 40–45 minutes. if the top browns too quickly, tent it loosely with aluminum foil. the babka is done when a digital thermometer reads 93°c in the center. step 6: syrup and cooling 1. while the babka bakes, boil the 50g water and 50g sugar until dissolved. 2. brush the hot syrup over the hot babka immediately when it comes out of the oven. 3. let it cool in the pan for 20 minutes, then lift it out onto a wire rack to cool completely before slicing. timeline wednesday night (9:00 pm) — build the levain: mix your 50% hydration starter, flour, water, and sugar. ferment 11 hours overnight at room temperature. thursday morning (8:00 am) — mix the final dough: mix the dough ingredients and your active levain in the stand mixer. incorporate the butter and knead until smooth (25 minutes). thursday day (8:30 am – 2:30 pm) — warm bulk rise: let the dough ferment in a warm spot for 6 hours. thursday afternoon (2:30 pm) — cold proof: transfer the covered dough into the refrigerator for 16.5 hours. friday morning (7:00 am) — shape: make the chocolate filling. roll out the cold dough, spread the filling, roll into a log, slice, and braid. place into the lined loaf pan (30 minutes). friday morning (7:30 am – 11:15 am) — final proof: cover the pan and let the babka rise in a warm spot until swollen and puffy (3 hours 45 minutes). preheat oven to 190°c at 10:45 am. friday mid-morning (11:15 am – 12:00 pm) — bake: bake 40–45 minutes until the center reaches 93°c. brush with warm sugar syrup immediately out of the oven.

title: Chuck Roast
text: chuck roast source: sundaysuppermovement.com ingredients - one chuck roast with good marbling - unsalted butter - vegetable oil - one large yellow onion, cut into large wedges - fresh garlic cloves - whole carrots, cut into 2-inch pieces - celery, cut into 2-inch pieces - potatoes (yukon gold or russet), cut into 2-inch chunks - fresh rosemary sprig - two bay leaves - two tablespoons tomato paste - one cup red wine - two cups beef stock - kosher salt or sea salt flakes - black pepper instructions 1. pat the beef dry and season it generously with salt and pepper on all sides. 2. heat butter and vegetable oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. 3. sear the chuck roast on all sides until browned, then remove and set aside. 4. add the onion, garlic cloves, carrots, and celery to the pot and cook until fragrant. 5. stir in the tomato paste and cook for one minute. 6. deglaze the pot with red wine, scraping up any browned bits. 7. return the roast to the pot and add the beef stock, bay leaves, and rosemary. 8. braise low and slow until the roast is very tender and falls apart easily. 9. add the potatoes during the final portion of cooking until they are tender. 10. remove the bay leaves and rosemary sprig before serving.

title: Classic Lemon Meringue Pie
text: classic lemon meringue pie source: sallysbakingaddiction.com ingredients - pie crust - 5 large egg yolks (use the whites in the meringue below) - 1 and 80ml (320ml) water - 240ml (200g) granulated sugar - 80ml (38g) cornstarch - 1ml salt - 120ml (120ml) fresh lemon juice - 15ml lemon zest - 30ml (28g) unsalted butter, softened to room temperature - 5 large egg whites, at room temperature - 2ml cream of tartar - 120ml (100g) granulated sugar - 1ml salt instructions 1. i like to make sure my pie dough is prepared before i begin making lemon meringue pie. i always make pie dough the night before because it needs to chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours before rolling out and blind baking (next step). 2. preheat oven to 191°c (190°c) and adjust your oven rack to the lowest position. partially blind bake pie crust in a 9-inch pie dish. (follow blind baking instructions through step 9. be sure to crimp or flute the pie crust edges, too.) tip: you can get started on the lemon meringue pie filling steps while your crust is blind baking. but making the filling is time sensitive because you will temper the egg yolks, so if multi-tasking isn’t your thing, just wait until your crust is done blind baking before beginning the filling. 3. reduce oven temperature to 177°c (177°c). 4. watch the video below to see how i work through each of the following steps. 5. whisk the egg yolks together in a medium bowl or liquid measuring cup. set aside. whisk the water, granulated sugar, cornstarch, salt, lemon juice, and lemon zest together in a medium saucepan over medium heat. the mixture will be thin and cloudy, then eventually begin thickening and bubbling after about 6 minutes. once thickened, give it a whisk and reduce heat to low. 6. very slowly stream a few large spoonfuls of warm lemon mixture into the beaten egg yolks. then, also in a very slow stream, whisk the egg yolk mixture into the saucepan. turn heat back up to medium. cook until the mixture is thick and big bubbles begin bursting at the surface. remove the pan from heat and whisk in the butter. spread filling into the warm partially baked crust. set aside as you prepare the meringue. (don’t let the filling cool down too much as you want a warm filling when you top with the meringue in step 7. the warm filling helps seal the two layers together, preventing separation.) 7. with a handheld mixer or a stand mixer fitted with a whisk attachment, beat the egg whites and cream of tartar together on medium speed for 1 minute, then increase to high speed until soft peaks form, about 4 more minutes. add the sugar and salt, then continue beating on high speed until glossy stiff peaks form, about 2 more minutes. spread meringue on top of filling. (i like to make decorative peaks with the back of a large spoon.) make sure you spread the meringue all the way to the edges so that it touches the crust. this helps prevent the meringue from weeping. 8. bake pie on the lowest oven rack for 20-25 minutes. (if the meringue is browning too quickly, tent a piece of foil over it as best you can without the foil touching the meringue.) when pie is done, remove from the oven, place on a wire rack, and allow to cool at room temperature for 1 hour before placing in the refrigerator to chill. chill for 4 hours before slicing and serving. 9. cover any leftovers and store in the refrigerator. lemon meringue pie tastes best on day 1 because it doesn’t keep very well. no matter how hard you try to prevent it, the meringue will wilt and separate over time. best to enjoy right away.

title: עוגיות קפה ושוקולד
text: עוגיות קפה ושוקולד רכיבים - 1 כף נס קפה מגורען איכותי - 1 כף מים רותחים - 200 גרם חמאה בטמפרטורת החדר - 100 גרם אבקת סוכר - ¼ כפית מלח - 1 כפית תמצית וניל איכותית - 2 כוסות קמח כוסמין לבן או קמח רגיל - 100 גרם שוקולד מריר קצוץ הוראות הכנה 1. מערבבים את נס הקפה עם כף המים רותחים בכוס קטנה. 2. במיקסר עם וו גיטרה מקרימים את הסוכר והחמאה כשלוש דקות עד שהתערובת חלקה ותפוחה. 3. מוסיפים את הקפה והוניל ומערבבים היטב. 4. מורידים את מהירות המיקסר לנמוכה ומוסיפים את הקמח והמלח. 5. מוסיפים את השוקולד ומערבבים היטב עד לאחידות. 6. מעבירים את התערובת לשקית ניילון, מהדקים את הבצק היטב כלפי מטה ויוצרים צורה של ריבוע או גליל. 7. שולחים למקרר לשעתיים לפחות, עדיף ללילה. 8. מחממים תנור ל-180 מעלות. 9. חותכים את השקית בעדינות, משחררים את הבצק ומניחים אותו על קרש חיתוך. 10. חותכים עוגיות בעזרת סכין גדולה וחדה בעובי חצי ס״מ. 11. מניחים על נייר אפייה ברווחים. 12. אופים 8-11 דקות עד שהעוגיות מתחילות להזהיב. 13. מוציאים את העוגיות כשהן נראות לא מוכנות כי הן מתקשות כשהן מתקררות.
