title: Corned Beef & Pastrami
text: corned beef & pastrami source: amazingribs.com ingredients - beef brisket (preferably the flat cut) - kosher salt (5-6% of total water weight) - sugar (2-3% of total water weight) - pink curing salt (0.25% of total weight) - whole allspice berries (15ml) - whole mustard seeds brown or yellow (15ml) - coriander seeds (15ml) - red pepper flakes (15ml) - whole black peppercorns (15ml) - whole cloves (10ml) - whole cardamom pods (9 pods) - bay leaves (6 large, crumbled) - ground ginger (10ml) - cinnamon stick (1/2 stick) - juniper berries (9 berries) - fresh coarsely ground black pepper (15ml per 1/2 kg meat) - coriander powder (15ml per 1/2 kg meat) - brown sugar (15ml per 1/2 kg meat) - paprika (15ml per 1/2 kg meat) - garlic powder (10ml per 1/2 kg meat) - onion powder (10ml per 1/2 kg meat) - yellow mustard seeds (2ml per 1/2 kg meat) - mustard powder (2ml per 1/2 kg meat) - water - apple juice (for wrapping) instructions 1. toast and crush the allspice berries, mustard seeds, coriander seeds, red pepper flakes, peppercorns, cloves, and cardamom pods in a small frying pan on medium heat until fragrant, being careful not to burn them. 2. remove the toasted spices from heat and place in a small bowl, then crush them lightly with a mortar and pestle or the back of a spoon. 3. stir the crumbled bay leaves and ground ginger into the crushed spices. 4. add about 45ml of the spice mix, the half stick of cinnamon, kosher salt, pink salt, and brown sugar to a gallon of water in a large pot. 5. bring the brine to a boil, then remove from heat and let cool to room temperature before refrigerating until well chilled. 6. place the brisket in a large container and cover completely with the chilled brine, weighing it down with a plate if it floats. 7. cure the brisket in the refrigerator for at least 5 days. 8. desalinate the cured brisket by covering it with cold water in the refrigerator for at least 8 hours, changing the water at least once. 9. for corned beef, place the desalted brisket in a large pot covered with at least one inch of water. 10. add a tablespoon of the pickling spices to the pot and bring to a boil, then reduce to a very low simmer and cook for 3-4 hours until fork tender. 11. for pastrami, rinse the desalted meat and apply the dry rub, then refrigerate for at least overnight, preferably a day or two. 12. smoke the rubbed brisket at 120°c until it reaches an internal temperature of 71°c and the crust is brown. 13. wrap the smoked brisket tightly in foil, add a bit of apple juice or water, and roast until the internal temperature reaches 95°c. 14. alternatively, after smoking, transfer the brisket to a steamer and steam it for 2-3 hours until tender. 15. let the finished brisket rest for at least 30 minutes. 16. slice the brisket by hand into thin slices about 1/8 inch (3.2 mm) thick, cutting perpendicular to the grain.

title: Milk Bar Crack Pie
text: milk bar crack pie source: ifyougiveablondeakitchen.com ingredients - nonstick vegetable oil spray - 135ml (1 stick plus 15ml or 127 g) unsalted butter (room temperature, divided) - 82ml (70 g) packed light brown sugar (divided) - 30ml (25 g) granulated sugar - 1 large egg (room temperature) - 180ml plus 30ml old-fashioned oats - 120ml (62 g) all purpose flour - 1ml baking powder - 1ml baking soda - 1ml generous salt - 180ml (150 g) granulated sugar - 120ml (100 g) packed light brown sugar - 15ml nonfat dry milk powder - 1ml salt - 120ml (1 stick or 113 g) unsalted butter (melted, cooled slightly) - 98ml heavy whipping cream - 4 large egg yolks - 5ml vanilla extract - powdered sugar (for dusting) instructions 1. preheat oven to 177°c. line a 13x9 cookie sheet (rimmed) with parchment paper and coat with nonstick spray. set aside. 2. in the bowl of a stand mixer (or using a hand mixer), combine 90ml butter, 60ml brown sugar, and 30ml sugar. beat mixture until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes. scrape down the sides of the bowl as necessary. add egg and beat until pale and fluffy, about 2 more minutes. add oats, flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt and beat on medium speed until well blended, about 1 minute. 3. turn oat mixture out onto prepared baking pan; press out evenly to edges of pan. if the dough is sticking to your fingers, wet them with water and continue pressing oat mixture out evenly. cookie layer should be about 1/4-inch thick. 4. bake until light golden, about 12 to 14 minutes (don't overbake). transfer baking pan to rack and cool cookie completely. 5. using hands (or a food processor), crush oat cookie into small crumbles and place in a large bowl. add 45ml butter and 22ml brown sugar. rub in with fingertips until mixture is moist enough to stick together. transfer cookie crust mixture to 9-inch diameter glass pie dish. using fingers, press mixture evenly onto bottom and up sides of pie dish. place pie dish with crust on rimmed baking sheet. 6. position rack in center of oven and preheat to 177°c. 7. in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the whisk attachment (or you can whisk vigorously by hand), combine both sugars, milk powder, and salt in medium bowl to blend. add melted butter and whisk until blended. add cream, then egg yolks and vanilla, and whisk until well combined and mixture is pale in color. 8. pour filling into crust. bake pie at 177°c for 20 minutes (filling may begin to bubble). reduce oven temperature to 163°c. continue to bake pie until filling is brown in spots and set around edges but center still moves slightly when pie dish is gently shaken, about 15 to 20 minutes longer. cool pie 2 hours in pie dish on rack. chill uncovered overnight. 9. sift powdered sugar lightly over top of pie. cut pie into wedges and serve cold.

title: Cranberry Ginger Shandy
text: cranberry ginger shandy source: thespruceeats.com ingredients - 360ml cranberry juice - 1 (12-ounce) bottle ginger beer - 120ml freshly squeezed lemon juice, from 2 to 3 lemons - 2 (12-ounce) bottles pale ale or wheat beer - ginger sugar, for optional rim - lemon wedges, for garnish instructions 1. in a large pitcher, combine the cranberry juice, ginger beer, and lemon juice and stir well. 2. chill the mixture until you're ready to serve. 3. add beer to the pitcher just before serving. 4. before serving, rim tall glasses with a ginger-sugar rim by wetting the rim with lemon juice and rolling it in a mix of ground ginger and sugar. 5. pour the shandy into the prepared glasses over ice if desired and garnish with a lemon wedge.

title: Cream Sufganiyot
text: cream sufganiyot source: null ingredients - 38 g active sourdough starter (white, 100% hydration) - 38 g water - 76 g bread flour - 390 g bread flour or 50/50 bread/ap - 152 g stiff levain - 100 g eggs (2 eggs) - 128 g whole milk (cold) - 75 g sugar - 7 g salt - 75 g unsalted butter (softened, cubed) - 360 g whole milk - 1 vanilla bean pod or 5ml extract - 60 g sugar - 23 g corn starch - 4 egg yolks - pinch of salt - 25 g unsalted butter - 2 l frying oil - 200 g sugar for coating instructions 1. mix starter, water, and flour and cover to rise at 75-26°c (24-26°c) for 8-10 hours until tripled. 2. mix flour, levain, eggs, milk, sugar, and salt with dough hook until just combined and autolyse for 30 minutes. 3. mix for 5 minutes more. 4. slowly add butter cubes and mix on medium for 15-25 minutes until the dough passes the windowpane test. 5. perform bulk proof for 6 hours at 75-26°c with folds at 1.5 hours and 3 hours. 6. cold-proof for 6-8 hours. 7. whisk egg yolks, sugar, cornstarch, and salt together. 8. halve vanilla bean and scrape the seeds. 9. heat milk with vanilla until almost boiling. 10. slowly pour the hot milk over the yolks while whisking constantly. 11. strain the mixture back into the pot and heat while whisking until thick and shiny. 12. remove from heat, add butter, and add extract if using vanilla extract instead of bean. 13. cover pastry cream with plastic wrap touching the surface and cool, then refrigerate. 14. divide dough into 15 pieces of 60g each, shape into rounds, and place on floured parchment squares. 15. proof in oven with light on at approximately 26°c for 10-14 hours until doubled. 16. heat oil to 180-185°c (356-185°c). 17. fry each doughnut for approximately 2 minutes per side, top down first. 18. drain on a rack with paper towels and toss in sugar while warm. 19. stir cooled pastry cream, pierce doughnut centers, and pipe filling generously. 20. serve the same day as frying.

title: Cream of Mushroom Soup
text: cream of mushroom soup source: food.com ingredients - 227g fresh mushrooms - 30ml chopped onions - 1 to 2 minced garlic cloves - 30ml butter - 2 to 45ml flour, separated - 480ml chicken broth - 240ml light cream or 240ml evaporated milk - 2ml salt - 1ml pepper - 1ml nutmeg instructions 1. cut the mushrooms into slices. 2. melt butter in a large frying pan and add the onions, garlic, and mushrooms, then cook until the onions are soft. 3. blend in 30ml of flour and stir. 4. add the chicken broth and heat until slightly thickened while stirring frequently. 5. stir cream with an additional 15ml of flour and seasonings, then add the cream to the soup and heat to thicken while stirring frequently. 6. serve and enjoy.

title: Cream סופגניות
text: cream סופגניות <https://breadbyelise.com/sourdough-cream-filled-doughnuts/ --- sourdough cream filled doughnuts ingredients stiff levain - 38 g active sourdough starter (white, 100% hydration) - 38 g water - 76 g bread flour main dough - 390 g bread flour or 50/50 bread/ap - 152 g stiff levain - 100 g eggs (2 eggs) - 128 g whole milk (cold) - 75 g sugar - 7 g salt - 75 g unsalted butter (softened, cubed) vanilla cream filling - 360 g whole milk - 1 vanilla bean pod or 5ml extract - 60 g sugar - 23 g corn starch - 4 egg yolks - pinch of salt - 25 g unsalted butter other - 2 l frying oil - 200 g sugar for coating instructions day 1: stiff levain mix starter, water, and flour. cover and rise at 75-26°c (24-26°c) for 8-10 hours until tripled. day 2: main dough 1. mix flour, levain, eggs, milk, sugar, salt with dough hook until just combined. autolyse 30 min. 2. mix 5 minutes more. 3. slowly add butter cubes. mix on medium 15-25 min until passes windowpane. 4. bulk proof 6h at 75-26°c. 5. folds at 1.5h and 3h. 6. cold-proof 6-8h. day 2: vanilla pastry cream 1. whisk yolks, sugar, cornstarch, salt. 2. halve vanilla bean and scrape. 3. heat milk + vanilla until almost boiling. 4. slowly pour over yolks while whisking. 5. strain back into pot. heat, whisking, until thick and shiny. 6. off heat, add butter. add extract if using. 7. cover with plastic touching surface. cool, refrigerate. day 2: shape & final proof 1. divide into 15 pieces (60g). shape into rounds. place on floured parchment squares. 2. proof in oven with light on, 26°c, 10-14 hours until doubled. day 3: fry 1. heat oil to 180-185°c (356-185°c). 2. fry 2 min per side, top down first. 3. drain on rack with paper towels. 4. toss in sugar while warm. assembly stir cooled pastry cream. pierce doughnut centers, pipe filling generously. notes - serve same day as frying - yields 15 doughnuts

title: Beetroot and Apple Salad with Yogurt Dressing and Hazelnuts
text: beetroot and apple salad with yogurt dressing and hazelnuts source: tobiascooks.com ingredients - 500 grams boiled beetroot - 250 grams peeled apples - juice of half a lemon - 150 grams greek yogurt - 15ml honey - pinch of salt - 100 grams hazelnuts, chopped instructions 1. grate the beetroot and the peeled apple into a bowl. 2. sprinkle the lemon juice over the grated vegetables and mix well. 3. for the dressing, dissolve the honey and salt with the lemon juice. 4. dissolve the greek yogurt into the dressing mixture. 5. crush the hazelnuts with a knife. 6. place salad on a plate, pour some dressing over it, and sprinkle nuts on top.

title: Crispy Baked Chicken Wings
text: crispy baked chicken wings source: kitchensanctuary.com ingredients - 998g (1 kg) chicken wings - 2 level tbsp aluminium-free baking powder - 2ml salt - 2ml pepper - 300ml (300g) tomato ketchup - 60ml white wine vinegar - 75ml dark brown sugar - 30ml black treacle or molasses - 45ml honey - 30ml vegetable oil - 15ml worcestershire sauce - 2ml mustard powder - 8ml smoked paprika - 2ml black pepper instructions 1. preheat the oven to 120c/121°c and place a rack on a large baking tray. 2. cut each wing at the joint so you have a mini wing and a drumette. 3. dry the wings with paper towels, then place in a large bowl and add the baking powder, salt and pepper. 4. toss to combine and discard any remaining coating once tossed together. 5. place in a single layer on the rack on the lower shelf of the oven for 30 minutes. 6. after 30 minutes, turn the oven up to 220c/218°c and rotate the tray for even cooking. 7. cook for a further 45-50 minutes until the wings are lightly golden and crispy. 8. whilst the wings are baking, place all barbecue sauce ingredients in a saucepan and mix together. 9. heat over a medium-high heat until boiling, then simmer for 5 minutes and turn off the heat. 10. toss the barbecue sauce with the wings and serve straightaway. notes ninja air fryer with smke 200 for 20-30 minutes, flip middle cooking cornstarch and chicken soup mix with the backing powder

title: Crown O'Gold Meat Loaf
text: crown o'gold meat loaf ingredients - 360ml fine soft bread crumbs - 680g ground lean chuck beef - 4 egg yolks - 8ml salt - 30ml french's mustard - 22ml prepared horseradish - 45ml finely diced green pepper - 30ml french's minced onion - 80ml ketchup - 4 egg whites - 1ml french's cream of tartar - 60ml french's mustard (for topping) instructions 1. mix bread crumbs with meat. 2. combine the egg yolks, salt, mustard, horseradish, green pepper, minced onion, and ketchup. 3. blend the mixture into the meat and bread crumbs. 4. pack lightly into a 9-inch casserole and bake in a moderate oven at 163°c for 30 minutes. 5. beat egg whites until foamy and add cream of tartar, then beat until very stiff. 6. fold mustard gently into the egg white mixture. 7. swirl the topping on the hot meat and return to the oven. 8. bake for 20 to 25 minutes longer or until tipped with brown.

title: Crumb Cake Muffins
text: crumb cake muffins source: thefirstyearblog.com ingredients - 900ml all purpose flour - 420ml granulated sugar - 15ml baking powder - 5ml salt - 5ml cinnamon - 1ml nutmeg - 2 large eggs - 300ml buttermilk - 120ml vegetable oil - 10ml vanilla extract - 45ml unsalted butter, melted - 80ml brown sugar - 8ml cinnamon - 180ml all purpose flour - 80ml brown sugar - 5ml cinnamon - 1ml salt - 60ml unsalted butter, melted - 60ml powdered sugar - 2ml vanilla extract - 5ml milk instructions 1. prepare the cinnamon sugar layer by melting the butter, stirring in the brown sugar and cinnamon until thick, and setting it aside to thicken while you make the muffin batter. 2. in a mixing bowl combine the flour, granulated sugar, baking powder, salt, cinnamon and nutmeg, then stir with a spoon to combine and set aside. 3. in a larger mixing bowl combine the eggs, buttermilk, vegetable oil and vanilla extract, then stir to combine with a fork or spatula for 30 seconds. 4. gradually mix in the dry ingredients, mixing by hand just until combined until the batter is thick. 5. cover the bowl with a towel and allow the batter to rest for 15 minutes while preheating the oven to 425ºf. 6. during the 15 minute rest, make the crumb topping by combining the flour, brown sugar, cinnamon, salt and melted butter in a mixing bowl, stirring well with a spatula and using your hands to squeeze clumps together until the mixture looks wet and sandy in texture. 7. line a 12 count muffin pan with 6 muffin liners in every other well to allow the muffins to spread and dome without running into each other. 8. fill the liners with 30ml of batter, drop 5ml of the cinnamon sugar mixture in the center of each muffin and spread with your fingers, then add 4-90ml of batter to cover the cinnamon sugar. 9. crumble the crumb topping into fine crumbs over each muffin and press it on slightly, optionally sprinkling with sanding sugar. 10. place the pan in the center of the oven and bake for 7 minutes at 425ºf, then reduce the temperature to 350ºf and bake for 16-20 minutes until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. 11. allow the muffins to cool in the pan for 15 minutes before removing, then repeat with the remaining batter. 12. for the optional glaze, combine the powdered sugar, vanilla extract and milk in a small mixing bowl, adjusting thickness by adding more powdered sugar if needed, then drizzle over the muffins.

title: Crunchy Baked Chicken Tenders
text: crunchy baked chicken tenders source: recipetin eats ingredients - 360ml panko breadcrumbs - oil spray - 1 egg - 15ml mayonnaise - 22ml dijon mustard - 30ml flour - 2ml salt - black pepper - 500 g chicken tenderloins instructions 1. preheat oven to 200c/199°c. 2. spread panko on a baking tray, spray with oil, and bake for 3 to 5 minutes until light golden, then transfer to a bowl. 3. place a rack on a baking tray. 4. whisk together the egg, mayonnaise, dijon mustard, flour, salt, and black pepper until combined. 5. add the chicken into the batter and toss to coat. 6. pick up chicken with tongs and place it into the panko bowl, sprinkle the surface with breadcrumbs, press down to adhere, and transfer onto the baking tray. 7. spray lightly with oil, sprinkle with a touch of salt if desired, and bake for 15 to 20 minutes. 8. remove from oven and serve immediately with your choice of dipping sauce.

title: Curd Meat Basturma
text: curd meat basturma ingredients - beef or lamb (whole cut, trimmed) - curing salt - smoking wood instructions 1. hang the meat in the refrigerator on a wire rack at temperatures between 34-4°c (1-4°c) to allow airflow. 2. check for firmness, which indicates the meat is drying well. 3. continue the dry curing phase for 10 to 14 days, or until the surface is dry and the meat feels firmer to the touch. 4. once the meat has fully cured and dried in the refrigerator, cold smoke it at around 70-32°c (21-32°c) for 12-24 hours depending on the smokiness you prefer. 5. keep the smoking chamber's temperature low to avoid cooking the meat while infusing it with smoke. 6. ensure the meat hangs freely with good air circulation on all sides throughout the process. 7. monitor the meat's weight before and after curing to check for moisture loss, aiming for about a 30% weight reduction.

title: Cured Meat Basturma
text: cured meat basturma ingredients - 756.6 gr meat - 100 gr ground fenugreek - 100 gr sweet paprika - 15ml freshly ground black pepper - 15ml cayenne pepper - 15ml ground cumin - 15ml ground coriander - 6 large garlic cloves, ground - 5ml beet powder - 20 cc cognac instructions 1. wash off the meat and soak in cold water for 3 hours. 2. mix together the ground fenugreek, sweet paprika, black pepper, cayenne pepper, cumin, coriander, ground garlic cloves, beet powder, and cognac. 3. cover the meat with the spice mixture.

title: Danielle's Italian Dressing
text: danielle's italian dressing ingredients - 240ml extra virgin olive oil - 100ml white wine vinegar - 30g minced garlic - 1/2 lemon - 5ml dried oregano - 1ml chilli flakes - 40g minced shallots or onion instructions 1. finely chop the garlic and shallots, or use onion instead of shallots if preferred. 2. sizzle the garlic and shallots in the olive oil over low heat for five minutes. 3. add in the chilli and oregano and sizzle for one more minute. 4. pour this combined mixture into a jar and allow to cool before adding the vinegar. 5. juice half a lemon and add salt to the jar. 6. shake well to combine. 7. pour onto the salad and enjoy.

title: Danish Loaf Bread - 3 Ways (Cocoa/Matcha/Ube)
text: danish loaf bread - 3 ways (cocoa/matcha/ube) source: the glutton ingredients - 180 grams bread flour - 50 grams cake flour - 3 grams instant yeast - 15 grams milk powder - 1 egg - 90 grams cold water - 25 grams caster sugar - 1ml fine sea salt - 10 grams butter, softened - 115 grams unsalted butter to make a 5 x 5-inch square butter insert - 8 grams cocoa powder (valrhona) for cocoa version - 6 grams matcha powder (uji) for matcha version - 6 grams ube/purple yam powder for ube version instructions 1. knead dough until it passes a window pane test, about 20 to 30 minutes, using manual kneading, stand mixer, or bread machine 2. chill dough in fridge overnight to proof 3. take out dough from fridge and form into a smooth, round ball 4. cover with tea towel and let rest for 20 minutes 5. cut butter into pieces and lay them down side by side on parchment paper 6. sprinkle cocoa/matcha/ube powder on both sides of butter, pound with rolling pin to soften, roll evenly and shape into a 5-inch square 7. chill butter insert overnight before using 8. roll out dough into 8 x 8-inch square, place butter at an angle like a diamond 9. roll out each flap/side into about 4-inch length and fold each flap to encase butter within dough, pressing edges to seal 10. sprinkle flour on work surface and top of dough to prevent sticking 11. press rolling pin up and down, creating ridges on top of dough 12. roll out dough into 8 x 15-inch rectangle and do 3-fold by folding one short side at two-thirds of the rectangle length, then the other short side over it making 3 layers 13. rotate dough 90 degrees with opening on the right side, creating a 5 x 8-inch rectangle 14. repeat the turn 3 times total, wrapping dough in plastic wrap and freezing for 20 minutes after each turn 15. fluff/lift dough often as you roll to prevent sticking, sprinkling flour as needed and brushing off excess before folding 16. freeze dough for 20 minutes after the 3rd turn 17. lightly grease an 8x4-1/2x4-1/4 inch non-stick pullman tin 18. roll out dough into 6 x 16-inch rectangle 19. cut dough into 3 equal strips and cut strips into 3 equal pieces, not cutting the top part through 20. do a 3-strand braid, making sure the layered part is exposed at the top 21. turn the braid upside down and fold into 3 layers with the top of braid in the middle 22. place the stacked braid middle side up in the prepared pullman pan and spray with water to prevent drying 23. cover pan with plastic wrap or tea towel, place on baking sheet and let proof until it fills about 90% of tin or nearly to the rim, 4 to 4 1/2 hours depending on ambient temperature 24. preheat oven to 210°c 25. put the cover on the pullman tin and let proof for another 10 to 20 minutes 26. bake for 35 to 40 minutes until crust is golden brown 27. take danish loaf immediately out of tin and place on wire rack to cool completely before slicing

title: Date & Nut Energy Bites
text: date & nut energy bites source: null ingredients - 500g seedless dates (medjool or vacuum-packed) - 100g raw or lightly roasted pistachios - 100g raw or lightly roasted cashew nuts - 100g raw or lightly roasted almonds - 60ml ghee or coconut oil - 15ml chia seeds - 2ml ground cardamom or cinnamon - 5ml vanilla extract - 30ml cacao nibs - 1–30ml unsweetened shredded coconut instructions 1. coarsely chop the pistachios, cashews, and almonds or pulse them in a food processor a few times. 2. optionally lightly toast the nuts in a dry pan over medium heat for 3–5 minutes, stirring constantly, until just fragrant, then let cool. 3. if your dates are dry, soak them in warm water for 5–10 minutes, then drain well. 4. add the softened dates and ghee to a food processor and blend until you get a thick, sticky paste, scraping down the sides as needed. 5. add vanilla or spices to the date paste if using. 6. transfer the paste to a mixing bowl and mix in the chopped nuts, chia seeds, and cacao nibs if using. 7. knead everything together with your hands or a spatula until it is thick and moldable. 8. roll the mixture into small balls, about 25–30 pieces depending on size. 9. optionally roll the balls in shredded coconut, cocoa powder, or ground nuts for coating. 10. store in an airtight container in the fridge for 2–3 weeks or freeze for up to 3 months.

title: Detox Juice
text: detox juice ingredients - 4 large carrots, unpeeled, ends trimmed - 4 celery sticks, leaves attached, washed - 1/2 beetroot, scrubbed - 6 sprigs fresh continental parsley - 4cm-piece fresh ginger, washed, unpeeled - ice cubes, to serve instructions no instructions provided.

title: Drambuie Cocktail
text: drambuie cocktail ingredients - 1 part drambuie - 1 part ginger ale - 1 part soda or sparkling white wine - 1 part orange juice - grated ginger for garnish instructions 1. fill a glass with ice. 2. add equal parts drambuie, ginger ale, soda or sparkling white wine, and orange juice. 3. garnish with grated ginger.

title: Early 18th-Century Batter Cake
text: early 18th-century batter cake ingredients - 237.5 g flour - 142.5 g dark raisins or sultanas - 83 g melted butter - 100 g mature stiff sourdough starter (60% hydration) - 2 large egg yolks - 100 ml 38% cream - 35.5 g candied citron, lemon, and orange peel - 25 ml sack (sherry or sweet cooking wine) - 24 g sugar - 1.5 g ground mace - 1 g ground clove - 1.5 g grated nutmeg - pinch of beaten cinnamon - 2 tbls honey water instructions 1. soak raisins and candied peel in the sack for 15–30 minutes to enhance flavor and texture. 2. in a large bowl, mix the flour, sugar, spices, and soaked fruits. 3. in a separate bowl, whisk together the melted butter, cream, egg yolks, and honey water. 4. add the wet mixture and the mature stiff sourdough starter to the dry ingredients and stir until a thick, cohesive batter forms, adjusting with a small amount of cream or water if needed. 5. cover and let rise in a warm place for 3–5 hours, or until visibly puffed. 6. stir down or gently fold the batter to redistribute air pockets and fruit. 7. line the bottom of a 6-inch baking hoop or springform pan with parchment paper and grease sides if needed. 8. pour in the batter and smooth the surface. 9. bake at 180°c (177°c) for 40–50 minutes, or until a skewer inserted in the center comes out clean. 10. let cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then remove and cool completely on a wire rack.

title: Easy One-Bowl Yogurt Coffee Cake
text: easy one-bowl yogurt coffee cake ingredients streusel topping - 115g (120ml packed) brown sugar - 70g (120ml) whole wheat flour - 15ml cinnamon - 1ml salt - shy 1ml cardamom - 55g (60ml) unsalted butter, melted cake - 395g (480ml) sugar - 170g (180ml) unsalted butter, softened - 20ml baking powder - 5ml salt - 14g vanilla extract - 3 eggs - 340g (2⅔ cups) all-purpose flour - 395g (1⅔ cups) plain greek yogurt instructions 1. preheat oven to 177°c and grease a 9x13 baking pan. 2. combine brown sugar, flour, cinnamon, salt, cardamom, and melted butter to make the streusel, mix until crumbly, and set aside. 3. in a large bowl, beat together sugar, butter, baking powder, salt, and vanilla until fluffy. 4. add eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition. 5. alternately fold in flour and greek yogurt, beginning and ending with flour, until just combined. 6. pour batter into prepared pan and sprinkle streusel evenly over the top. 7. bake for approximately 40 minutes, or until a toothpick comes out clean. 8. cool before serving.

title: Pro Eggnog
text: pro eggnog ingredients - 4 large eggs - 128g (135g) granulated sugar - 340g (360ml) whole milk - 227g (240ml) heavy whipping cream - 142g (150ml) añejo tequila - 198g (210ml) amontillado sherry - freshly-grated nutmeg instructions 1. add eggs to blender and turn on at low speed. 2. with blender still running, slowly add sugar, milk, and cream. 3. slowly add in tequila and sherry. 4. store in refrigerator until ready to serve. 5. pour into chilled glass. 6. grate fresh nutmeg over the top.

title: Shelf-Stable Banana Peel Switchel
text: shelf-stable banana peel switchel ingredients - 1ml banana peel flour - 2ml ground ginger - 30 ml raw apple cider vinegar - 30 ml blackstrap molasses - 1ml sea salt or pink salt - 15 ml bottled lemon juice - 1.5 liters water instructions 1. in a mug, combine 2ml ground ginger and 125 ml boiling water, stir and let steep for 2–3 minutes to release full flavor. 2. in a large pitcher or bottle, combine 1ml banana peel flour, 30 ml apple cider vinegar, 30 ml molasses, lemon juice, and salt. 3. add the strained ginger tea to the pitcher and pour in the remaining 1375 ml water, then stir or shake well. 4. refrigerate for 1–2 hours for best flavor, shake before serving, and pour over ice or add a splash of sparkling water for fizz.

title: Electrolyte Drink
text: electrolyte drink ingredients - 1ml banana peel flour - 1ml pink himalayan salt or sea salt - 1ml cream of tartar - juice of ½ lemon or lime - 5ml apple cider vinegar with the mother (optional) - 5ml honey or a pinch of stevia (optional) - 300–500 ml water, still or lightly sparkling instructions 1. in a cup or shaker bottle, add the banana peel flour, salt, and cream of tartar. 2. add the lemon juice, vinegar, and honey or stevia. 3. pour in the water and whisk or shake vigorously to mix. 4. drink immediately or chill briefly for better flavor.

title: End-of-Season Zucchini and Green Pepper Relish
text: end-of-season zucchini and green pepper relish source: thekitchn.com ingredients - 1.4kg zucchini (if it’s a truly giant one, remove the woody seeds) - 680g green peppers, seeded - 1 medium yellow onion, halved - 600ml apple cider vinegar - 240ml brown sugar - 15ml mustard seeds - 15ml sea salt - 2ml red chili flakes - 1 lemon, zested and juiced instructions 1. arrange 4 empty regular mouth pint jars in a canning pot or a 12-quart stock pot fitted with a round cake cooling rack. fill the pot with enough water to cover the jars. place a lid on the pot and bring it to a boil. wash the lids and rings in warm, soapy water and set aside. 2. fit a food processor with a grating blade and use it to break down the zucchini, green peppers, and onion. if you don't have a food processor, pull out your trusty box grater and get to work. 3. combine the zucchini, pepper, and onion shreds with the vinegar, brown sugar, mustard seeds, salt, and red chili flakes in a large pot and bring to a boil. 4. cook the relish at a boil until the liquid has reduced some, 2 to 3 minutes. add the lemon zest and juice and stir to combine. 5. remove relish from the heat and, using a wide-mouth funnel, funnel it into prepared jars, leaving approximately 1/2 inch headspace. after all the jars are full, use a wooden chopstick to work the air bubbles out of the jars. 6. wipe the rims, apply the lids and rings, and lower the filled jars into the canning pot and make sure that they are covered with only about an inch of water. if you need to remove some water from the pot, use a heatproof measuring cup. once the pot has returned to a rolling boil, start your timer for 10 minutes. this proces sterilizes the jars and contents, and it forces the air out of the jars, creating a situation in which the jars will form a vacuum seal once out of the water. 7. when time is up, remove jars from canner and place them on a folded kitchen towel to cool. when the jars have cooled enough that you can comfortably handle them, check the seals by removing the rings, grasping the jar by the edge of the lid and gently lifting it an inch or two off the countertop. if the lid holds fast, the seal is good. sealed jars can be stored at room temperature for up to a year. any unsealed jars should be refrigerated and used promptly.

title: English Muffins
text: english muffins ingredients - 250g bread flour - 100g ap flour - 50g semolina flour - 50g whole wheat flour - 50g spelt flour - 310g water - 100g levain - 20g salt instructions 1. mix the flour, water, levain and salt for 5 minutes in a mixer or by hand. 2. ferment at room temperature for 6 hours. 3. cold ferment for 15 hours or more. 4. turn the dough onto a floured work surface. 5. stretch or roll the dough to a 1cm thickness. 6. line a sheet pan with parchment paper for proofing and top with semolina or corn meal. 7. use a baking ring 7.5-10cm in diameter and cut out pieces. 8. put leftover dough back together, roll out and cut out additional muffins. 9. proof for 1 hour. 10. heat a cast iron skillet on low to medium heat. 11. dust the cast iron skillet with semolina or corn meal. 12. bake each muffin 3-4 minutes per side.

title: Vintage Cocktail Books - A Timeline
text: vintage cocktail books - a timeline source: difford's guide this is a bibliography and reference guide rather than a recipe, documenting the history and timeline of vintage cocktail books published from 1800 onwards. the page provides links to historical cocktail recipe books organized chronologically by publication period, many of which are available to read online through resources including the exposition universelle des vins et spiritueux digital library, archive.org, and cocktail kingdom's library. the timeline begins with richard cook's first known dedicated english-language book recording drinks recipes in 1827 and continues through 1999, helping readers understand the origin and development of classic cocktails that appear on bar menus today.

title: Fermented Lemons
text: fermented lemons ingredients - 850g lemons - 60g coarse salt - mint (or other herbs like lavender) instructions 1. chop off the ends of the lemons and quarter them. 2. mix the lemon quarters with coarse salt, approximately 60g. 3. squeeze the lemons to release their juices. 4. layer the squeezed lemons and salt mixture in a jar with mint or other herbs of your choice.

title: Step by Step Sourdough Croissants
text: step by step sourdough croissants source: homegrownhappiness.co.nz ingredients - 30 g starter - 60 g all-purpose flour - 60 g water - 450 g all-purpose flour - 8 g salt - 40 g sugar - 230 g water - all the active sourdough starter (around 140g) - 50 g unsalted butter (room temperature) - 250 g unsalted butter (room temperature or cold depending on method used, see notes) - 22ml all-purpose flour ((only for the flour method, see notes)) - 1 egg + 15ml water instructions 1. in the morning, feed your starter by combining the starter, flour, and water in a bowl and mixing until well combined. tip it into a clean jar and leave until doubled or tripled and at peak. 2. mix all the dough ingredients together by hand to form a sticky dough ball. knead on the bench for 5 to 8 minutes until smooth. it will still be a bit sticky, which is fine. 3. place the dough in a greased bowl and cover. ferment for 3 hours at 23 to 25°c / 74 to 25°c (4 hours if your room is cooler), until puffed by around 30 to 40%. 4. shape the dough into a flat rectangle, wrap tightly or place in an airtight container, and chill in the fridge overnight. shaping it into a rectangle now means less rolling tomorrow, which keeps the dough cold and relaxed for lamination. 5. make the butter packet using either the bashing method or the flour method (see notes). roll it into a rectangle of about 15 x 20cm (6 x 8 inch) between two sheets of baking paper, then chill it in the fridge. 6. take the butter packet from the fridge and bash it firmly all over with the rolling pin, then give it a roll to bring it into a workable, bendy state. bashing the cold butter with the rolling pin works the fat into a smooth, pliable state without warming it, so it bends like cold clay instead of cracking. 7. on a floured bench, roll the chilled dough into a 20 x 40cm (8 x 16 inch) rectangle. place the butter packet in the middle. bring the top of the dough down and the bottom up to meet in the middle over the butter, then pinch the seam where they meet to seal. 8. make a shallow slit along each of the folded long edges (the closed sides where the butter is sealed in, not the open ends), to relieve the tension. then turn the dough a quarter turn. 9. gently press along the length of the dough with the rolling pin to start dispersing the butter, then roll out to around 8mm thick, focusing on lengthening rather than widening. always roll in one direction, away from you, lifting the pin and starting again rather than rolling back and forth, which smears the butter. dust with flour if it sticks. 10. brush off any excess flour, then fold the dough like a pamphlet, bringing the top third down to the middle and the bottom third up over the top. wrap tightly and chill for 30 minutes. 11. turn the chilled dough 90 degrees and roll out again to around 8mm thick. trim off any scraggly edges for more even layers. brush off excess flour, repeat the pamphlet fold, and chill for 20 to 30 minutes. 12. repeat the rolling and folding once more. after this third fold, chill the dough, tightly covered, for at least 2 hours. 13. roll the chilled dough into a 28 x 60cm (11 x 24 inch) rectangle, around 4mm thick. 14. mark 5cm (2 inch) intervals along both long edges. using a pizza cutter or large knife, cut triangles connecting the marks from top to bottom. a ruler helps keep your lines straight. 15. stretch the base of each triangle out a little, then roll up tightly from the base to the tip. bend the ends in slightly to make a crescent, or leave them straight. 16. place the shaped croissants on parchment-lined trays and proof in a warm but not hot spot until puffy, lighter, and jiggly when the tray is gently shaken, with visible layers. this can take 4 to 7 hours depending on your room temperature, so go by the look and feel rather than the clock. 17. to stop them drying out, spritz them gently with water or create a warm, humid spot by placing them in a cold, turned-off oven next to a cup of hot water. don't put the cup directly under the croissant tray, and don't let the spot get too hot, or the butter will melt and ruin the layers. 18. brush the proofed croissants with egg wash. 19. bake at 205°c / 204°c for around 20 minutes, until deeply browned. if they brown too quickly, turn the oven down a little. 20. let them cool to room temperature before slicing, so the layers stay nice and distinct.

title: Flaky Sourdough Discard Pie Crust (Sweet or Savory)
text: flaky sourdough discard pie crust (sweet or savory) source: theperfectloaf.com ingredients - 350g all-purpose flour - 14g granulated sugar - 6g fine sea salt - 226g unsalted butter, cold - 230g ripe sourdough starter discard, 100% hydration - 74g cold water instructions 1. in a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, and salt. cut the butter into small cubes. add the butter and lightly toss to coat with flour. using a pastry blender or the back of a fork, cut the butter into the flour until the butter is the size of small peas. add the sourdough starter and water. stir with a spatula until well combined. the dough should just come together, but add more water, one tablespoon at a time, as needed. 2. scrape the dough onto a clean work surface and knead it until it comes together. form the dough into a disc, then using a bench scraper, divide it directly in half. form each half into a disc, tightly wrap each in plastic wrap, and refrigerate for 2 hours (or overnight). 3. to use the crust, remove one disc from the fridge, unwrap it, and place it on a lightly floured work surface. using a rolling pin, roll the dough out into a round about 12 inches in diameter. fit to the bottom of a pie dish and repeat for the second disc for the top of the pie crust.

title: Flaky Dough
text: flaky dough ingredients - 185g (1¼ cups) all-purpose flour - 10ml sugar - 2ml salt - 115g (120ml) cold unsalted butter, cut into cubes - 2½ tbsp ice water instructions 1. combine flour, sugar, and salt in a food processor. 2. add cold butter cubes and pulse until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs with pea-sized pieces of butter remaining. 3. add ice water one tablespoon at a time, pulsing briefly after each addition, until the dough just comes together when pressed. 4. turn dough out onto a sheet of plastic wrap. 5. shape into a disc, wrap tightly, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour. 6. roll out on a lightly floured surface to the desired thickness. 7. drape dough over the pie tin, pressing gently into the edges. 8. trim and crimp edges. 9. for blind baking, line with parchment and fill with pie weights. 10. bake at 200°c/199°c for 15 minutes, remove weights, and bake another 5–10 minutes until golden.

title: Fluffy Sourdough Cornbread
text: fluffy sourdough cornbread source: blessthismessplease.com ingredients - 240ml sourdough starter, discard or fed - 240ml buttermilk - 240ml cornmeal - 240ml all-purpose flour - 2 eggs - 80ml granulated sugar - 2ml salt - 120ml melted butter - 10ml baking powder - 2ml baking soda instructions 1. mix the sourdough starter, milk, cornmeal, and flour together in a medium mixing bowl. at this point, you can cover the bowl with a clean dish towel and set the mixture aside at room temperature for 1 to 2 hours to help it develop a more sour flavor, or you can go right into adding the other ingredients. it's very flexible and can work with your taste preferences and schedule. do not let it rest more than 2 hours at room temperature, though. 2. when you are ready to move forward with making the cornbread after your chosen timing, preheat the oven to 177°c., and spray a 9-inch baking dish, cast iron skillet, or a round pie plate well with cooking spray (or butter it well). 3. add the eggs, sugar, salt, and butter to the flour mixture, and stir to combine. 4. add the baking powder and baking soda, and stir. 5. add the batter to the prepared pan, and smooth out the top with a spatula. 6. bake in the hot oven for 35 to 40 minutes, or until the top is golden-brown and the middle is cooked through. a toothpick inserted into the center should come out clean. 7. remove from the oven, and allow to cool for 10 minutes before slicing and serving hot with additional butter and honey to taste.

title: Focaccia
text: focaccia source: null ingredients - 50 g to 100 g sourdough starter - 10 g salt - 428 g water - 512 g bread flour - olive oil for drizzling - coarse sea salt - fresh, chopped rosemary instructions 1. whisk the starter and water together in a large bowl. 2. mix in salt and flour, stirring with a spatula until incorporated. 3. perform one fold 30 minutes after mixing the dough, folding 8 to 10 times. 4. drizzle with a splash of olive oil and rub the surface to coat. 5. cover the bowl and set aside to rise at room temperature until the dough reaches 50% rise. 6. pour about 30ml of olive oil into a 9×13-inch pan. 7. wet the dough with a tablespoon of olive oil, gently deflate it, and scoop into the center of the oil in the prepared pan. 8. fold the dough in from all sides to the center and rub the top with oil. 9. leave uncovered for 4 to 6 hours until puffy and nearly doubled. 10. heat the oven to 218°c. 11. rub your hands lightly with oil and use all ten fingers to press gently into the dough to dimple and stretch it to nearly fit the pan. 12. sprinkle generously with sea salt and rosemary. 13. transfer the pan to the oven and bake for about 25 minutes until golden all around.

title: Focaccia Genovese
text: focaccia genovese ingredients - 325 g bread flour - 275 g water - 50 g active starter - 6 g fine sea salt - 8 g olive oil - 1-2 small russet potatoes, julienned - 1 medium onion, thinly sliced - drizzling olive oil - large handful fresh herbs such as parsley or thyme - 50 g water for brine - 40 g olive oil for brine - 8 g fine sea salt for brine instructions 1. in a large mixing bowl, combine the flour and water, mix well until incorporated and cover, then let it rest for 20 minutes. 2. add the active starter, sea salt, and olive oil to the rested dough, then using wet hands, combine and mix the dough for 5 minutes using the rubaud method. 3. let the dough rest for 30 minutes after mixing. 4. grease a separate bowl and using wet hands, coil fold the dough a few times, rotating the bowl as needed, until it comes together into one blob. 5. transfer the dough to the greased bowl, cover, and let it double in size on the counter for around 7-8 hours depending on kitchen temperature. 6. preheat the oven to 260°c (260°c) once the dough has doubled in size. 7. using well-oiled hands, split the dough into two equal parts and transfer one piece into a well-oiled large cast iron skillet or baking sheet. 8. using your fingers, spread the dough out into a thin circle or rectangle and let rest for 10 minutes. 9. in a large shallow bowl, whisk together the water, olive oil, and salt to make the brine and set aside. 10. use a julienne peeler or knife or mandoline to prepare the potato or slice the onions. 11. add the potato or onions to a small bowl with a drizzling of olive oil and toss well to coat. 12. use your fingers to sprinkle and spread the toppings over the dough and gently press them in, or dimple the dough with your fingers if not using toppings. 13. whisk the brine again and pour it evenly over the bread. 14. bake for 13-15 minutes, then broil for around 3-5 minutes until the potatoes or onions and edges are slightly golden. 15. transfer the focaccia to a wire rack to cool for 10 minutes using a thin spatula. 16. sprinkle with roughly chopped fresh herbs if using, slice, and enjoy.

title: French Lentil Salad
text: french lentil salad ingredients - 200g french green lentils (puy lentils) - 1 bay leaf - 1 shallot, finely chopped - 1–2 carrots, finely diced - 30ml olive oil - 15ml red wine vinegar - 5ml dijon mustard - 30ml chopped parsley - salt and black pepper - optional: celery or fennel, extra herbs instructions 1. rinse the lentils. put them in a saucepan with the bay leaf and cover with plenty of water. 2. bring to a boil, then simmer gently for 20–25 minutes until tender but not mushy. 3. drain well and discard the bay leaf. 4. while the lentils cook, finely chop the shallot and carrots (and fennel/celery if using). 5. whisk together olive oil, red wine vinegar, dijon mustard, salt, and pepper to make the dressing. 6. toss the warm lentils with the vegetables, parsley, and dressing. 7. let sit at least 15–30 minutes before serving — it improves as it rests. notes - puy lentils are preferred: they stay firm and nutty. - some versions lightly sauté the vegetables first in olive oil for a sweeter, softer flavour. - excellent with feta, goat cheese, salmon, or a poached egg.

title: Fresh Basil Pesto
text: fresh basil pesto source: simplyrecipes.com ingredients - 480ml fresh basil leaves, packed (can sub half the basil leaves with baby spinach) - 120ml freshly grated romano or parmesan-reggiano cheese (about 57g) - 120ml extra virgin olive oil - 80ml pine nuts (can sub chopped walnuts) - 3 garlic cloves, minced (about 15ml) - 1ml salt, more to taste - 1ml freshly ground black pepper, more to taste instructions 1. place the basil leaves and pine nuts into the bowl of a food processor and pulse several times. 2. add the garlic and parmesan or romano cheese and pulse several times more. scrape down the sides of the food processor with a rubber spatula. 3. while the food processor is running, slowly add the olive oil in a steady small stream. adding the olive oil slowly while the processor is running will help it emulsify and help keep the olive oil from separating. occasionally, stop to scrape down the sides of the food processor. 4. add salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste. toss with pasta for a quick sauce, dollop over baked potatoes, or spread onto crackers or toasted slices of bread. did you enjoy this recipe? let us know with a rating and review!

title: Fried Cheese Balls From Crete
text: fried cheese balls from crete source: lemonandolives.com ingredients - 425g (425g) ricotta cheese - 1 egg - 60ml flour, plus extra for rolling - 5ml oregano - 30ml dried parsley - 2ml thyme - salt - pepper - 160ml oil for frying instructions 1. in a large bowl, combine all ingredients except oil and mix well. 2. place the mixture in the refrigerator to set for about 30-45 minutes. 3. add oil to a pan and heat over medium heat. 4. once the oil is hot, remove the cheese mixture from the refrigerator. 5. add some flour to a plate for easy rolling. 6. take a golf ball-sized amount of cheese mixture, place it in the flour, roll it around to coat and form a ball. 7. shake off excess flour and place the ball in the pan. 8. fry for 3-4 minutes on each side or until golden brown. 9. remove and place on a paper towel. 10. repeat with the remaining cheese mixture. 11. serve warm.

title: Fruit Filled Cheesecake
text: fruit filled cheesecake source: allrecipes.com ingredients - 240ml all-purpose flour - 240ml rolled oats - 2ml baking powder - 80ml packed brown sugar - 120ml butter - 420ml apple pie filling - 2 (227g) packages cream cheese, softened - 240ml white sugar - 8ml vanilla extract - 480ml sour cream - 3 eggs instructions 1. preheat oven to 177°c (175 degrees c). 2. in a medium bowl, combine flour, oats, baking powder, brown sugar and butter. 3. press all but 180ml of the crumb mixture into the bottom of a 10 inch round baking pan. 4. spread the fruit pie filling over the top and sprinkle with the remaining crumbs. 5. bake at 177°c (175 degrees c) for 15 minutes. 6. remove from oven and let cool for 10 minutes. 7. in a large bowl, beat the cream cheese and sugar together. 8. add the vanilla and sour cream and beat until smooth. 9. beat in the eggs one at a time. 10. pour batter into the prepared crust. 11. place the pan in a large roasting pan and place in the oven. 12. fill the roasting pan with water to the 1 inch mark. 13. bake at 177°c (175 degrees c) for 55 minutes. 14. remove cake from oven, cool to room temperature and refrigerate overnight.

title: Fudge Brownies
text: fudge brownies ingredients - 230 grams chocolate (half semi sweet and half dark) - 170 grams butter - 200 grams sugar (half white and half brown) - 5ml salt - 3 large eggs - 90 grams all purpose flour - vanilla extract (optional) - 30 grams dutch processed cocoa powder - 5ml espresso powder - 100 grams chocolate chips instructions 1. cut the 230 grams of chocolate into chunks. 2. using a double boiler with simmering water, melt the chocolate along with the butter until it becomes a shiny glossy mixture. 3. set the chocolate and butter mixture aside to cool down for 30 minutes. 4. beat the 200g of sugar with salt and add the eggs incrementally, continuing to beat for 5 minutes. 5. add the chocolate and butter mixture and beat for another minute until everything is combined. 6. fold in the flour, cocoa powder and espresso powder, folding until you no longer see visible dry mixture. 7. fold in the chocolate chips and gently transfer the batter into the rectangular pan. 8. leave the batter in the fridge for at least 24 hours, preferably 48 hours for best results, keeping it in the baking pan. 9. bake the brownies for 25 minutes at 180°c. 10. after 23 minutes, insert a skewer or toothpick in the middle of the brownies to check doneness. 11. the skewer should come out a little wet with some crumbs clinging to it, which normally happens around the 25 minute mark. 12. if the skewer comes out completely clean, the brownies are overbaked. 13. allow the brownies to cool down for at least 1 hour before cutting and serving.

title: Garlic Buns
text: garlic buns ingredients - 1 packet yeast - 120ml warm water - a little sugar - 120ml shortening - 80ml sugar - 2 eggs - 4 rounded cups plain flour - 5ml baking powder - 5ml salt - 1 rounded cup plain flour - parmesan cheese - 180ml softened butter - garlic instructions 1. dissolve 1 packet yeast in 120ml warm water with a little sugar and bloom for 10 minutes. 2. beat together 120ml shortening, 80ml sugar, and 2 eggs until lightly combined. 3. add the bloomed yeast to the beaten mixture. 4. mix in 4 rounded cups of plain flour and proof for 1 hour. 5. add 5ml baking powder, 5ml salt, and 1 rounded cup of flour to bring the total to 1200ml of flour. 6. make herby garlic butter by mixing 180ml softened butter with garlic to taste. 7. proceed as you would for cinnamon rolls, filling with the garlic butter mixture and topping with parmesan cheese.

title: Garlic Sauce
text: garlic sauce ingredients - 30 garlic cloves, peeled - 5ml salt - 45ml fresh lemon juice - 480ml canola oil or other neutral oil instructions 1. place garlic cloves and salt in a food processor and pulse until the garlic is finely minced, scraping down the sides as needed, until you have a smooth paste. 2. with the processor running, very slowly drizzle in a thin stream of canola oil, alternating with small additions of lemon juice, and continue adding oil and lemon juice slowly over 8–10 minutes. 3. the sauce will emulsify and turn white, thick, and creamy; if it looks oily or broken, slow down the oil additions. 4. taste and adjust salt and lemon juice as desired, then serve immediately or refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 weeks.

title: George Washington’s Cherry Bounce
text: george washington’s cherry bounce source: almanac.com ingredients - 10 to 5kg fresh sour or tart cherries, pitted - 960ml brandy - 720ml sugar, plus more as needed - 2 cinnamon sticks, broken into pieces - 2 to 3 cloves - 1 (1/4-inch) piece fresh whole nutmeg instructions 1. note: the recipe lists fresh cherries, but you can also buy jars of preserved cherries, specifically 3 jars (454g, 255g), preferably morello cherries. 2. or if jarred cherries are not available, thawed pie cherries can be substituted.mash cherries to extract as much juice as possible. 3. strain the juice through a large fine-mesh strainer, pressing the fruit with a sturdy spoon. 4. you should have about 1920ml. (keep the mashed cherries; don't throw them out!).  note: if using jarred cherries, drain the fruit and set the juice aside before halving and mashing the cherries. 5. add any pressed juice to the reserved jarred juice.in a 1-gallon glass jar (or glass container) with a lid, combine the juice with the brandy and sugar.  stir to dissolve the sugar. 6. cover and set aside in the refrigerator for 24 hours, occasionally stirring or carefully shaking the jar.bring 480ml of the juice to a simmer over medium heat. 7. taste the sweetened juice and add more sugar if desired. 8. stir in the cinnamon sticks, cloves, and nutmeg.cover and simmer for five minutes; remove from heat and set aside to cool to room temperature. 9. strain, and discard the spices.stir the spiced juice back into the 1-gallon glass jar with the reserved sweetened juice.cover loosely with the lid, and set aside for at least 2 weeks before serving, occasionally shaking the jar with care.serve at room temperature in small cordial or wine glasses. 10. store extra in fridge.

title: Georgian Tarragon Soda
text: georgian tarragon soda ingredients - 180ml sugar - 120ml water - 1 bunch fresh tarragon - 5ml aniseed or fennel seeds - 15ml lemon zest - 1ml baking soda - pinch kosher salt - 60ml fresh lemon juice - seltzer water, to serve instructions 1. combine sugar and water in a small saucepan over medium heat and stir until sugar dissolves. 2. add tarragon, aniseed or fennel seeds, and lemon zest to the pan and simmer for 5 minutes. 3. remove from heat and let steep for 15–20 minutes. 4. strain out solids and let syrup cool completely. 5. stir baking soda, salt, and lemon juice into the cooled syrup. 6. fill a glass with ice, add 2–45ml syrup, and top with seltzer water. 7. stir gently before serving.

title: Ginger Snaps with Brandy Cream
text: ginger snaps with brandy cream ingredients biscuits - 50g butter - 50g caster sugar - 30ml golden syrup (30ml) - 50g plain flour - 5ml ground ginger (5ml) - lard for greasing brandy cream filling - 150ml double cream - 30ml brandy (30ml) instructions 1. preheat the oven to 180°c (gas mark 4). 2. melt butter, caster sugar and syrup in a saucepan over low heat. remove from heat and stir in sieved flour and ginger. allow to cool until the side of the pan can be touched comfortably. 3. thoroughly grease 2 baking trays and the handles of 2 wooden spoons with lard. place heaped teaspoons of the biscuit mixture at least 10cm apart on one tray (max 4 per tray). 4. bake for about 5 minutes until bubbling and evenly golden. remove from the oven and cool for a few minutes until almost set. 5. meanwhile, place 4 more teaspoons of mixture on the second tray and bake as before. 6. quickly lift a cooling biscuit and wrap it around a wooden spoon handle with the bubbled side uppermost. allow to set. repeat with the remaining biscuits. (if biscuits harden before shaping, return to the oven briefly to soften.) 7. continue cooking and shaping until all the mixture is used. 8. whip the double cream and brandy together until thick. fill the cold biscuit rolls with the brandy cream. notes - unfilled ginger snaps can be stored in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks, or frozen for several months.

title: Ginger Bug Soda
text: ginger bug soda ingredients - 10g sugar - 10g ginger - 250ml water instructions 1. feed ginger bug with extra ginger and sugar daily until bubbly.

title: Gluten-Free Vanilla Cake
text: gluten-free vanilla cake source: ricardo cuisine — spring 2016 what gives this almond cake wonderful elasticity is the mixture of egg whites beaten into stiff peaks. plus, it's so moist no one will ever believe it's gluten-free. ingredients cake - 150g gluten-free all-purpose flour - 65g ground almonds - 3ml baking powder - 4 eggs, separated - 1 whole egg - 125ml canola oil - 125ml milk - 10ml vanilla extract - 210g sugar buttercream - 4 egg whites - 5ml vanilla extract - 265g sugar - 60ml water - 340g unsalted butter, cut into cubes, at room temperature instructions cake 1. preheat the oven to 180°c with the rack in the middle position. line a 20cm springform pan with parchment paper. do not butter. 2. in a bowl, combine the gluten-free flour, ground almonds and baking powder. set aside. 3. in another bowl, whisk together the egg yolks, whole egg, oil, milk, vanilla and 55g of the sugar. stir in the dry ingredients and mix until smooth. 4. in a third bowl, beat the egg whites with an electric mixer until soft peaks form. gradually add the remaining sugar and beat until stiff peaks form. 5. fold half the meringue at a time into the batter, stirring vigorously. spread into the prepared pan. 6. bake for about 70 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean. cool completely on a wire rack before unmoulding. buttercream 1. place the egg whites and vanilla in a large bowl. set aside. 2. in a small pot over medium-high heat, bring the sugar and water to a boil. simmer until a candy thermometer reads 116°c. remove from heat. 3. beat the egg whites with an electric mixer on medium speed until frothy. with the machine running, slowly drizzle the hot syrup over the whites (avoiding the beaters). beat until completely cooled and stiff peaks form. 4. add the butter 1–2 cubes at a time, beating until smooth and creamy, scraping the bowl regularly. assembly 1. run a knife between the cake and pan and unmould. cut the cake horizontally into 2 layers. 2. frost one layer with one-third of the buttercream. cover with the second layer. 3. apply a crumb coat (thin layer of buttercream over the entire cake) and refrigerate for 20 minutes. 4. completely frost the cake with the remaining buttercream. notes - no need to be delicate when folding the meringue — it gives the cake its spring, while the baking powder helps it rise. - freezes well.

title: Glyko Karydaki (Green Walnuts Preserve)
text: glyko karydaki (green walnuts preserve) source: kopiaste.org ingredients - 2 kilos (about 50) big, fresh green walnuts - pickling lime and water to cover them (1 heaped tablespoon lime for every litre of water) - 240ml lemon juice, divided (reserve 60ml lemon to add at the end) - 1 kilo sugar - 1200ml water - 1 piece of cinnamon stick - 6-7 cloves - 2-3 fragrant geranium leaves (optional) - 50 blanched and roasted almonds instructions 1. thinly peel the outer skin of the walnuts with a sharp knife or a vegetable peeler, wearing latex gloves to prevent your hands from turning black. 2. cut off the top part where the fruit is attached to the tree, as it is woody. 3. take a skewer or a knitting needle and prick the walnuts horizontally and vertically, then put them in a bowl with water. 4. change the water for six days, once in the morning and once in the evening. 5. on the sixth day, drain the walnuts and put some pickling lime in the bowl with water and mix. 6. put the walnuts in the lime water and let them soak for 3-4 hours to help keep them firm. 7. wash the walnuts thoroughly two or three times, then put them into a large pot with water to cover them. 8. boil for 3 minutes and discard the water. 9. boil again for 2-3 minutes, drain and add cold water. 10. boil for a third time until soft, then drain and add cold water. 11. test if the walnuts are ready by pricking them with a skewer or needle; if it passes through easily, they are ready for the final process. 12. put the blanched almonds in a baking tray and roast them for 15-20 minutes, then set aside to cool and sterilize the jars while the oven is hot. 13. when the walnuts are soft, add the lemon juice. 14. leave them in the water for 1 hour to make them crunchy and shiny. 15. drain them and put them back in the pot, then add the sugar, water and spices. 16. leave them for a while for the sugar to dissolve, then boil the preserve until the temperature reaches 105°c. 17. add the leftover lemon juice and remove from the heat. 18. when it cools, store in clean and sterilized jars. 19. store in a cupboard.

title: Greek Yogurt Sourdough Flatbreads
text: greek yogurt sourdough flatbreads source: ediblecommunities.com ingredients - 2½ cups /300 g all-purpose flour - 15ml /12 g sugar - 5ml /5 g fine sea salt - 2ml baking powder - 120ml /120 g leftover starter - 60ml /60 g greek yogurt - 60ml /60 ml oil - 1 to 30ml /15 to 30 ml warm water - 30ml /28 g unsalted butter, melted instructions 1. whisk the flour, sugar, salt, and baking powder together in a large bowl. add the leftover starter, yogurt, oil, and 15ml (15 ml) of water. mix with your hands until a rough dough forms. the dough should feel soft but not sticky. add more water or flour as needed to get the right texture. cover with a damp kitchen towel and let rest for 1 hour. 2. remove the dough onto a lightly floured work surface. flatten into a rectangle, and then divide into 8 equal pieces, about 80 grams (163g) each. cover with a damp towel. 3. working with one piece at a time, roll the dough into a thin circle about 8 inches (20 cm). the exact shape does not need to be perfect—you’re looking for something slightly smaller than the width of your skillet. note: thinly rolled dough will get you soft, bendable flatbreads; thicker rolled dough will create puffy flatbreads. 4. melt the butter in a small saucepan or in the microwave. warm a large cast-iron skillet over medium-low heat. 5. place the dough into the warm, dry pan and cook for 2 to 3 minutes on one side. when the dough puffs up and has a few bubbles on the surface, brush lightly with some of the melted butter and flip it over. cook for 1 to 2 minutes on the other side. when finished, brush with more butter and transfer to a cutting board. wrap in a towel to keep warm. roll out the next piece of dough and cook the rest of the flatbreads. 6. these sourdough flatbreads are best enjoyed warm. you can also reheat them in a low oven, about 135°c (140°c), in a foil package. for crispy flatbreads, reheat directly on the center oven rack. 7. flatbreads will keep fresh stacked, wrapped, and stored at room temperature for 1 to 2 days. reheat as indicated above for best texture. to freeze, cover the flatbreads in plastic wrap and foil for up to 3 months. 8. tip: after you’ve made this recipe, try spicing up the dough with different seasonings. chopped herbs including rosemary and sage are always nice or try a light dusting of garlic powder and sesame seeds. sometimes i’ll fold in a handful of chopped scallions, which gives the dough a mild onion flavor.

title: Green Walnuts Nocino Liqueur
text: green walnuts nocino liqueur ingredients - 600 grams green walnuts, washed and quartered - 5 nutmeg pods - 7 cloves - 4 grams cinnamon sticks (2 types) - 1 star anise - 5 cardamom pods - 3 juniper berries - 1 lemon rind - 400 milliliters 96% alcohol - 920 milliliters water - 30ml angostura bitters - 240ml plus 30ml demerara sugar - 60ml plus 30ml water instructions 1. pick green walnuts near the beginning of summer between june 6 and june 24. 2. wash and quarter the green walnuts. 3. combine the quartered green walnuts, nutmeg, cloves, cinnamon sticks, star anise, cardamom pods, juniper berries, and lemon rind in a container. 4. add 400 milliliters of 96% alcohol to the walnut and spice mixture. 5. steep the mixture for 6 months. 6. filter the steeped mixture after 6 months. 7. make a rich demerara syrup by cooking 240ml plus 30ml demerara sugar with 60ml plus 30ml water. 8. add 920 milliliters of water and 30ml of angostura bitters to the filtered walnut liqueur. 9. add the cooled demerara syrup to the liqueur and stir to combine.

title: Grilled Lamb & Fruit Salad with Feta and Mint-Lime Dressing
text: grilled lamb & fruit salad with feta and mint-lime dressing ingredients - 480ml romaine lettuce, chopped - 240ml cherry tomatoes, halved - 240ml cantaloupe, cubed - 240ml mango, cubed - 1 banana, cubed - 200 g lamb chops, chopped - salt and pepper to taste - touch of cinnamon for lamb - 100 g feta cheese, crumbled - 45ml extra virgin olive oil - 15ml fresh lime juice - 5ml honey - 5ml dijon mustard - 15ml fresh mint, finely chopped - pinch of chili flakes or aleppo pepper - 1ml cinnamon instructions 1. grill lamb chops with a sprinkle of cinnamon, salt, and pepper until cooked to your liking. 2. let the lamb rest for a few minutes, then chop into bite-size pieces. 3. in a small jar or bowl, whisk together olive oil, lime juice, honey, mustard, mint, chili flakes, salt, and black pepper until smooth and emulsified. 4. in a large bowl or platter, arrange the romaine, cherry tomatoes, cantaloupe, mango, and banana. 5. top with the grilled lamb and sprinkle over the feta cheese. 6. drizzle with the mint-lime dressing just before serving and toss gently if desired, or serve with dressing on the side.

title: Larabars Recipe
text: larabars recipe source: leitesculinaria.com ingredients - mild olive oil, vegetable, or coconut oil for the pan - 240ml packed dried cherries - 60ml packed pitted soft whole dates - 240ml warm water - 240ml raw almonds - 1ml ground cinnamon - 1ml fine sea salt (optional) instructions 1. rip off a large piece of plastic wrap, press it into a 9-by-5-inch loaf pan, and slick the plastic wrap with a little oil. 2. combine the cherries, dates, and warm water in a small bowl and let stand for 5 to 10 minutes until the fruit is soft, then drain the fruit and pat it dry with paper towels. 3. place the almonds in a food processor and process until finely chopped but not pastelike. 4. add the drained fruit, cinnamon, and salt to the food processor and pulse until the fruit is finely chopped and the larabar mixture begins to stick together and clump, which may take up to 2 minutes. 5. transfer the larabar mixture to the prepared loaf pan and use a large piece of parchment paper, wax paper, or plastic wrap slicked with oil to spread and flatten the mixture evenly in the pan. 6. refrigerate for 30 minutes. 7. using the paper or plastic lining the pan, lift the bar mixture from the pan and transfer it to a cutting board, then discard the paper and cut the rectangle into 6 bars. 8. tightly wrap each bar in plastic wrap and store at room temperature for up to 3 days, in the refrigerator for up to 3 weeks, or in the freezer for up to 3 months.

title: Halva
text: halva ingredients - 480ml granulated sugar - ½ vanilla bean, scraped - zest of 1 lemon - 360ml tahini - pinch kosher salt instructions 1. line an 8 x 8 inch baking pan with parchment paper. 2. combine sugar, vanilla seeds and lemon zest with 120ml water in a saucepan over medium heat, stirring to dissolve sugar. 3. allow mixture to simmer into a syrup, without stirring, until temperature registers 245 degrees on candy thermometer. 4. place tahini and salt in bowl of a stand mixer fitted with paddle and beat on medium speed. 5. carefully stream syrup into tahini with mixer running and mix until syrup is incorporated and mixture begins to pull away from sides of bowl, about 30 seconds to 1 minute. 6. working quickly with a heatproof spatula, transfer mixture to the prepared pan. 7. place another piece of parchment on top and use your hands on top of the parchment to smooth out halvah. 8. cool completely to room temperature and cut into squares. 9. store at room temperature, well wrapped in plastic, for a week.

title: Healthy Nutella –
text: healthy nutella – \#1 yield: 480ml ingredients healthy nutella ·480ml raw hazelnuts (240g) ·22ml pure vanilla extract ·60ml cocoa powder ·60ml \+ 30ml pure maple syrup, xylitol, or unrefined sugar ·pinch stevia, or 15ml additional sugar ·1ml \+ 1ml salt ·optional: 10ml oil for extra smoothness ·120ml milk of choice instructions nutella recipe: roast hazelnuts for 6\-8 minutes at 204°c. rub them together in a paper towel to get the skins off. (it’s ok if a few stubborn skins won’t come off.) in a vita\-mix or food processor, blend the nuts until they’ve turned to butter, then add all other ingredients and blend a long time until it’s smooth like nutella! \#2 yield: 600ml ingredients ·720ml (415 g) raw or roasted unsalted hazelnuts ·160ml (96 g) dairy\-free dark chocolate (chopped // see notes for cacao version) ·5ml pure vanilla extract ·2ml sea salt instructions 1\.preheat oven to 177°c (176 c) and add hazelnuts to a baking sheet in a single layer. if raw, roast for a total of 12\-15 minutes. if already roasted, roast for 8\-10 minutes just to warm the natural oils and loosen the skins. this will make it easier to blend into butter. 2\.remove from oven and let cool slightly. then transfer to a large kitchen towel and use your hands to roll the nuts around and remove most of the skins (see photo). you want to get as much as possible off because it yields a creamier nutella. but it doesn’t have to be perfect! 3\.leaving excess skin behind, add hazelnuts to a food processor or high\-speed blender. blend on low until a butter is formed \- about 8\-10 minutes total \- scraping down sides as needed. 4\.in the meantime, heat the chocolate over a double boiler or in the microwave in 30 second increments. set aside. 5\.once the hazelnut butter is creamy and smooth, add the melted chocolate, sea salt, and vanilla. blend/puree again until well incorporated. taste and adjust seasonings as needed, adding more salt or vanilla if desired. 6\.if your nutella isn’t sweet enough, add stevia to taste, or 1\-30ml maple syrup or agave (amount as original recipe is written). note: just know the more liquid sweetener you add the firmer/stiffer the nutella will get, so add sparingly. 7\.transfer to a clean jar and store at room temperature for everyday use for 2\-3 weeks or more. \#3 ingredients 480ml hazelnuts 80ml or to taste sugarhttps://www.amazon.com/organic-anthonys-certified-gluten-free-non-gmo/dp/b0182yku1y/ref=aslisstl?ie=utf8&qid=1496884439&sr=8-2&keywords=organic+cane+sugar&linkcode=ll1&tag=wellnessmama-20&linkid=ced8cf5c85fcf1acc6a49a6ff8376276 or other preferred sweetener 60ml cocoa powder 15ml coconut oil 5ml vanilla 1ml salt instructions 1\.preheat oven to 191°c. spread the hazelnuts on a baking sheet and roast for 12 to 15 minutes, until fragrant. 2. carefully put the hot hazelnuts in a mason jar with the lid on and shake. the papery skins will fall right off. remove the nuts that are now skinless and put them in a food processor or a high\-powered blender, then re\-shake the jar until the rest of the skins come off as well. 3. grind the hazelnuts for about 5 minutes until they turn into a creamy hazelnut butter. 4. add the sugar or other sweetener, cocoa powder, coconut oil, vanilla, and salt. blend for another minute until all the ingredients are combined smooth. 5. transfer to a pint mason jar. store in the refrigerator for several weeks. \#4 yield 240ml ingredients 120ml semisweet chocolate chips (85g) 180ml skinned hazelnuts, toasted (about 113g) 160ml sweetened condensed milk, such as eagle brand 15ml honey 1ml kosher salt \#5 ·480ml (heaping) hazelnuts, preferably skinned (about 284g) ·60ml sugar ·454g semisweet or bittersweet chocolate, coarsely chopped ·120ml (1 stick) unsalted butter, cut into 1\-inch pieces, room temperature ·240ml heavy cream ·4ml kosher salt \#6 yield: 1 c course: dessert, sauce cuisine: italian servings: 8 (30ml) servings author: sarah \| curious cuisiniere ·227g hazelnuts ·¼ c cocoa powder ·113g semi\-sweet chocolate, melted ·¼ c powdered sugar ·22ml vegetable oil or light tasting olive oil ·2ml pure vanilla extract ·1ml salt instructions preheat your oven to 177°c. place the hazelnuts in a single layer on a baking tray and roast for 8\-12 minutes, until fragrant. remove the nuts from the oven and let them cool slightly. dump the warm nuts into a towel and use the towel to rub them together so that the skins come off. (if not all the skins come off, that is ok and won’t affect the flavor of your nutella too much.) place the de\-skinned, roasted hazelnuts into the bowl of your food processor. process until the nuts are fine. then continue processing until they form a paste. add the remaining ingredients to the bowl of your food processor and process until smooth. add a little more oil if you like your spread a bit thinner. (the spread will thicken slightly as it cools.) store your homemade nutella in a sealed container at room temp for 2 weeks \- 1 month.

title: Himmas Kassa
text: himmas kassa ingredients - 240ml boiled chickpeas - 30ml tahini - 30ml water - 30ml wine vinegar - 60ml finely ground walnut - 30ml lemon juice - 5ml wine vinegar - 120ml chopped parsley - 60ml chopped mint - 45ml olive oil - 1ml caraway - 1ml coriander - 1ml black pepper - 1ml ginger - 1ml cinnamon - 2ml salt - olive oil for garnish - olives for garnish - chopped pistachios for garnish - flatbread for serving instructions 1. in a mixing bowl, mash the boiled chickpeas until they form a coarse paste. 2. stir in the tahini mixture and the walnut mixture until combined. 3. fold in the parsley, mint, olive oil, and spices, then taste and adjust salt as needed. 4. transfer to a shallow serving dish and garnish with olive oil, olives, and pistachios. 5. serve with flatbread.

title: Baileys Irish Cream
text: baileys irish cream source: averiecooks.com ingredients - 400ml irish whiskey (i used jameson) - one 14-ounce can sweetened condensed milk - 240ml half-and-half or heavy cream (i used half-and-half) - 30ml chocolate syrup (i used hershey’s) - 10ml vanilla extract - 5ml instant coffee granules or instant espresso (make sure it’s instant so it dissolves) instructions 1. combine all ingredients in the canister of a blender and blend on high speed until smooth, 30 to 60 seconds. 2. transfer mixture to a glass bottle or airtight container with a tight-fitting lid and store in the refrigerator for up to 2 months (i have read anywhere between 1 to 2 months; the alcohol helps preserve it, but always use the sniff test and common sense). 3. shake well before using.

title: Beef Jerky
text: beef jerky source: allrecipes.com ingredients - 180ml worcestershire sauce - 180ml soy sauce - 15ml smoked paprika - 15ml honey - 10ml freshly ground black pepper - 5ml red pepper flakes - 5ml garlic powder - 5ml onion powder - 907g beef top round, thinly sliced instructions 1. whisk together worcestershire sauce, soy sauce, smoked paprika, honey, black pepper, red pepper flakes, garlic powder, and onion powder in a large bowl. 2. add beef to the bowl and mix until completely coated with marinade. 3. cover the bowl with plastic wrap and marinate in the refrigerator for 3 hours to overnight. 4. preheat the oven to 79°c (80 degrees c). 5. line a baking sheet with aluminum foil and place a wire rack on top. 6. transfer beef to paper towels to dry and discard the marinade. 7. arrange beef slices in a single layer on the prepared wire rack on the baking sheet. 8. bake in the preheated oven until dry and leathery, 3 to 4 hours. 9. cut jerky with scissors into bite-sized pieces.

title: Cocktail Bitters
text: cocktail bitters source: the spruce eats ingredients - 240ml 151-proof grain alcohol - 15ml quassia bark - 5ml cardamom seeds - 5ml coriander seeds - 5ml dried orange peel, minced - 2ml caraway seeds - 2ml dried gentian root - 480ml water - 80ml sugar instructions 1. in a 1-pint jar or larger, combine 240ml 151-proof grain alcohol, 15ml quassia bark, 5ml cardamom seeds, 5ml coriander seeds, 5ml minced dried orange peel, 2ml caraway seeds, and 2ml dried gentian root. 2. seal the jar, shake, and let the mixture stand in a cool, dark place for 14 days, shaking vigorously once a day. 3. strain the infused alcohol into a clean jar through cheesecloth to remove the botanicals, gathering the cloth into a ball and squeezing to release as much liquid as possible. 4. use a muddler or mortar and pestle to break up the strained botanicals as much as possible. 5. in a medium nonreactive saucepan, add 480ml water and the botanicals, then bring to a boil. 6. cover and lower the heat, allowing the mixture to simmer for 5 to 7 minutes. 7. pour the mixture without straining into a 1-pint jar or larger, cover, and allow it to sit for 5 days in a cool and dry place, shaking vigorously once a day. 8. strain the infused water through cheesecloth and discard the botanicals. 9. measure the infused alcohol and combine it with an equal amount of aromatic water in a 1-pint jar or larger. 10. in a small saucepan over medium-high heat, add 80ml sugar, stir constantly, and allow the sugar to caramelize until dark brown, about 3 to 4 minutes. 11. add the caramelized sugar to the alcohol and water mixture and let it dissolve within a few minutes. 12. shake the bitters, then strain through cheesecloth to remove any sediment. 13. pour into a bitters bottle or small decanter with a tight-sealing lid and store for up to 12 months unrefrigerated in a cool place.

title: Marshmallow Fluff
text: marshmallow fluff source: livforcake.com ingredients - 80ml water - 180ml granulated sugar - 180ml corn syrup (or honey) - 3 large egg whites (room temperature) - 2ml cream of tartar - 5ml vanilla extract instructions 1. place water, sugar, and corn syrup in a medium saucepan. stir to combine. 2. insert a candy thermometer into the pot and heat over medium-high. do not stir from this point on as crystals will form. 3. wipe down your mixer bowl, whisk, etc with lemon juice or vinegar to ensure they are completely grease free. 4. place egg whites and cream of tartar in the bowl of a stand mixer. 5. when the sugar syrup reaches about 225°f, start whipping the egg whites to soft peaks. approx 3-4mins. 6. when the whites are ready, the sugar syrup should be at 240°f. remove from the heat, turn mixer to medium and very slowly and carefully pour the sugar syrup into the whites in a thin, steady stream. 7. once all of the syrup is in, set mixer to medium/high and continue whipping. the whites will deflate at first, but they will thicken and fluff up. 8. continue to whip for 7-8 minutes, or until the mixture is thick and fluffy. 9. add in vanilla and whip until the fluff has cooled completely. 10. use right away as a frosting or filling or transfer into an airtight container and store for up to 2 weeks at room temperature.

title: מוצרלה ביתית
