text: מוצרלה ביתית source: frenchguycooking.wixsite.com ingredients אין רשימת מרכיבים מפורשת בטקסט המקורי. instructions 1. הוסף אנזים בטמפרטורה של 32 מעלות. 2. המתן 45 דקות לאחר הוספת האנזים. 3. בשל את הקרדס בטמפרטורה של 43 מעלות. 4. התח את הגבינה במים רותחים בטמפרטורה של 85 מעלות. 5. בדוק את יחס הרנט לחלב שלך בבית ולא לפי המתכון כדי להימנע מיתרת אנזים שמפרקת את הקרדס.

title: Mozzarella
text: mozzarella ingredients - 4l fresh whole milk - 8ml citric acid - 5ml cheese salt - 2ml rennet instructions 1. measure out 250ml of warm water and stir in the citric acid until dissolved. 2. measure out 60ml of warm water in a separate bowl and stir in the rennet until dissolved. 3. pour the milk into a saucepan and stir in the citric acid solution. 4. put the saucepan over medium-high heat, stirring gently until it reaches 32°c. 5. remove from the heat and stir in the rennet solution for around 30 seconds. 6. cover the saucepan and leave to rest for 5-10 minutes until the milk sets and feels like soft silken tofu. 7. cut the set milk in a grid formation in the pan to create uniformly sized cheese curds. 8. put the pan back onto medium-high heat and stir gently until the curds reach 41°c, then remove from heat and continue stirring until combined. 9. use a slotted spoon to remove the curds and place them into a microwave-safe bowl. 10. microwave the curds for 1 minute, then drain away any additional whey and fold the curds over on themselves a few times. 11. continue microwaving and folding in 30-second bursts until the curds reach 57°c. 12. sprinkle the cheese salt over the curds and stretch and fold them repeatedly until the mozzarella becomes firm and glossy on top. 13. store in a container with salt and whey to keep fresh for up to a week if desired.

title: Oatmeal Cream Pies
text: oatmeal cream pies source: mybakingaddiction.com ingredients - 240ml unsalted butter (softened) - 180ml firmly packed light brown sugar - 120ml granulated sugar - 2 large eggs - 5ml pure vanilla extract - 360ml all-purpose flour - 5ml baking soda - 5ml ground cinnamon - 2ml salt - 720ml quick or old fashioned oats - 180ml unsalted butter (softened) - 600ml confectioners' sugar (sifted) - 5ml pure vanilla extract - 15ml milk or half and half instructions 1. preheat oven to 177°c. line cookie sheets with parchment paper. 2. in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment, or in a large bowl with an electric mixer, cream together butter and sugars until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes. add in eggs and vanilla and mix until combined. 3. in a medium bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda, cinnamon and salt. slowly add the flour mixture to the wet ingredients, mixing until just combined. add in oats and mix until incorporated. 4. to make large cookies, use a large cookie scoop (about 45ml) to drop dough onto prepared cookie sheets. bake in preheated oven for 13-15 minutes or until golden brown. to make small cookies, use a medium cookie scoop (about 22ml) of dough per cookie and bake for 10-12 minutes. 5. allow cookies to sit on cookie sheets for about 5 minutes before removing them to a wire rack to cool completely. once cookies have cooled completely, prepare the cream filling. 6. in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment or in a large bowl with an electric hand mixer, beat butter on medium-high speed for about 5 minutes. this process will lighten the color of the butter and ensure you buttercream in extra fluffy. 7. turn the speed down to low and gradually add in the powdered sugar. continue mixing on low speed until the powdered sugar is completely incorporated. add in vanilla extract and milk and mix until combined. 8. turn mixer back up to medium-high speed and beat the mixture for an additional 3-5 minutes. if needed, add in a little more milk or half-and-half 5ml at a time until you reach the consistency you desire. 9. to assemble the cookies, pipe or spread the cream filling on the flat side of half of the cookies and put the remaining cookies on top.

title: Phyllo (or Filo) Dough
text: phyllo (or filo) dough source: allrecipes.com ingredients - 480ml all-purpose flour, plus more for kneading - 25ml olive oil - 2ml fine salt - 180ml warm water (43°c / 43 degrees c) - 10ml white wine vinegar - 120ml cornstarch - 30ml all-purpose flour instructions 1. place 480ml flour in a mixing bowl and make a well in the center, then drizzle in olive oil and add salt. 2. pour in warm water and white wine vinegar, then mix until dough just comes together and pulls away from the sides of the bowl, about 1 to 2 minutes. 3. transfer dough to a lightly floured work surface and knead until smooth, using just enough flour to keep it from sticking, for 2 or 3 minutes, then continue to knead until dough is supple and elastic for about 5 more minutes. 4. wrap dough ball in plastic wrap and let rest at room temperature for 1 to 2 hours. 5. use a kitchen scale to divide dough into twenty 25-gram portions and roll each portion into a ball, then place on a plate and cover with plastic wrap to prevent drying out while working in batches of 5. 6. mix cornstarch and 30ml flour together in a bowl, then dust a work surface and the first dough ball with the cornstarch mixture. 7. flatten and roll out into a circle about 5 inches in diameter, dust again with cornstarch mixture, then roll out 4 more dough balls to about the same diameter and stack them on the first one, dusting each layer with more cornstarch mixture to keep them from sticking together. 8. roll out the 5-circle stack to a larger circle about double in size, turning as you go to maintain a round shape, then separate each layer and lay out the circles, reapplying more cornstarch mixture where needed and restacking them. 9. roll again until the 5-layer stack is paper-thin, about 10 to 12 inches in diameter, then place on a sheet of parchment paper, top with another piece of parchment, gently roll up the dough, wrap it in plastic wrap, and refrigerate. 10. repeat with the remaining 15 balls of dough in batches of 5.

title: Pierogi
text: pierogi ingredients - 480ml (241g) king arthur unbleached all-purpose flour - 2ml salt - 1 large egg - 120ml (113g) sour cream - 60ml (57g) butter, room temperature - 240ml (227g) warm mashed potatoes - 240ml (113g) sharp cheddar cheese, shredded - 60ml (57g) butter, cold - 2 large (156g) shallots, diced, or one medium (156g) onion, sliced instructions 1. mix together the flour and salt. 2. add the egg to the flour and combine. 3. work in the sour cream and soft butter until the dough comes together in a slightly rough, slightly sticky ball. 4. using just your fingertips, knead and fold the dough without adding additional flour until the dough becomes less sticky but still quite moist. 5. wrap the dough well in plastic wrap and refrigerate for 30 to 60 minutes, or up to 48 hours. 6. combine the warm mashed potato and cheese, stirring and mashing until the cheese is melted and the filling is cool to the touch, then taste and adjust the seasonings with salt and pepper. 7. roll half the dough 1/8" thick and use a 2" round cutter to cut circles of dough, then repeat with the other half of the dough. 8. place 8ml of filling on each round of dough. 9. gently fold the dough over, forming a pocket around the filling, then pinch the edges of the pierogi to seal and seal again with the tines of a fork. 10. cook the pierogi in a large stockpot of boiling salted water, cooking about 10 pierogi at a time so they have room to float without sticking, until they float. 11. sauté the shallots or onion in the butter in a large skillet until the onion begins to brown. 12. add the drained pierogi and cook until browned and crisped. 13. serve hot with additional sour cream, applesauce, or other condiments.

title: Pomegranate Liqueur
text: pomegranate liqueur source: instructables ingredients - roughly six pomegranates, depending on their size - peel of 1 lemon (meyer preferred) - 1 cinnamon stick - 720ml vodka - 360ml white sugar - 180ml water instructions 1. cut the pomegranate in half vertically and fill a large bowl with water. 2. turn the pomegranate half seed-side down and push on the center with your thumbs to turn the half inside-out, working under water to minimize juice spraying. 3. allow the membrane, flesh, and pith to float to the top while seeds fall to the bottom, then rinse and agitate to free any extra membrane. 4. place a fine mesh metal strainer in a bowl and press pomegranate seed pods down against the strainer with a spoon to crush the pods and extract the juice, reserving both seeds and juice. 5. using a vegetable peeler or paring knife, carefully peel the lemon while avoiding the white pith to preserve the oils in the peel. 6. sterilize a large glass jar in boiling water or a dishwasher rinse cycle, then add the pomegranate juice and seeds, lemon peel, and cinnamon stick. 7. pour in the vodka, wipe the rim clean, and seal the jar. 8. store the jar in a cool, dark location and agitate daily with a good swirl for two to three weeks. 9. carefully strain the liquid through several layers of moistened cheesecloth and gently wring to extract all liquid, then discard the rind, pulp, and spices. 10. return the strained liquid to the jar. 11. gently heat the sugar and water on medium-low to create a simple syrup, stirring only until the sugar is dissolved, then allow it to cool completely. 12. add the cooled simple syrup to the jar with the strained liquid. 13. store the jar in a cool, dark, and dry location, agitating every few days, and allow to age for at least three more weeks, ideally four to five weeks. 14. sterilize glass bottles, a funnel, and any transfer utensils in a boiling water bath or dishwasher sterilizing rinse. 15. carefully scoop the liqueur into a glass measuring cup, avoiding any sediment at the bottom. 16. pour the liqueur into sterilized bottles through a funnel, wipe the lids, and seal quickly. 17. serve chilled straight up, mix one-to-one with vodka for a pomegranate martini, or add an ounce to champagne for a festive drink.

title: Smoked Pastrami (Close to Katz's)
text: smoked pastrami (close to katz's) source: amazingribs.com ingredients - beef brisket (preferably the flat cut) - kosher salt (5-6% of brine weight) - sugar (2-3% of brine weight) - pink curing salt (0.25% of total weight) - whole allspice berries (15ml) - whole mustard seeds, brown or yellow (15ml) - coriander seeds (15ml) - red pepper flakes (15ml) - whole black peppercorns (15ml) - whole cloves (10ml) - whole cardamom pods (9 pods) - bay leaves (6 large, crumbled) - ground ginger (10ml) - cinnamon stick (1/2 stick) - juniper berries (9 berries) - water (1 gallon) - fresh coarsely ground black pepper (15ml per 1/2 kg meat) - coriander powder (15ml per 1/2 kg meat) - brown sugar (15ml per 1/2 kg meat) - paprika (15ml per 1/2 kg meat) - garlic powder (10ml per 1/2 kg meat) - onion powder (10ml per 1/2 kg meat) - yellow mustard seeds (2ml per 1/2 kg meat) - mustard powder (2ml per 1/2 kg meat) - apple juice or water for wrapping (optional) instructions 1. toast and crush the allspice berries, mustard seeds, coriander seeds, red pepper flakes, peppercorns, cloves, and cardamom pods in a small frying pan on medium heat until fragrant, being careful not to burn them. 2. remove the toasted spices from heat and place in a small bowl, then use a mortar and pestle to crush them slightly. 3. add the crumbled bay leaves and ground ginger to the crushed spices and mix well. 4. add about 45ml of the spice mix, the cinnamon stick, kosher salt, pink salt, and brown sugar to a gallon of water in a large pot. 5. bring the brine to a boil, then remove from heat and let cool to room temperature before refrigerating until well chilled. 6. place the brisket in a large container and cover with the chilled brine, weighing it down with a plate if needed to keep it submerged. 7. refrigerate the brined brisket for the curing period (typically 5-7 days for corned beef, longer for pastrami). 8. desalinate the brisket by covering it with cold water in the fridge for at least 8 hours, changing the water at least once. 9. rinse the desalted brisket and rub it generously with the spice rub mixture, then refrigerate for at least overnight, preferably one to two days. 10. smoke the brisket at 120°c until the internal temperature reaches 71°c and the crust is brown. 11. wrap the smoked brisket tightly in foil, add a bit of apple juice or water, and roast until the internal temperature reaches 95°c. 12. let the brisket rest for at least 30 minutes before slicing. 13. alternatively, after smoking, transfer the brisket to a steamer and steam for 2-3 hours until tender. 14. slice the brisket by hand into thin slices about 1/8 inch (3.2 mm) thick, cutting perpendicular to the grain.

title: Sourdough Croissants
text: sourdough croissants source: aberlehome.com ingredients - 115g active sourdough starter, 100% hydration - 36g sugar - 10g kosher salt - 29g (30ml) unsalted butter, melted - 240g whole milk, cold - 423g unbleached all-purpose flour - 227g (240ml) 82% fat (european-style) unsalted butter, cold - 8g (15ml) unbleached all-purpose flour - 1 egg - 15g (15ml) whole milk instructions 1. feed starter several hours before mixing dough and allow it to peak 2. sourdough croissant dough: 3. 1 4. day 1: mix the dough ingredients until a shaggy dough forms 5. remove dough to a clean countertop and knead for a few minutes until a smooth dough forms 6. form dough into a ball. 7. 2 8. transfer dough to a large bowl and cover 9. leave in a warm place (75°-26°c) to ferment for 4 hours, or until it has nearly doubled in size. 10. 3 11. cover and refrigerate dough overnight 12. butter block: 13. 1 14. day 2: place cold butter on a sheet of parchment paper and sprinkle with the flour 15. fold the ends of the parchment loosely to cover the butter and begin pounding the butter with a rolling pin until it begins to flatten. (update: i find it's easier to measure and fold the parchment before placing the butter inside.) 16. 2 17. use a measuring tape to form the parchment paper into a 6x8-inch rectangle pouch over the butter 18. flip the pouch over to keep the edges closed 19. then use a rolling pin and your fingers to evenly press the butter into the pouch to make a butter block 20. chill if butter has begun to melt and looks greasy on the edges 21. if butter is still cold but very pliable when you bend the package, it is ready for the next step 22. lock in butter block: 23. 1 24. remove dough from fridge and turn it out onto a lightly floured surface 25. use your hands to begin to shape the dough into a rectangle and pinch the corners to shape them 26. roll the dough into a 13x9-inch rectangle. 27. 2 28. unwrap butter block and place in the center of your dough with a short side facing you. 29. 3 30. bring the ends of the dough over the butter so they meet in the middle of the butter block, encasing the butter 31. press every seam to seal so the butter does not escape during rolling 32. brush away any loose flour with a pastry brush 33. first lamination fold (book fold): 34. 1 35. turn the dough so the center seam is parallel to you 36. use your rolling pin to gently pound the dough to lengthen it 37. then roll to a 24x10-inch rectangle 38. try to keep the edges and corners straight, and dust underneath with more flour as needed to prevent sticking. 39. 2 40. fold the short ends of the rectangle inward to meet in the center (update: meeting the edges together off-center is actually better) 41. then fold the new ends together like you're closing a book 42. brush away any loose flour as you go. 43. 3 44. wrap book in plastic wrap and refrigerate for 20 minutes 45. second lamination fold (tri-fold or letter fold): 46. 1 47. place dough on your lightly floured surface again, this time with the fold facing you 48. pound and roll to a 24x10-inch rectangle again. 49. 2 50. fold the short ends of the rectangle in thirds this time, as if you are folding a letter 51. brush away loose flour as you go. 52. 3 53. wrap in plastic again, and chill for 1 hour 54. shaping and baking croissants: 55. 1 56. remove dough from fridge and allow it to rest for 20 minutes or until the butter is pliable again 57. with the folded side facing you, roll to a 18x11.5-inch rectangle 58. use a pizza cutter to trim the edges. 59. 2 60. cut the rectangle into 5 equal rectangles, measuring for accuracy 61. cut each rectangle in half on the diagonal to form 10 triangles. 62. 3 63. set a triangle in front of you with the bottom two corners facing you 64. brush away loose flour 65. gently stretch these corners wider with your fingers and then roll the croissant tight enough that there won't be gaps in the finished pastry. (update: i now make a small cut in the center of the base of each triangle instead of stretching the edges, then roll.) lightly press the tip of the triangle into the croissant to help it adhere to the underneath side 66. repeat for remaining triangles. 67. 4 68. arrange the croissants on 2 parchment-lined half sheet pans, 5 to each pan 69. cover with plastic wrap (not too tightly) and leave at room temperature to proof for several hours (do not exceed 24°c during proofing), or until croissants have doubled in size and wobble like marshmallows when you bump the pan 70. you should begin to see some separation in the layers when proofing is finished 71. meanwhile, preheat your oven to 204°c. 72. 5 73. beat your egg and milk together to make an egg wash 74. use a pastry brush to brush egg wash over each proofed croissant, avoiding the laminated edges. 75. 6 76. bake one pan at a time on the center rack for 15-20 minutes, or until deeply golden brown. (hold second pan in the fridge until you're ready to egg wash and bake if done proofing.) 77. 7 78. place croissants on a cooling rack, and serve or store once they've cooled completely.

title: Honey-Roasted Root Vegetable Salad
text: honey-roasted root vegetable salad source: foodandwine.com ingredients - 454g medium beets, with 1 inch of the stem attached - 454g carrots, peeled and cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces - 454g parsnips, peeled and cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces - 454g turnips, peeled and cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces - 45ml vegetable oil - 3 small white onions (about 340g), cut into 2-inch wedges - salt and freshly ground pepper - 45ml honey, warmed - 15ml chopped sage leaves - 113g fresh goat cheese, at room temperature - 60ml minced fresh herbs, such as chives, tarragon and flat-leaf parsley - 30ml extra-virgin olive oil - 60ml extra-virgin olive oil - 30ml sherry vinegar - 1 large garlic clove, minced - 15ml minced herbs, such as chives, tarragon and flat-leaf parsley - salt and freshly ground pepper - 960ml packed arugula leaves (from two 4-ounce bunches) instructions 1. preheat the oven to 400°. tightly wrap the beets in a double layer of aluminum foil and roast them on the bottom shelf of the oven for 1 1/2 hours, or until they are tender when pierced with the tip of a knife. when the beets are cool enough to handle, peel and cut them into 1-inch pieces. 2. meanwhile, divide the carrots, parsnips and turnips between 2 large rimmed baking sheets. toss the vegetables in each pan with 15ml of the vegetable oil. arrange the onion wedges on the baking sheets, keeping them intact. brush the onion wedges all over with the remaining 15ml of vegetable oil. generously season the vegetables with salt and pepper. roast the vegetables for 40 minutes. brush the vegetables with the warm honey and sprinkle with the sage. continue to roast the vegetables for 25 minutes longer, or until they are tender and glazed. loosen the vegetables with a spatula and let them cool to room temperature in the pans. 3. in a small bowl, mix the goat cheese with the herbs and olive oil and season with salt and pepper. 4. in a small bowl, combine the olive oil with the vinegar, garlic and herbs; season with salt and pepper. in a large bowl, toss the arugula with 15ml of the vinaigrette and arrange on plates. add the roasted vegetables to the bowl and toss with the remaining vinaigrette. top the arugula with the vegetables, dot each plate with small spoonfuls of the herbed goat cheese and serve.

title: Honey Tahini Cookies
text: honey tahini cookies ingredients - 120ml sesame seeds - 1½ cups almond flour - 2ml baking soda - 1ml sea salt - 80ml honey - 80ml tahini - 5ml vanilla extract instructions 1. preheat oven to 177°c and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. 2. spread sesame seeds on a shallow plate. 3. in a bowl, whisk together almond flour, baking soda, and sea salt. 4. stir in honey, tahini, and vanilla until a dough forms. 5. roll dough into balls about 15ml each. 6. roll each ball in the sesame seeds to coat, then place on the prepared baking sheet. 7. flatten each ball slightly with your palm. 8. bake for 8 minutes, until golden around the edges. 9. cool on the pan for 5 minutes before transferring.

title: Bake Sourdough Bread Every Day in Less Than 30 Minutes
text: bake sourdough bread every day in less than 30 minutes source: culinaryexploration.eu ingredients - 55g water (for starter feeding) - 55g strong white bread flour (for starter feeding) - 388g strong white bread flour - 257g water - 8g salt - 98g starter (100% hydrated) - rice flour for dusting instructions 1. feed your sourdough starter at 21:00 with 55g room temperature water and 55g strong white bread flour, using the scrapings left in the jar. 2. the next morning, add 257g water to a bowl and roughly dissolve the 98g starter into it. 3. add 8g salt and stir, then add 388g strong white bread flour and mix with a spoon until all dry flour is incorporated into a rough dough. 4. rest the dough covered in the bowl for 10 minutes, then knead for 1 minute. 5. rest the dough covered at room temperature for 30 minutes. 6. turn the dough out and perform one set of stretch and folds or lamination, then shape into a ball and leave covered at room temperature to bulk ferment for about 6 hours until expanded by 75%. 7. turn the dough out and give it a quick pre-shape, then rest uncovered for 10 minutes. 8. lightly dust the banneton and top of the dough with rice flour, shape the dough simply into a cylinder, and place seam-side up in the banneton. 9. leave the dough out at room temperature uncovered for about 1.5 hours until it feels springy and expanding. 10. pop the dough into the fridge uncovered to ferment overnight. 11. the next morning, preheat your oven to 220°c (221°c) with a baking stone, then score the dough and bake covered with a large pot for the first 20 minutes. 12. uncover and bake for a final 30 minutes without steam until the bread is golden brown.

title: How To Make Butter
text: how to make butter source: thekitchn.com ingredients - 1 pint (480ml) heavy cream, preferably organic and not ultra-pasteurized - 30ml plain yogurt (optional) - scant 1ml of salt (optional) - 2 or 720ml of ice water, for washing the butter instructions 1. culture the cream (optional): the day before you would like to make your butter, pour the cream into a bowl (i like to use the bowl of my stand mixer) and add the yogurt. whisk briefly to combine and cover the bowl with a clean kitchen towel. set in a slightly warm place (about 21°c - 24°c) to culture. check after 8 to 12 hours. the cream is ready when it has thickened slightly and is a little foamy. it will smell slightly sour and tangy. this can possibly take an additional 12 to 24 (see recipe notes). once it has cultured, place it in the refrigerator for about 1 hour to chill.→ if you did not culture your butter, let it warm on the counter for about an hour (to about 16°c) before churning. 2. prepare the sieve and mixer: place a sturdy sieve over a bowl and line with a few layers of cheesecloth or a clean napkin. you can use a stand mixer, a hand mixer, a food processor, or a canning jar to churn your cream. (see recipe notes below if you want use a canning jar.) 3. prepare the cream and mixer for churning: place the cream in the bowl of your mixer or processor. cover the top with plastic wrap or a kitchen towel to prevent splattering. 4. churn the cream: turn on the mixer to medium-high. the cream will first whip into peaks (at around 2 minutes) and then become grainy (around 3 minutes). keep whipping until the solid mass (butter) and liquid (buttermilk) are separated (about 5 minutes total). the mixture will splatter heavily in the final stages of churning, so be sure the plastic wrap is secure. the process may take a little longer, up to 8 to 10 minutes, although it usually takes me less than 5 minutes. 5. strain off the buttermilk: pour the buttermilk through the cheesecloth and strainer, holding the butter solid back. allow the buttermilk to strain through, then plop in the butter. gather the cloth around the butter and press it hard with your fist. do this several times to get as much buttermilk out of the butter as possible. pour the buttermilk into a container, label and refrigerate. 6. wash the butter: rinse out the bowl used for buttermilk. remove the butter from the cloth and place it in the bowl. add 120ml of ice water to the bowl, and using a spatula, press the butter into the ice water. it will quickly become cloudy with buttermilk. pour off the cloudy water, add another 120ml of ice water to the bowl, and keep pressing. repeat until the water is clear. this may take up to 6 washings. the butter will firm up towards the end, so you may find it easier to use your hands. 7. salt the butter (optional): sprinkle the salt over the butter and knead in. again, your hands may be the best tool here. 8. store the butter. pack the butter into a jar with a cover, or roll it into a log using waxed paper or parchment paper. the butter will keep in the refrigerator for about three weeks or can be frozen for several months. 9. notes on culturing: many factors will influence how long the cream takes to culture: ambient room temperature, how your cream was processed and pasteurized, how your yogurt was processed and pasteurized, etc. if the cream cultures too quickly and you're not ready to make the butter yet, simply put it into the refrigerator until you are ready. just be sure you remove it about an hour before churning so that it can warm up a bit.cultured cream will be thickened and slightly foamy, and it will have a somewhat tangy, almost yogurt-like smell. trust your senses! if you feel it is too strong and has gone bad, just throw it away. but remember that the yogurt is introducing beneficial cultures that help prevent spoilage, so the likelihood of this happening is small.unplugged butter: you can skip the electric mixer/processor and simply shake your cream in a covered canning jar or well-sealed container until it forms into the butter mass. this can take a while, up to 20 minutes or more, so be prepared for a work-out or solicit some help.recipe can easily be doubled.

title: How To Make Sourdough Cardamom Buns
text: how to make sourdough cardamom buns source: breadbyelise.com ingredients - 45 g active sourdough starter (100% hydration, white) - 45 g whole milk (cold) - 45 g all-purpose or bread flour - 10 g sugar - 550 g bread flour (11-13% protein) - 90 g sugar - 10 g salt - 2 g ground cardamom ((5ml)) - 250 g whole milk (cold) - 2 eggs (small-medium sized) - 145 g sweet levain - 110 g unsalted butter (softened, cut into cubes) - 100 g unsalted butter (softened) - 90 g brown sugar - 2,5 g ground cardamom ((1,25ml)) - 50 g brown sugar - 50 g water - 1 g ground cardamom ((0,25ml)) instructions 1. start by mixing active sourdough starter, milk, flour, and sugar in a medium-sized bowl. cover and rise in a warm spot for 4 hours or until the levain has doubled/tripled in size. 2. start by gathering all the ingredients. add them all, except the butter, to the bowl of your stand mixer fitted with a dough hook. mix on medium speed until the dough comes together. cover, and autolyse/rest for 30 minutes. 3. start your mixer again and knead on medium speed for 5-10 minutes. 4. after 5-10 minutes: slowly add in the softened butter, one cube at a time. 5. when all the butter is added, continue kneading at medium speed for 15-25 minutes until your dough passes the window-pane test. 6. place the dough in a clean bowl and proof in a warm spot, ideally at around 26°c/26°c, for two hours. 7. after two hours, transfer the dough to the fridge to cold-proof for a minimum of six hours. 8. add softened butter, brown sugar, and cardamom to a bowl. mix with a fork until you have a spreadable paste. leave at room temperature until you're ready to shape the buns. 9. transfer the dough to a lightly floured work surface. you might want to leave it at room temperature for 10-15 minutes if it's really cold and difficult to roll out. 10. with a rolling pin, roll the dough into a 19x12in/50x30cm rectangle. 11. evenly spread out the cardamom filling using an offset spatula. 12. grab one of the long sides of the rectangle and fold it down to cover 2/3 of the dough, then grab the other side and fold it over the top (see pictures above for reference). 13. go over the dough a couple of times with a rolling pin to even out the sides. 14. use a sharp knife to cut the dough into 12 strips, roughly 1,5-2 inches each. 15. split each strip into three, leaving one side joined. braid the strips to create a three-stranded plait. grab the end of the plait and roll it up to create a bun—place all the shaped buns in a greased muffin tin. 16. loosely cover the muffin tin with cling film and proof at around 26°c/26°c for 9-12 hours until they've doubled in size. 17. preheat your oven to 179°c/180°c and bake the cardamom buns for 18-20 minutes until golden brown. meanwhile, you can make the brown sugar glaze: 18. while the buns are baking, you can make the glaze. add the ingredients to a small pot and heat up over medium heat until all the sugar is dissolved. 19. when the buns are out of the oven, immediately brush over the syrup using a pastry brush. transfer to a cooling rack and cool for 20-30 minutes before serving.

title: Salt Crusted Chicken
text: salt crusted chicken source: paleoscaleo.com ingredients - 1 five pound chicken - 5 - 1440ml kosher salt - 360ml water instructions 1. preheat the oven to 400° and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. 2. in a large bowl, combine the salt and water and stir until you have "wet sand." set aside. 3. using a sharp pair of kitchen shears, cut the backbone out of the chicken. (this is called "spatchcocking" and allows the chicken to cook more evenly.) 4. spread a small amount (1-2 handfuls) out on the parchment paper, and place the chicken on top, laying flat. 5. pile the rest of the salt mixture on top. pat it down like you're building a sandcastle, making sure it's completely coated, there are no holes, and no spots of skin peeking through. you're trying to achieve an even coating. 6. bake in the oven for 1 hour and 30 minutes. 7. remove from oven, and using a knife or mallet, break open the 'crust' the salt has formed over the chicken and discard. use a pastry brush to brush off any loose salt. 8. peel the skin off the chicken to reveal the juicy, tender, and perfectly cooked meat underneath. the skin will be very salty, but the meat underneath will not be. 9. serve immediately.

title: Almond Milk
text: almond milk source: minimalistbaker.com ingredients - 240ml raw almonds ((soaked overnight in cool water // or 1-2 hours in very hot water)) - 1200ml filtered water ((less to thicken, more to thin)) - 1 pinch sea salt - 2 whole dates ((optional // pitted // or other sweetener of choice // omit for unsweetened)) - 5ml vanilla extract ((optional // or sub 1 vanilla bean, scraped per 5ml extract // omit for plain)) - 30ml cocoa powder ((optional // for "chocolate milk")) - 120ml berries ((optional // for "berry milk")) instructions 1. add your soaked almonds, water, salt, and any additional add-ins (optional) to a high-speed blender and blend until creamy and smooth. keep it running for at least 1-2 minutes so you get the most out of your almonds. 2. strain using a nut milk bag or my favorite trick - a thin dish towel. simply lay a clean dish towel over a mixing bowl, pour over the almond milk, carefully gather the corners, and lift up. then squeeze until all of the liquid is extracted. discard pulp, or save for adding to baked goods (especially crackers). find more ways to use almond pulp here. 3. transfer milk to a jar or covered bottle and refrigerate. will keep for up to 4-5 days, though best when fresh. shake well before drinking, as it tends to separate.

title: Chicken Stock
text: chicken stock source: simplyrecipes.com ingredients - leftover bones and skin from 1 large cooked or raw chicken carcass, or from 2 rotisserie chickens - celery tops and 1 large celery rib, cut into 2-inch segments - 1 large unpeeled onion, quartered - 1 carrot, cut into 2-inch segments - 1 bunch parsley (stems and leaves) - salt, to taste - black pepper, to taste - 15ml olive oil - 4 to 2.3kg chicken wings, backs and/or legs, skin-on, trimmed of excess fat, hacked with a cleaver into 2-inch pieces - 1 large rib celery plus 1 handful leafy celery tops, cut into 2-inch segments - leek or green onions (if you have them) - 1 bay leaf - 6 quarts cold water - 15ml salt, or to taste - 1.8kg chicken wings, backs, and/or legs, hacked with a cleaver into 2-inch pieces - 1 large onion, chopped - 2 quarts boiling water - 10ml salt, or to taste - 2 bay leaves instructions 1. put the leftover bones and skin from a chicken carcass into a large stock pot and add vegetables like celery, onion, carrots, and parsley, then cover with water and add salt and pepper to taste. 2. bring the stock to a boil and immediately reduce heat to bring it to barely a simmer, simmering partially covered for at least 4 hours while occasionally skimming off any foam that comes to the surface. 3. optionally reduce the stock by simmering an hour or two longer to make it more concentrated and easier to store. 4. remove the bones and vegetables with a slotted spoon or spider ladle, and strain the stock through a fine mesh sieve. 5. coat the bottom of a large stock pot with olive oil and place half of the chicken pieces skin side down in the bottom of the pot, heating on medium high until the chicken is browned. 6. add the rest of the chicken pieces and cook, occasionally stirring until the chicken is no longer pink. 7. add the onion, carrot, celery, parsley, leek or green onions if using, and bay leaf to the pot, then cover with 6 quarts of cold water. 8. bring to a boil on high heat and reduce to a low simmer, skimming off any scum that rises to the surface in the first half hour of cooking. 9. let simmer uncovered at a low simmer for 4 to 6 hours, checking every hour to ensure there is still enough water in the pot and lowering the heat or adding more water if needed. 10. use a large metal spoon with holes or a spider ladle to remove the cooked chicken and vegetables, and discard them. 11. use a large sieve lined with dampened cheesecloth or paper towel and place over a large bowl or pot, then pour the stock through the sieve to strain out any remaining solids. 12. pour the strained stock into jars or optionally boil on high heat for 1 hour to reduce by about half, then let cool completely before refrigerating or freezing, leaving at least 1-inch head space if freezing. 13. heat 15ml of olive oil in a large stock pot, add one chopped onion, and sauté until softened and slightly colored for 2 to 3 minutes, then transfer to a large bowl. 14. add half of the chicken pieces to the pot and sauté until no longer pink, about 4 to 5 minutes, then transfer to the bowl with the onions and repeat with the remaining chicken pieces. 15. return the onion and chicken pieces to the pot, reduce heat to low, cover, and cook until chicken releases its juices for about 20 minutes while simultaneously bringing 2 quarts of water to a boil in a large tea kettle. 16. after the chicken pieces have been cooking for 20 minutes, raise the heat to high, add the 2 quarts of boiling water, 10ml of salt, and 2 bay leaves. 17. return to a low simmer while scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan with a wooden spoon, then cover and barely simmer for about 20 minutes. 18. strain the stock through cheesecloth or paper towel-lined large sieve, discarding solids and removing the large pieces of bone with a slotted spoon first. 19. pour the strained stock into jars and cool completely before refrigerating or freezing, where it will last about a week in the refrigerator or several months in the freezer.

title: Japanese Soufflé Creme Brûlée Pancakes
text: japanese soufflé creme brûlée pancakes source: iamafoodblog.com ingredients - 90ml milk - 1 large egg yolk - 30ml sugar - 15ml flour - 30ml room temperature butter - 1 egg yolk - 8ml sugar - 30ml milk - 45ml flour - 1ml baking powder - 2 large egg whites - 1ml cream of tartar - 15ml sugar instructions 1. start by making the creme sauce by whisking together the egg yolk, sugar, and flour until smooth. 2. whisk in the milk and strain into a small pot. 3. heat over medium low heat until the custard thickens. 4. remove from the heat and stir in the butter and set aside. 5. whisk the egg yolk with 15ml of sugar until pale and frothy. 6. mix the milk in batches into the yolk mixture. 7. sift the flour and baking powder over the yolk mixture and whisk well making sure everything is incorporated. 8. whip the egg whites with the cream of tartar until frothy and pale, adding in the sugar a bit at a time until the whites are whipped into a glossy thick meringue that holds a peak. 9. take 1/3 of the whipped egg whites and whisk it into the bowl with the yolks until completely incorporated. 10. add half of the remaining whites and whisk into the yolk batter, being careful not to deflate. 11. transfer the egg yolk mixture to the remaining egg whites and fold together with a spatula. 12. heat up a large non stick frying pan with a lid and very lightly brush with oil. 13. using an ice cream scoop or measuring spoon, scoop about 60ml batter onto the pan, leaving space in between and cover and cook for 3 minutes. 14. remove the lid and add some more batter on top of each pancake, cover and continue to cook for 4-5 more minutes. 15. lift the lid and use a spatula to gently peek under the pancake to check if it releases easily. 16. if you still have any batter left, pile it on top of the pancakes and then gently flip. 17. cover and cook for 5-6 minutes while making sure your creme sauce is loose and pourable, heating it gently with extra milk if needed. 18. once the pancakes are golden and cooked through, gently remove and pile onto a plate. 19. spoon the creme sauce on top and sprinkle generously with sugar. 20. use a cooking torch to brûlée the sugar and serve immediately.

title: Sticky Toffee Pudding
text: sticky toffee pudding source: the guardian ingredients - 50g unsalted butter, plus extra to grease - 175g medjool dates - 5ml bicarbonate of soda - 75g walnuts (optional) - 80g golden caster sugar - 80g dark muscovado sugar - 1 pinch salt - 2 cloves - 175g flour - 5ml baking powder - 2 eggs - 115g unsalted butter (for sauce) - 75g golden caster sugar (for sauce) - 40g dark muscovado sugar (for sauce) - 140ml double cream (for sauce) instructions 1. heat the oven to 200c (180c fan)/199°c/gas 6 and soften the butter. stone and roughly chop the dates with a small, sharp knife. 2. put all sauce ingredients in a small pan over low heat until the butter melts, stirring regularly. turn up the heat and bring to a boil. simmer for about four minutes until thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. 3. grease a 24cm x 24cm baking dish with butter. pour half the sauce into the dish, tip it to coat the base completely, then place in the freezer. boil a kettle of water. 4. put the dates and bicarbonate of soda in a heatproof bowl and pour over 300ml boiling water to cover. leave to soften. if using walnuts, toast them in a dry frying pan over medium-high heat until fragrant, then roughly chop. 5. put the butter and both sugars into a large bowl or food mixer with a pinch of salt. beat vigorously until very light and fluffy. grind the cloves to a fine powder and whisk with the flour and baking powder in a separate bowl. beat the eggs in a cup or jug. 6. beat the eggs into the butter and sugar mixture a little at a time until thoroughly incorporated. fold in the dry ingredients with a large metal spoon, being careful not to knock out too much air. finally, fold in the dates with their soaking water and the walnuts if using. 7. take the dish out of the freezer and pour the batter on top of the sauce. level out the batter and bake for about 30 minutes until just firm to the touch in the centre. reheat the remaining sauce in the pan towards the end of cooking. 8. heat the grill to medium. poke small holes across the top of the baked pudding with a skewer, then pour the sauce over the top. put the dish under the grill until the top is molten and bubbling, watching carefully so the sugar doesn't burn. 9. serve immediately with ice-cream, custard, crème fraîche or greek yoghurt. alternatively, bake the pudding ahead of time without the remaining sauce, cover with foil, reheat in a 180c (160c fan)/177°c/gas 4 oven for about 20 minutes, then continue with the grilling step.

title: Hungarian Goulash
text: hungarian goulash source: spendwithpennies.com ingredients - 10ml salted butter, oil, or lard - 2 medium yellow onions, diced - 5ml caraway seeds - 30ml paprika - 1½ pounds stewing beef or chuck, trimmed and cut into 1-inch cubes - 30ml all-purpose flour - 480ml beef broth or water - 240ml canned diced tomatoes, drained - 5ml salt or to taste - 1ml black pepper - 2 medium potatoes, peeled and diced (optional) - 3 medium carrots, diced (optional) - chopped fresh parsley and sour cream for serving (optional) instructions 1. in a dutch oven or large pot, melt the butter over medium-low heat, add the onion and cook until translucent about 5 minutes, then stir in caraway seeds and paprika. 2. in a bowl or zip-top bag, dredge the beef with flour and shake off any excess, then add the beef to the onion mixture and cook for 2-3 minutes. 3. slowly add 60ml of beef broth while scraping up any brown bits from the bottom of the pan, then add the remaining broth and diced tomatoes, and add potatoes and carrots if using, and season with salt and black pepper. 4. bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce the heat to a low simmer, cover, and cook for about 1½ to 2 hours or until the beef is fork-tender. 5. garnish with parsley if desired and serve with a dollop of sour cream.

title: Kohlrabi Soup with Kohlrabi Greens
text: kohlrabi soup with kohlrabi greens source: chocolatemoosey.com ingredients - 15ml olive oil - salt (preferably kosher), to taste - 60ml diced white or yellow onion - 1 large carrot, peeled and diced - 1 clove garlic, minced - 1200ml vegetable broth/stock - 454g kohlrabi, bulbs peeled and diced and leaves chopped - 1 small sweet potato, peeled and diced (roughly 227g) - 15ml lemon juice instructions 1. in a dutch oven or large pot, add the oil. once hot, add the onion, carrot, and a big pinch of salt. cook until they start to soften and brown, about 3-5 minutes. add the garlic and cook 1 minute. 2. add 1 + 120ml broth and bring to a boil. cook until carrots are softened, about 8-10 minutes. 3. transfer mixture to a blender and blend until smooth. there should be enough broth but if it's too thick to blend, you can add a little more. 4. pour the carrot puree back into the dutch oven. add the remaining 3 + 120ml broth then bring to a boil. 5. once boiling, add the kohlrabi bulbs, sweet potato, and a big pinch of salt. cook until fork tender, about 15 minutes.you should have enough broth, but if your vegetable amounts are bigger than indicated, it's possible you may need to add more as the vegetables will absorb the broth. 6. add kohlrabi leaves and cook 3-5 minutes until the leaves are softened. add lemon juice then taste and adjust for salt.

title: Hungarian Plum Cake
text: hungarian plum cake source: cookpad.com ingredients - 4 medium eggs - 190g butter - 190g cane sugar - 1 large pinch salt - 125g plain yogurt - 12g baking powder - 190g whole grain spelt flour - 5ml ground cinnamon - 350g plum preserve - ground cinnamon for topping - 100g granulated sugar - 30g coarsely chopped walnuts instructions 1. melt the butter slightly, add the sugar and mix, then add the egg yolks and yogurt and mix well. 2. add the cinnamon and the flour mixed with sifted baking powder and mix together. 3. beat the egg whites until stiff and fold them into the batter carefully little by little. 4. pour the batter into a buttered and floured 21x31 cm baking pan, then place the halved plums on top and sprinkle with cinnamon. 5. bake in a preheated oven at 180 degrees c for 40-45 minutes until a skewer inserted into the centre comes out clean, covering the top with foil halfway through to prevent over-browning. 6. while the cake bakes, prepare the praline by melting the sugar in a pot over heat, stirring constantly until it becomes light brown, then add the walnuts and stir. 7. pour the hot praline onto an oiled board, roll it thinly with an oiled rolling pin, cut it into pieces, and sprinkle over the baked cake brushed with plum jam.

title: Indian Barfi Fudge
text: indian barfi fudge ingredients - 720ml milk powder - 360ml powdered sugar - 120ml plus 45ml milk - 45ml butter or ghee - 1/2 to 5ml ground cardamom - 1ml salt - 5ml vanilla extract - approximately 30ml slivered pistachios - saffron, rose buds, and silver leaf for garnish instructions 1. grease a 9×6 baking pan. 2. heat a heavy bottom pan on medium to low heat and add the butter and 120ml of milk, allowing the butter to melt. 3. once the butter melts, add the milk powder while stirring constantly, then gradually add the powdered sugar. 4. if dry powder bits remain, add the three tablespoons of milk one tablespoon at a time until the mixture reaches a paste-like consistency. 5. while continuously stirring, cook the mixture for 8–9 minutes until it easily leaves the surface of the pan and resembles dough. 6. turn off the heat and add vanilla extract, cardamom, and a tablespoon of pistachios, then mix well. 7. spread the mixture evenly on the greased pan and top with the remaining tablespoon of pistachios. 8. let the barfi set for at least three hours before serving or storing in an airtight container at room temperature for up to seven days.

title: Italian Marinade
text: italian marinade source: unknown ingredients - 240ml extra-virgin olive oil - 180ml red wine vinegar - zest of 1 lemon - 60ml freshly squeezed lemon juice (about 2 lemons) - 4 cloves garlic, peeled, smashed and roughly chopped - 1 bay leaf - 15ml thyme leaves - 15ml oregano leaves - 15ml basil leaves, rolled and chopped into chiffonade - 5ml granulated sugar - 5ml kosher salt - 5ml freshly cracked black pepper - 5ml red pepper flakes, or to taste instructions 1. combine the olive oil, red wine vinegar, lemon zest, lemon juice, garlic, bay leaf, thyme, oregano, basil, sugar, salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes in a bowl and whisk until well blended.

title: Jacques Torres Chocolate Chip Cookies
text: jacques torres chocolate chip cookies source: bakeorbreak.com ingredients - 480ml cake flour - 480ml bread flour - 8ml teaspoons baking powder - 6ml teaspoons baking soda - 8ml teaspoons salt - 300ml unsalted butter (softened) - 360ml firmly packed light brown sugar (scant (300ml + 45ml)) - 270ml granulated sugar - 2 large eggs - 10ml vanilla extract - 567g bittersweet chocolate discs (about 60% cacao) - sea salt instructions 1. thoroughly whisk together (or sift) the cake flour, bread flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. set aside. 2. using a mixer with the paddle attachment, beat the butter, brown sugar, and sugar until light and fluffy (about 5 minutes). add the eggs, one at a time, mixing well after each addition. mix in the vanilla. 3. reduce mixer speed to low. add the flour mixture, mixing just until combined (about 10 seconds). stir in the chocolate discs, trying not to break them. 4. cover the dough with plastic wrap, pressing the plastic directly against the dough. chill for 24 to 72 hours. 5. preheat oven to 177°c (175°c). line baking sheets with parchment paper or silicone liner. 6. divide the dough into 99g (99g) portions. (use a #14 or #16 scoop to get about 60ml of dough and use your scale to adjust.) place the mounds of dough on the prepared pans. (you can get about 6 cookies on a pan, but i often just bake 4 at a time to give them a little more space to spread.) sprinkle the top of each cookie with a pinch of sea salt. 7. bake 18 to 20 minutes, or until golden brown but still soft. 8. cool on the pans on a wire rack for 10 minutes. then transfer the cookies to a rack to cool completely.

title: Jam Cake
text: jam cake source: youtube.com ingredients - 500 g flour - 200 g sugar - 200 g butter - 150 g sour cream - 150 g ground walnut - 10 g baking powder - 1 jar raspberry jam (350 g) - 15ml vanilla extract - 1 egg yolk - 1 egg - lemon peel - salt to taste instructions no instructions provided in source text.

title: ג'מבון דה פריז כשר
text: ג'מבון דה פריז כשר בצרפת יש משהו מאוד קלאסי שנקרא jambon de paris — "ג'מבון של פריז". זה בעצם נקניק/פסטרמה עדינה בסגנון צרפתי, בדרך כלל עשויה מחזיר, מבושלת בעדינות, עם מרקם חלק, רך ונקי, וטעם עדין של "נקניק ביתי של פעם". הנה גרסה כשרה. מרכיבים - 500 גר פרגיות - 500 גר חזה עוף - 20 גר מלח - 100 גר מים קרים מאד הוראות הכנה 1. קוצצים בסכין (או פולסים במעבד מזון) את העופות. 2. ממיסים מלח במים ויוצקים על העוף. 3. מערבבים במשך חמש דקות — זה קריטי להוצאת החלבון ולקבלת מסה דביקה. 4. מעבירים לשקית בד ומכניסים למקרר ל-12 שעות. 5. אחרי 12 שעות תולים על הרשת של התנור ואופים ב-70°c במשך 12 שעות. 6. מקררים לחלוטין ופורסים. הערות - הנקניק מחזיק כ-4–5 ימים במקרר (ללא חומרים משמרים וללא ניטריט). - גרסאות דומות: ראו smokedchickenbeefsalami.md ו-smokedchickenbeefsalamininja.md — נקניקי דלי מעושנים המבוססים על עוף ובקר יחד, עם מלח כבישה (ניטריט) ומעבד מזון ליצירת אמולסיה. בניגוד למתכון הזה הם אינם כשרים בהכרח (משלבים בקר ועוף), כוללים עישון, ותהליך הכנה מורכב יותר.

title: Coffee Liqueur
text: coffee liqueur source: america's test kitchen ingredients - 120ml medium-roast coffee beans - 8ml cacao nibs - 1/4 vanilla bean, halved lengthwise - 227g vodka - 113g brandy - 113g simple syrup instructions 1. place coffee beans, cacao nibs, vanilla bean, vodka, and brandy in a pint-size glass jar, cover tightly, and shake to combine. 2. store the jar in a cool, dark place for 1 week, shaking the mixture once every other day. 3. set a fine-mesh strainer in a medium bowl and line it with a triple layer of cheesecloth. 4. strain the vodka mixture through the prepared strainer and discard the solids. 5. return the infused strained vodka mixture to a clean jar and add the simple syrup. 6. cover and gently shake to combine. 7. store in a cool, dark place for up to 1 year, shaking gently before using.

title: Karaage (Japanese Fried Chicken)
text: karaage (japanese fried chicken) source: justonecookbook.com ingredients - 1½ lb boneless, skin-on chicken thighs ((4–6 pieces; read the blog post for details)) - 2ml diamond crystal kosher salt - 1ml freshly ground black pepper - 2ml ginger ((grated, with juice)) - 1 clove garlic - ½–15ml soy sauce - 8ml sake ((or substitute dry sherry, chinese rice wine, or skip it)) - 2ml toasted sesame oil - 3–960ml neutral oil - 30ml potato starch or cornstarch ((plus more, if needed)) - 30ml all-purpose flour (plain flour) ((plus more, if needed)) - lemon wedges - japanese kewpie mayonnaise - shichimi togarashi (japanese seven spice) instructions 1. before you start…please note that this recipe requires 30 minutes of marinating time. gather all the ingredients. 2. prepare 1½ lb boneless, skin-on chicken thighs by cutting each into 2-inch (5-cm) pieces. season with 2ml diamond crystal kosher salt and 1ml freshly ground black pepper. 3. now, grate the ginger (i use a ceramic grater) and measure 2ml ginger (grated, with juice). add it to a large bowl. mince or press 1 clove garlic (i use a garlic press) and add it to the bowl. 4. add ½–15ml soy sauce, 8ml sake, and 2ml toasted sesame oil to the ginger and garlic. whisk to combine. 5. add the chicken to the marinade and mix it with your hands. cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 30 minutes. 6. while the chicken is marinating, prepare the oil for deep-frying. pour about 3–960ml neutral oil into a heavy-bottomed pot (i like using the 2.75-qt staub), until you have at least 1 to 1½ inches (2.5 to 3.8 cm) of oil. heat it to 325ºf (160ºc) over medium-low heat so you have enough time to prep the chicken. 7. meanwhile, dredge the chicken pieces. prepare separate piles of 30ml all-purpose flour (plain flour) and 30ml potato starch or cornstarch in a tray. lightly coat a piece of marinated chicken in the flour and dust off the excess. 8. next, dredge it in the potato starch and shake off the excess. place it in a separate tray. continue with the remaining chicken pieces. 9. check that the oil temperature has reached 325ºf (160ºc). tip: if you don‘t have an instant read thermometer, insert a wooden chopstick into the oil; you‘ll know it‘s hot enough if small bubbles start to appear around the tip. for more helpful tips, see my post how to deep-fry food.when it's ready, gently add 3 to 5 chicken pieces at a time to the hot oil. do not overcrowd the pot. tip: if you add too many pieces at once, the oil temperature will drop quickly, and the chicken will absorb too much oil. 10. deep-fry for 90 seconds, or until the chicken is a light golden color. transfer to a wire rack to drain the excess oil. tip: if the chicken browns too quickly, then the oil temperature is too high. either put a few more pieces of chicken in the oil or lower the heat setting. controlling the oil temperature at all times is very important for deep-frying. 11. the residual heat will continue to cook the chicken as it rests. continue to fry the remaining chicken pieces. between batches, scoop up and discard the crumbs in the oil with a fine-mesh sieve. this keeps the oil clean and prevents it from becoming darker. 12. now, raise the oil temperature to 350ºf (180ºc). place the first 3 to 5 pieces of rested chicken back into the oil and deep-fry for 45 seconds, or until the skin is golden brown and crispy. transfer them to the wire rack to drain the excess oil. continue frying the remaining chicken pieces. 13. the left photo shows the chicken pieces after the first fry and the right photo shows them after the second fry. the chicken pieces on the right are slightly darker in color. 14. serve the chicken hot with lemon wedges and a dipping plate of japanese kewpie mayonnaise. you can also sprinkle shichimi togarashi (japanese seven spice) on the mayo for a bit of spice, if desired. 15. let it cool completely and transfer to an airtight container. you can store it in the refrigerator for up to 3 days and in the freezer for up to a month.

title: Kasha
text: kasha ingredients - 240ml kasha (buckwheat groats), coated in 1 egg - 480ml boiling liquid (water and osem seasoning or broth) - 1 large onion, thinly sliced - 200–250 g mushrooms, sliced - 100–120 g egg noodles (dry) - olive oil or schmaltz - salt, to taste - black pepper instructions 1. heat oil in a wide pan and cook onions over medium-low heat until deeply golden. 2. add mushrooms and sauté until their liquid evaporates and they brown, then push to the side. 3. add egg-coated kasha to the pan, stir and toast for 1–2 minutes until dry, fragrant, and grains separate. 4. pour in 480ml boiling liquid, stir once, cover, and cook on low for 10–12 minutes until absorbed. 5. meanwhile, boil egg noodles until just tender and drain well. 6. turn off heat, let kasha rest 5 minutes covered, then gently fold in noodles. 7. add salt as needed, lots of black pepper, and a drizzle of olive oil, then toss gently.

title: How To Make the Very Best Sweet Cornbread
text: how to make the very best sweet cornbread source: kitchn.com ingredients - 2 sticks (225g) + 30ml unsalted butter, divided - 480ml yellow cornmeal - 480ml all-purpose flour - 10ml baking powder - 5ml baking soda - 5ml salt - 480ml buttermilk - 2 large eggs - 120ml brown sugar - 60ml + 30ml honey, divided instructions 1. preheat oven to 191°c and melt 30ml butter in a 9x13 baking pan in the oven while it preheats. 2. melt the remaining 2 sticks of butter in a saucepan or microwave and let cool slightly. 3. in a large bowl, whisk together cornmeal, flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. 4. in a separate bowl, whisk together buttermilk, eggs, brown sugar, and 60ml honey, then whisk in the melted butter. 5. pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients and stir until just combined, being careful not to overmix. 6. pour batter into the hot buttered pan and drizzle remaining 30ml honey over the top. 7. bake for 25–30 minutes, until golden and a toothpick comes out clean.

title: Kohlrabi Pickles
text: kohlrabi pickles ingredients - 720ml kohlrabi, peeled and cut into sticks - 2 medium carrots, peeled and cut into sticks - 1 clove garlic - 1 bay leaf - 180ml white vinegar - 1¼ cups water - 45ml sugar - 15ml pickling spice mix - 5ml salt - 1ml red pepper flakes instructions 1. pack the kohlrabi sticks, carrot sticks, garlic clove, and bay leaf into a clean quart-sized mason jar. 2. in a small saucepan, combine vinegar, water, sugar, spice mix, salt, and red pepper flakes, and bring to a boil while stirring until sugar and salt dissolve. 3. pour the hot brine over the vegetables in the jar, making sure they are fully submerged. 4. let cool to room temperature, then seal and refrigerate until ready after 24 hours.

title: Latvian Cold Beet Soup
text: latvian cold beet soup ingredients - 3 medium beets, cooked, peeled, and grated or diced - 3–4 cucumbers, diced - 4–5 green onions, sliced - bunch of fresh dill, chopped - 1 liter kefir or buttermilk - 15ml horseradish or mustard - salt and pepper, to taste - 2–4 hard-boiled eggs, halved - cold boiled water, to thin as needed - 30ml lemon juice - 100g sour cream instructions 1. cook beets until tender by boiling or roasting, then let cool, peel, and grate or dice. 2. combine beets, cucumbers, green onions, and dill in a large bowl. 3. pour in kefir or buttermilk and stir in horseradish or mustard, lemon juice, salt, and pepper. 4. add cold boiled water to reach desired consistency and stir well, tasting for seasoning. 5. refrigerate until thoroughly chilled and serve cold, topped with hard-boiled egg halves and a dollop of sour cream.

title: Lekvar (Prune Butter)
text: lekvar (prune butter) ingredients - prunes - water - orange zest - orange juice - sugar - nuts (optional) instructions 1. in a small pot, add the prunes and water and bring to a boil over medium heat. 2. once the water boils, turn the heat down and simmer for 5 to 7 minutes to soften the prunes. 3. using a strainer or a slotted spoon, remove the prunes and place them in a mixing bowl or a mini food processor, reserving the prune water. 4. place the prunes, orange zest and juice, sugar and 10ml of the reserved prune water in the bowl of a mini food processor. 5. pulse until mostly smooth, a few pieces of prune are acceptable. 6. if using a hand blender or potato masher, put all ingredients in a bowl and proceed to blend. 7. taste for flavor and notice the texture. 8. if it seems too thick to use easily, add the third teaspoon of the prune water. 9. if using nuts, place the mixture in a bowl and mix in nuts, adding about half and adjusting to taste.

title: Lekvar (Prune Filling or Prune Butter)
text: lekvar (prune filling or prune butter) ingredients - 480ml dried prunes - 240ml water - 60ml orange juice - 15ml lemon juice - 2ml salt - 1 dash clove - 1 dash cinnamon - 80ml brown sugar instructions 1. combine prunes, water, orange juice, lemon juice, salt, clove, and cinnamon into a saucepan and cook on low heat, stirring every few minutes until the mixture reaches a boil. 2. lower heat to simmer, cover the pan, and cook for 20 minutes, stirring every few minutes. 3. remove the lid from the pan and add brown sugar, then cook while reducing the liquid and stirring every few minutes, being careful not to scorch the mixture. 4. mash the mixture with a wooden spoon until the prunes are soft and broken up and the consistency resembles oatmeal, about 20 more minutes, then allow to cool as it will thicken further.

title: Lemon Buttermilk Muffins with Greek Yogurt & Honey
text: lemon buttermilk muffins with greek yogurt & honey ingredients - 200 ml buttermilk - 60 g oat flakes - 200 g wholemeal flour (e.g., spelt) - 2 eggs - 10ml regular baking powder - 80 g whole cane sugar - 5ml pure vanilla extract - 100 ml canola oil - 2 organic lemons (zest and juice) - 2–15ml full-fat greek yogurt (10%) - 15ml honey instructions 1. preheat your oven to 180°c (fan/convection) and place paper muffin liners in your tray. 2. wash the lemons, grate the zest, then squeeze out the juice and set both aside. 3. in a bowl, mix buttermilk, oat flakes, and lemon zest and let it sit for about 5–10 minutes to soften. 4. slice the vanilla pod and scrape out the seeds, or use vanilla extract. 5. beat the eggs, then stir in the soaked oat mixture, sugar, vanilla, canola oil, and lemon juice. 6. in a separate bowl, whisk together the wholemeal flour and baking powder, then add to the wet mixture and stir until just combined without overmixing. 7. divide the batter evenly between the muffin cups and bake on the middle rack for 20–25 minutes, or until golden brown and a toothpick comes out clean. 8. let the muffins cool in the tray for 5 minutes, then remove and cool completely on a rack. 9. in a small bowl, mix greek yogurt with honey until smooth and spoon or pipe a little on top of each muffin before serving.

title: Lemon Pound Cake
text: lemon pound cake source: once upon a chef ingredients - 720ml all-purpose flour, spooned into measuring cup and leveled-off - 2ml baking soda - 2ml salt - 240ml buttermilk - 30ml packed grated lemon zest - 30ml fresh lemon juice - 240ml unsalted butter, softened - 540ml granulated sugar - 3 large eggs - 30ml water - 30ml granulated sugar - 10ml fresh lemon juice - 240ml confectioners' sugar - 30ml fresh lemon juice instructions 1. preheat the oven to 177°c and set an oven rack in the middle position. 2. spray two 8½ x 4½-inch loaf pans with nonstick cooking spray and line the long sides with parchment paper slings, then spray again. 3. in a medium bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda, and salt, then set aside. 4. in another bowl, whisk together the buttermilk, lemon zest, and lemon juice, then set aside. 5. in the bowl of an electric mixer fitted with the paddle attachment, cream the butter and sugar on medium speed until light and fluffy, about 3 to 4 minutes. 6. beat in the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition and scraping down the sides of the bowl. 7. with the mixer on low speed, alternate adding the flour and buttermilk mixtures, beginning and ending with the flour, then scrape down the sides and mix to ensure all ingredients are well-incorporated. 8. divide the batter into the prepared pans and smooth with a rubber spatula. 9. bake for 55 to 65 minutes, or until the top is golden and a tester comes out clean. 10. cool the cakes in the pans on a wire rack for 10 minutes, then carefully lift them out using the parchment slings and cool for about 1 hour more. 11. combine the water and sugar in a saucepan and bring to a boil, then remove from heat and stir in the lemon juice. 12. in a medium bowl, whisk together the confectioners' sugar and lemon juice until smooth, adjusting with more sugar or juice as needed for your preferred consistency. 13. brush the warm syrup all over the cooled cakes, including the sides, letting it soak in as you go. 14. spoon the glaze over the top of the cakes, letting it drip down the sides, and let sit for about 1 hour to allow the glaze to set before serving.

title: Margarita
text: margarita ingredients - 50 cc blanco tequila - 30 cc lime juice - 20 cc triple sec instructions 1. combine all ingredients in shaker tin. 2. add ice to small shaker tin. 3. shake vigorously. 4. strain into chilled rocks glass with a salt rim over fresh ice. 5. garnish with lime and enjoy.

title: Mac Pasta
text: mac pasta ingredients - 60ml olive oil - 1 shallot - 1 garlic clove - 120ml tomato paste - 30ml vodka - 240ml heavy cream - 5ml red pepper flakes - salt and pepper to taste - 454g fusilli or linguini - 30ml unsalted butter - parmesan cheese - fresh basil instructions 1. heat olive oil in a dutch oven or cast iron pan. 2. add shallot and garlic and wait until softened. 3. add tomato paste and cook until it starts to caramelize. 4. add vodka and cook until all liquid has evaporated. 5. add heavy cream and stir until the sauce reaches an orange color, then turn off heat. 6. cook pasta for 3 minutes less than the package cooking time. 7. add cooked pasta to the sauce and stir so all pasta is evenly coated. 8. stir in butter and red pepper flakes. 9. serve with lots of chopped fresh basil.

title: Magic Three Layer Custard Cake
text: magic three layer custard cake source: recipetineats.com ingredients - 4 eggs, yolks and whites separated (at room temperature) - 180ml (150g) sugar - 5ml vanilla extract - 1 stick (125g) unsalted butter, melted - 180ml (115g) plain all purpose flour - 480ml (500 ml) milk, lukewarm (full fat or low fat but not zero fat) - icing sugar (powdered sugar), for dusting - fresh strawberries, for serving - whipped cream, for serving instructions 1. preheat oven to 163°c/160c. 2. butter an 8" x 8" square cake tin. 3. beat egg whites with a mixer until stiff peaks form and set aside. 4. place the egg yolks and sugar in a bowl and beat until pale yellow, about 1 minute. 5. add the vanilla extract and melted butter and beat until well incorporated. 6. add the flour and beat until just combined. 7. pour the milk in slowly while beating until well combined. 8. use a spatula to fold in the egg whites one third at a time until just incorporated. 9. pour the batter into the prepared cake tin. 10. bake until the top is golden brown and the cake does not jiggle when gently shaken, around 40 to 50 minutes. 11. check the cake at 30 minutes and if the top is golden brown but the cake jiggles, cover loosely with foil and return to the oven for 10 minutes at a time until set. 12. allow the cake to cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a cooling rack and cool completely. 13. cut into squares and dust with icing sugar just before serving. 14. serve with whipped cream and strawberries if desired.

title: Make Your Own Herbes de Provence
text: make your own herbes de provence ingredients - 0-15ml dried anise seed - 1-30ml dried lavender - 1-30ml dried basil - 1-30ml dried tarragon - 15ml fennel seeds - 0-5ml dried mint - 30ml to 60ml dried thyme - 2-45ml dried marjoram - 1-30ml dried oregano - 1/2 to 30ml dried parsley and/or chervil - 2-45ml dried savory - 30ml dried rosemary - 5ml ground bay leaf powder instructions 1. combine all dried herbs and spices in a bowl or jar. 2. mix thoroughly until well blended. 3. store in an airtight container.

title: Slow Cooker Beef Bone Broth
text: slow cooker beef bone broth source: the healthy foodie ingredients - 1.36 kg mixed beef bones, oxtail, knuckles, neckbones and/or short ribs - 2 medium carrots - 3 celery stalks - 2 medium onions - 30ml apple cider vinegar - 1 bay leaf - 2.5 kg water instructions 1. preheat your oven to 200°c. 2. place the bones in a single layer on a baking sheet or roasting pan and roast for 60 minutes, flipping each bone over halfway through cooking time. 3. roughly chop the vegetables without peeling them and place them along with the bay leaf and apple cider vinegar into a 6 quart slow cooker. 4. add the bones as soon as they come out of the oven and fill the pot completely with water. 5. set the slow cooker on low, cover and cook for 18 to 36 hours, or until the broth has reached a beautiful brown color. 6. carefully remove the larger pieces with a slotted spoon and place them in a strainer set over a large bowl to collect the excess broth. 7. strain the broth that's still in the crockpot through a fine meshed sieve or through a strainer lined with cheesecloth. 8. transfer the bone broth into jars and refrigerate promptly. 9. once the broth has fully cooled, remove some or all of the fat layer that formed at the top for use in cooking.

title: Mango Pickle Recipe
text: mango pickle recipe source: indianhealthyrecipes.com ingredients - 300ml mango pieces (cubed (heaped cup, 1 medium mango)) - 15ml mustard seeds ( or 30ml. mustard powder) - 2ml methi seeds ((fenugreek seeds)) - 45ml red chili powder ((use low heat spice powder, or adjust to taste)) - 8ml salt (adjust as needed) - 4 garlic cloves (crushed) - 45ml oil instructions 1. choose raw, fresh and unripe green mango that is firm and has a clear skin. wash and dry mango thoroughly. wipe clean with a cloth. do this the previous night. 2. if possible sun dry the jar and other utensils used for making pickle, make sure all the bowls, spoons, chopping board and knife are dry. these precautions will increase the shelf life of the mango pickle. 3. dry roast methi seeds on a low flame until deep golden and aromatic. transfer to a plate and cool them completely. 4. to the same pan, pour oil and heat it up until slightly warm. set aside to cool completely. you can skip warming the oil if you intend to finish the mango pickle within 10 to 12 days. skip heating if using cold pressed oil. 5. blend methi seeds along with mustard seeds to a fine powder. crush garlic. 6. chop mangoes to slightly large cubes of 1 inch, using a large knife. 7. optional for shelf-life: sun dry each separately - spice powders, salt, garlic and chopped mangoes. alternately you may heat them in oven at 60 to 70 c (140 to 71°c) for 1 hour (avoid keeping salt in oven) 8. add them to a dry bowl, along with red chili powder, mustard powder, salt and lightly crushed garlic. 9. pour the oil and mix well. the pickle will be dry at this stage. cover and set aside for 24 to 28 hours in a dry place. 10. after 24 to 28 hours, mango pieces will release juices and the consistency of the pickle will change. check the step-by-step photos above. stir mango pickle well and taste test it. if needed add more salt. 11. store this mango pickle in a clean dry glass jar. store it in the refrigerator after 24 hours. if storing at room temperature avoid storing in the kitchen or places with high moisture. 12. it will be ready to serve after 3 days but it tastes best as it ages. 13. use dry clean spoons every time you use. after every use, wipe off the sides of the jar with a clean tissue or dry cloth to avoid mold.

title: Marcella Hazan’s Legendary Tomato Sauce
text: marcella hazan’s legendary tomato sauce source: thekitchn.com ingredients - 1 (28-ounce) can whole tomatoes, no salt or herbs added - 75ml unsalted butter - 1 small white onion, peeled and cut in half - kosher salt - cooked pasta - finely grated parmesan cheese - freshly ground black pepper instructions 1. place 1 (28-ounce) can whole tomatoes, 75ml unsalted butter, 1 halved small white onion, and a pinch of kosher salt in a large saucepan and bring to a simmer over medium-high heat. 2. lower the heat to maintain a gentle simmer and cook, stirring and crushing the tomatoes lightly with the back of a spoon occasionally, until droplets of fat appear on the surface of the tomatoes, about 45 minutes. remove and discard the onion. 3. serve over hot pasta with grated parmesan cheese and ground black pepper if desired. 4. storage: leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days or frozen for up to 3 months.adapted in my own words from marcella hazan's "essentials of classic italian cooking."

title: Masapan (Marzipan) — Jewish Food Society
