title: Mascarpone Mousse
text: mascarpone mousse source: food.com ingredients - 180ml heavy whipping cream - 15ml granulated sugar - 113g mascarpone cheese - 57g cream cheese - 1ml pure vanilla extract - 45ml powdered sugar instructions 1. in a small chilled metal bowl whisk heavy cream in a figure eight motion. 2. just as soft peaks are forming, add the granulated sugar gradually. 3. continue whipping the cream until stiff peaks form. 4. cover the bowl and chill in an ice bath. 5. combine room temperature mascarpone and cream cheese with a rubber scraper. 6. add vanilla and powdered sugar. 7. when cheese mixture reaches a smooth consistency, set aside, keeping the mixture at room temperature. 8. just before serving, lightly fold whipped cream into the cheese mixture.

title: Mascarpone and Sweet Cream Ice Cream
text: mascarpone and sweet cream ice cream ingredients - 240ml mascarpone cheese - 1 can (397g) sweetened condensed milk - 240ml heavy cream - 5ml vanilla extract - a pinch of salt instructions 1. whip the heavy cream in a large bowl until soft peaks form. 2. in another bowl, whisk together the mascarpone cheese, sweetened condensed milk, vanilla extract, and a pinch of salt until smooth. 3. gently fold the whipped cream into the mascarpone mixture, making sure not to deflate the whipped cream too much. 4. pour the mixture into a container and cover with plastic wrap. 5. freeze for at least 4 hours or overnight. 6. once frozen, scoop and enjoy.

title: Meat 6
text: meat 6 ingredients - 45ml olive oil - 1 whole piece of meat - 1 onion, quartered - 2 whole carrots - 3 celery stalks - 1 celeriac, halved - 2 large pieces of parsley root - 1 bunch parsley, halved - 1 basket whole button mushrooms - 7 whole garlic cloves - 240ml dry red wine - 2 bay leaves - 15ml coarse salt - 8ml ground black pepper - 240ml water - a few leaves of sage instructions 1. in a pot, add three tablespoons of olive oil and sear the whole piece of meat on all sides until it gets a charred and perfect color. 2. add the quartered onion, whole carrots, celery stalks, halved celeriac, parsley root pieces, halved parsley, button mushrooms, garlic cloves, dry red wine, bay leaves, coarse salt, ground black pepper, water, and sage leaves to the pot. 3. cover the pot and transfer it to a turbo oven at 160 degrees for three hours. 4. serve with a side of pirto.

title: בורקס בשר ורוטב פטריות
text: בורקס בשר ורוטב פטריות source: crunchit.co.il ingredients - חבילה אחת בצק עלים או בצק פילאס - 500 גרם בשר טחון (צוואר או צלעות) - בצל גדול מאוד חתוך לקוביות קטנות - 2 שיני שום כתושות - 4 כפות שמן - רבע צרור פטרוזיליה קצוצה (רק העלים) - כף צנוברים קלויים - קופסת רסק עגבניות קטנה (100 גרם) - כף פפריקה מתוקה - כף שטוחה סוכר - כפית מלח - כפית פלפל גרוס - פפריקה חריפה (אופציונלי) - בצל חתוך לקוביות קטנות - סלסלת פטריות טריות או קופסת שימורים של פטריות חתוכות - 2 כוסות מים רותחים - 2 כפות קמח או קורנפלור - מלח לפי הטעם - פלפל שחור לפי הטעם - כף גדושה מרק עוף - ביצה למריחה - שומשום instructions 1. לשים שמן במחבת גדולה ועמוקה וטגן את הבצל עד שקיפות והזהבה קלה. 2. להוסיף את השום הכתוש ערבוב קצר ומיד להוסיף את הבשר הטחון. 3. לפרור את הבשר עם מזלג ולערבב כל הזמן עד שמחליף את הצבע. 4. להוסיף פלפל ומלח והעבירו לקערה. 5. באותה מחבת לשים כפית שמן ולהוסיף את הרסק, הפפריקה, הסוכר ומלח. 6. להוסיף את הבשר הטחון ולאחד בין התערובות. 7. להוסיף פטרוזיליה וצנוברים ולערבב להאחדת טעמים. 8. לטעום ולתקן תיבול ולהניח בצד להתקררות. 9. לטגן את הבצל עד שקיפות להכנת הרוטב. 10. להוסיף את הפטריות לאידוי נוזלים. 11. להוסיף מים וברזל כמה דקות תוך כדי ערבוב תמידי. 12. בכוס לשים 2 כפות קמח ולשפוך מים עליהם לערבב עד שאין גושים. 13. להכניס את תערובת הקמח לרוטב החם וערבב מהר עד איחוד. 14. להכניס מרק עוף ולהכביא את האש. 15. לחלק את בצק העלים לשניים ולפתוח מעט. 16. לשים בקצה כמות מהמילוי וגלגל לרולדה או לחתוך ריבועים ולמלא כל ריבוע. 17. למרוח על הבצק ביצה ולפזר שומשום. 18. להכניס לתנור שחומם מראש ל-180 מעלות עד שמזהיב (כ-45 דקות). 19. למזוג את הרוטב על הבורקס לפני הגשה.

title: Aussie Meat Pie recipe
text: aussie meat pie recipe source: recipetineats.com ingredients - 1 1/2 batches homemade shortcrust pastry - 3 frozen shortcrust pastry sheets, thawed ((300g/284g)) - 2 refrigerated pie crusts (us/can) - 3 frozen puff pastry sheets, just thawed ((300g/284g) (note 2)) - 1 egg (, lightly whisked) - 1.25 kg / 1.1kg beef chuck (, 2.5cm/1" cubes (note 3)) - 2ml each salt & pepper - 2 - 45ml olive oil - 1 onion (, diced) - 4 garlic cloves (, minced) - 75ml flour (, plain/all purpose) - 300ml (315 ml) beef stock, low sodium ((note 4)) - 720ml (750 ml) red wine (, dry full bodied (note 5)) - 30ml tomato paste - 5ml worcestershire sauce - 10ml black pepper (, coarsely ground) - 2 bay leaves instructions 1. sprinkle beef with 2ml salt and pepper. 2. heat 15ml oil in a large heavy based pot over high heat. add 1/3 of the beef and brown aggressively all over, then remove. repeat with remaining beef, adding more oil if needed. 3. turn stove down to medium high. add garlic and onion, cook 3 minutes. 4. add flour, stir through. 5. slowly add beef stock while stirring constantly. once flour is dissolved, add wine, tomato paste, worcestershire, pepper and bay leaves. 6. return beef into pot, cover with lid, adjust heat so it's simmering gently. 7. simmer 1 hr 45 minutes. remove lid, increase heat slightly and simmer 30 - 45 minutes, stirring regularly, or until beef is fork tender and liquid reduces down to a thickish gravy, just about covering beef (see video). do not reduce liquid too much - thickens more as it cools & in pie. 8. remove from stove, cover and cool filling (i usually leave overnight). 9. preheat oven to 180c/177°c. 10. cut out 6 rounds from the shortcrust pastry, then drape pastry into pie tins - don't stretch and pull pastry, causes shrinkage. (notes 1 & 6) 11. place pies on tray. top each pie with large sheets of parchment / baking paper and fill with pie weights (note 7). 12. bake 20 minutes, remove, then use paper overhang to carefully remove pie weights. 13. return crusts into oven for 5 minutes or until base is light golden and dry (can skip, note 8). remove from oven. 14. fill pies with cooled filling, push down to fill. should be slightly mounded. 15. cut rounds from partially thawed puff pastry - cut them slightly larger than the edge of the cooked pastry bases. 16. brush edge of pie crusts with egg, then place lid on filling, pressing edges to seal puff pastry to the shortcrust pastry. 17. brush lids with egg, then cut a 1cm / 0.5" incision in the middle using a small knife. 18. bake 30 minutes or until deep golden and puffed. 19. devour hot and fresh, topped with tomato sauce or ketchup if desired!

title: Meatballs with Any Meat
text: meatballs with any meat ingredients - 454g ground meat (pork, beef, veal, chicken, turkey or a combination) - 120ml panko bread crumbs - 1 egg - 5ml kosher salt, more as needed - black pepper and/or ground cumin, curry powder, chile flakes, garam masala, etc., to taste - minced garlic, onion, scallions or shallot - chopped parsley, basil or cilantro - olive oil, for frying (optional) instructions 1. in a large bowl, gently combine all ingredients, roll into 1½-inch balls, and transfer to a baking sheet. 2. broil until golden and firm for 7 to 10 minutes, or fry in oil until deeply browned all over. 3. sprinkle with more salt before serving.

title: Mozzarella
text: mozzarella ingredients - 1¼ cups water, divided - 1½ tsp citric acid - ¼ rennet tablet - 1 gallon whole milk or 2% milk (not ultra-pasteurized/uht) - 5ml kosher salt instructions 1. dissolve citric acid in 240ml cold water and dissolve rennet in 60ml cold water, then set aside. 2. pour milk into a large pot, add citric acid solution and stir well, then heat over medium heat to 32°c (32°c) while stirring gently. 3. remove from heat, add the rennet solution and stir gently for 30 seconds, then cover and let sit for 5 minutes undisturbed. 4. check the curd to ensure it looks like soft tofu, letting it sit another 5 minutes if too soft, then cut the curd into ½-inch cubes with a knife. 5. return pot to medium heat, heat curds to 41°c (40°c) while gently stirring, then remove from heat and continue stirring slowly for 2–3 minutes. 6. scoop the curds into a microwave-safe bowl using a slotted spoon, draining off as much whey as possible and reserving the whey. 7. microwave curds on high for 1 minute, drain off excess whey, and fold curds over themselves several times. 8. microwave again for 30 seconds, drain whey and fold again, then repeat once more until the cheese reaches 57°c (57°c) and is smooth and stretchy. 9. add salt and knead it into the cheese. 10. stretch and fold the cheese until smooth and glossy, like taffy. 11. form into a ball or desired shape, then place in cool water or salted whey to firm up, and use immediately or refrigerate.

title: Mushroom Potpie
text: mushroom potpie source: new york times cooking ingredients - 120ml dried porcini mushrooms (14g) - 60ml olive oil, plus more as needed - 227g fresh oyster mushrooms, torn into separate pieces (or shiitake mushrooms, stemmed and halved) - kosher salt and black pepper - 227g cremini mushrooms, stemmed and quartered (or cut into sixths if large) - 60ml unsalted butter - 1 large yellow onion, finely chopped - 113g lacinato kale, stemmed, leaves thinly sliced crosswise - 4 garlic cloves, chopped - 15ml fresh thyme leaves - 10ml chopped fresh rosemary - 60ml all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting - 1½ cups chicken or vegetable stock - 180ml heavy cream - 240ml diced peeled carrots (from 2 medium carrots, cut into 1/2-inch pieces) - 240ml diced peeled parsnips (from 2 medium parsnips, cut into 1/2-inch pieces) - 240ml diced red potatoes (from 2 small potatoes, cut into 1/2-inch pieces) - 1 (14- to 16-ounce) package puff pastry, thawed - 1 large egg instructions 1. heat oven to 425 degrees and bring 480ml of water to boil in a small pot. 2. place the porcini mushrooms in a medium bowl and pour the boiling water on top; set aside to soak and soften. 3. in a large (12-inch) ovenproof skillet, heat 30ml oil over medium-high and working in two batches, add half the oyster mushrooms, season with salt and pepper and cook undisturbed until browned underneath, about 3 minutes. 4. stir the oyster mushrooms and continue to cook until browned all over, about 3 minutes, then transfer to a medium bowl. 5. repeat with 30ml oil and the remaining oyster mushrooms and transfer them to the medium bowl. 6. add another 30ml oil, then add the cremini mushrooms, season with salt and pepper and cook, stirring occasionally, until browned and tender, 6 to 8 minutes, lowering the heat as needed to avoid burning, then transfer to the bowl. 7. reduce the heat to medium and add the butter to the skillet, then once melted, add the onion and cook until starting to soften, about 5 minutes. 8. add the kale, garlic, thyme and rosemary, season with salt and pepper and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 3 minutes, adding 1 to 30ml oil if the pan seems dry. 9. sprinkle with the flour and cook, stirring, until flour is dispersed and lightly toasted, 2 minutes. 10. stirring constantly, gradually add the stock, cream and 180ml of the liquid from the soaking porcini mushrooms. 11. cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until thickened, about 5 minutes, then remove from heat. 12. stir in the carrots, parsnips, potatoes, and the sautéed mushrooms and any accumulated juices. 13. strain the soaked porcini mushrooms, discard any remaining liquid, then roughly chop the mushrooms and stir them into the filling. 14. season to taste with salt and pepper. 15. on a lightly dusted work surface using a lightly floured rolling pin, roll out the puff pastry into a roughly 14-inch circle. 16. transfer the puff pastry to the top of the skillet, allowing slight overhang, and fold under and pinch any overhang just below the rim of the skillet. 17. in a small bowl, whisk the egg with 5ml water and lightly brush the egg wash over the top of the puff pastry. 18. cut 5 (2-inch) slits into the puff pastry, starting near the center and radiating outward like the rays of the sun, or create a stripe or crisscross pattern by gently scoring it with a paring knife without fully cutting through. 19. crimp the edges using the tines of a fork if desired. 20. set the skillet on top of an aluminum foil-lined baking sheet and transfer to the middle rack of the oven. 21. bake until the puff pastry is puffed and golden, about 30 minutes, then let sit 10 minutes before serving.

title: Napoleon (Cream Cake)
text: napoleon (cream cake) source: domowe-wypieki.pl ingredients - 300 g butter - 300 g wheat flour - 1 egg (size m) - 8ml vinegar (about 5%) - approximately 100 ml hot water - 1 liter milk - 50 g butter - 4 egg yolks - 2 eggs (size m) - 200 g sugar - 10ml vanilla sugar - 120 g wheat flour - 70 g potato starch - powdered sugar for sprinkling instructions 1. prepare puff pastry by kneading 300 g butter and 100 g flour to a homogeneous mass, then place it between two pieces of food foil and flatten it by hand or roll out into a square about 2 cm thick, and refrigerate. 2. during this time, knead the dough from the remaining ingredients with enough water to make it resemble pierogi dough, then roll it out on a flour-covered surface into a circle. 3. place the cooled butter mass from the fridge in the center of the rolled dough, fold the dough into an envelope, and glue the edges thoroughly. 4. invert the dough with the joints facing downwards and roll out into a long rectangle approximately 1 cm thick, always rolling in one direction. 5. fold the dough into three parts like a letter, lightly roll out just by pressing with a roller to make it thinner, wrap in foil, and place on a wooden board in the freezer for 15 minutes. 6. remove the dough from the freezer, turn it 90 degrees, and roll it out again into an oblong rectangle, then re-fold as a letter, lightly roll out, wrap in foil, and place in the freezer for 15 minutes. 7. repeat the folding and freezing process two more times, each time placing the dough in the freezer for 15 minutes. 8. cut the finished dough in half, wrap one half in foil, and refrigerate. 9. roll out the other half of the dough on a flour-covered countertop into a large rectangular cake, transfer it to a large flat oven tray lined with baking paper, trim the edges with a knife, and prick with a fork. 10. bake in a preheated oven at 220°c with the top-down heater for about 15 minutes until golden brown, opening the oven after a few minutes to prick any bulges with a fork. 11. bake the second cake in the same way and allow both cakes to cool completely. 12. cut one cake intended for the top with a serrated knife into squares of the desired size for individual portions. 13. prepare the pudding mass by boiling approximately 750 ml of milk with butter, sugar, and vanilla sugar, then mix the remaining milk with eggs, yolks, flour, and starch and add to the boiling milk while stirring to prevent lumps from forming, and cook until thick. 14. allow the pudding to cool slightly while stirring briefly every now and then, then pour it still slightly warm onto the first puff pastry cake, wrapping the bottom with aluminum foil rolled several times to prevent the pudding from flowing out. 15. arrange the cut squares on top of the pudding mass. 16. place the cake in the refrigerator for at least a few hours. 17. sprinkle with powdered sugar and cut with a sharp serrated knife.

title: Naturally Leavened Bomboloni (Doughnuts)
text: naturally leavened bomboloni (doughnuts) source: theperfectloaf.com ingredients - 45g mature 100% hydration starter - 90g all-purpose white flour - 90g water - 253g all-purpose white flour - 253g high-protein bread flour - 187g eggs (about 3 large plus 1 yolk, cold) - 101g unsalted european butter - 101g fine white sugar - 91g water - 10g salt - 203g mature 100% hydration levain - 2g ground cinnamon - 200g sugar - 365g whole milk - 30g all-purpose flour - 100g fine sugar - 4 large egg yolks - 1g salt - 4g vanilla extract - zest of 1 lemon (optional) instructions 1. build levain with 45g mature starter, 90g all-purpose flour, and 90g water in the morning. store at 26°c until ripe, approximately 5 hours. 2. soften butter and cut into half-inch cubes. bring eggs to weight and keep cold. 3. add flour, sugar, eggs, levain, salt, and water to mixer with paddle attachment. stir 1 minute, then mix on speed two for 5 minutes and rest 10 minutes. 4. mix on speed three for 9-10 minutes, adding butter chunk by chunk, until dough almost passes the windowpane test. 5. perform 4 sets of stretch and folds every 30 minutes over 2 hours. rest for 4 hours after final fold, aiming for at least 30% rise. cover and refrigerate overnight. 6. allow flexible cold fermentation overnight. 7. dump cold dough on unfloured surface and divide into 18 pieces of 65g each. preshape into tight rounds with taut surface. 8. place on floured trays, 8 per tray. proof at 26°c for approximately 12 hours until nearly doubled and very puffy. bomboloni should feel air-filled when poked. 9. heat oil to 360-188°c in a heavy pot. fry bomboloni smooth-side down first, up to 3 at a time, for 2.5 minutes per side until golden brown. 10. drain fried bomboloni, then toss in cinnamon-sugar mixture while warm. 11. for crema pasticcera, heat milk until bubbles form on sides. whisk together flour, salt, and sugar, then add egg yolks to form a thick paste. 12. slowly pour warm milk over yolk mixture while whisking constantly. return to pot on medium heat and whisk until large bubbles pop. 13. strain crema through fine mesh. stir in vanilla extract and lemon zest if desired. 14. cover with plastic wrap on surface and refrigerate until firm. pipe into bomboloni just before serving.

title: New York Style Sourdough Bagels
text: new york style sourdough bagels source: baked-theblog.com ingredients - 240ml active sourdough starter - 300ml cold water - 30ml barley malt syrup (or maple syrup) - 1200ml all-purpose flour - 10ml fine salt - flour (or semolina for proofing) - 15ml baking soda - 15ml brown sugar - 120ml any combination of poppy seeds/dried onion flakes/dried garlic flakes/sesame seeds/flaky salt/za'atar instructions 1. in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a paddle attachment, mix your bubbly, active starter with the water and maple syrup until well-combined. alternatively, mix in a standard large bowl with a fork or whisk. 2. add in the flour and salt and transition to a dough hook. knead on medium until the dough is smooth and somewhat pliable, about 6-7 minutes. alternatively, knead the dough by hand on a countertop until smooth and pliable. 3. shape into a ball (return to bowl, if applicable) and cover bowl with a towel. rest 20 minutes. 4. divide the dough into 8 equal pieces for large bagels or 10 equal pieces for smaller ones. shape each piece into a small ball by tucking the corners underneath, cupping the dough, and rolling it in a circular fashion on a clean, flour-free countertop. this helps to create surface tension and a skin on the ball. 5. cover dough balls and rest another 15 minutes. 6. line a baking sheet with parchment paper and sprinkle generously with flour or semolina. note: if you make 10 bagels, you will need to use 2 baking sheets. 7. flatten the ball of dough into a disc and use your fingertips to roll into a log about 8 inches (20 cm) long. 8. wrap the log around your three middle fingers with the ends overlapping by 2 inches (5 cm) on the inside of your hand. 9. roll gently, palm down, until the ends are joined together. this will create a larger hole in the centre of the bagel. 10. poke a hole with your finger directly through the centre of the dough ball. 11. insert both index fingers into the hole and roll fingers around each other to stretch out the centre (like a barrel roll) until it’s about the size of a walnut. this will create a smaller bagel hole, but is much faster and more efficient to do. 12. place on the lined baking sheet and repeat with the rest of the bagels. this is a fun step to do with kids 3 years old or older. 13. cover the shaped bagels with a towel, let them proof at room temperature for 2.5 to 4.5 hours, or until puffy. this could take more time, depending on the temperature in your house. 14. take a test bagel and place it in cold water. if it floats, they’re done proofing. dry the test bagel off and return to the baking sheet. if it sinks, it still needs to proof longer. 15. once proofed, cover the pan with plastic wrap and refrigerate 12 to 24 hours. 16. preheat oven to 232°c (230°c). place toppings on flat plates, so they are ready to go. 17. bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil and add the baking soda and brown sugar. 18. remove the bagels from the fridge and gently place them, a couple at a time, into the water. 19. boil for 15 to 20 seconds on each side. 20. remove boiled bagels with a slotted spoon to get rid of most of the water. 21. shake off excess water and immediately dip the top of bagel into desired toppings. 22. set back on the baking sheet. 23. repeat this process with the remaining bagels. 24. place the baking sheet into the center of the oven and turn it down to 204°c (200°c). 25. bake for 18 to 22 minutes or until golden on top. 26. cool on a wire rack until ready to serve.

title: Ninja Grilled Salmon
text: ninja grilled salmon source: girlscangrill.com ingredients - 1.4kg salmon filet - 60ml olive oil - 15ml kosher salt - 15ml brown sugar - 10ml coarse ground black pepper - 2ml granulated garlic - 1ml ground ginger - 1ml ground cayenne pepper instructions 1. combine all of the rub ingredients in a small bowl. 2. cut the salmon in half so it will fit on the ninja grill. 3. brush both sides with olive oil. 4. sprinkle both sides with rub. 5. set the ninja grill to the grill function, set the heat to high and the time to 20 minutes. 6. place the filets on the grill skin side up and grill for 5-6 minutes. 7. flip the salmon and grill for 8-10 minutes to an internal temperature of 62 degrees celsius. 8. remove from the grill and serve.

title: Ninja Woodfire Grill Smoky Whole Chicken
text: ninja woodfire grill smoky whole chicken source: grillwhatyoulove.com ingredients - 1 whole chicken, 3-1.8kg - 30ml montreal chicken seasoning or your favorite chicken rub - wood pellets (apple, cherry, or pecan recommended) instructions 1. preheat your ninja woodfire outdoor grill to the grill setting on high heat. 2. add pellets to the hopper and press the woodfire button to add smoke. 3. set the cook time for 35 to 40 minutes. 4. spatchcock the chicken by placing it breast side down, cutting along both sides of the backbone with kitchen shears, removing the backbone, and pressing the chicken flat. 5. pat the chicken skin completely dry with paper towels. 6. sprinkle both sides generously with montreal chicken seasoning. 7. place the chicken on the grill skin-side down and cook for 5 to 6 minutes to sear the skin. 8. flip the chicken over and reduce the heat to low. 9. continue cooking the chicken cut-side down for 15 to 20 minutes. 10. flip the chicken back to skin-side down and continue cooking until the internal temperature reaches 71°c. 11. remove the chicken from the grill and let it rest for a few minutes so the juices can redistribute. 12. carve and serve.

title: No Bake Cheesecake With Condensed Milk
text: no bake cheesecake with condensed milk source: cookingwithcarlee.com ingredients - graham cracker crust - 454g cream cheese (softened) - 397g sweetened condensed milk - 80ml sour cream - 10ml lemon juice (optional) instructions 1. in a medium bowl, mix 454g cream cheese on low speed until it is creamy and lump free. be sure to scrape the sides of the bowl and the beater a few times along the way. 2. slowly add the 397g sweetened condensed milk, mixing on low after each addition until it is incorporated fully. 3. mix in 80ml sour cream until incorporated. if using 10ml lemon juice, add now. 4. spoon the cream cheese mixture into the prepared graham cracker crust. 5. chill for at least 4 hours, though longer is better, before serving.

title: Nougat
text: nougat ingredients - 240ml granulated sugar - 120ml honey - 2 egg whites - 240ml nuts (such as almonds, hazelnuts, or pistachios), coarsely chopped - 5ml vanilla extract instructions 1. in a small saucepan, combine the sugar and honey and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the sugar has dissolved and the mixture has reached a temperature of 116°c on a candy thermometer. 2. beat the egg whites in a large mixing bowl until stiff peaks form. 3. when the sugar mixture has reached the correct temperature, carefully pour it into the egg whites in a thin stream while continuing to beat the mixture on high speed. 4. add the vanilla extract and nuts to the mixture and continue beating until the mixture is thick and glossy. 5. spread the mixture evenly into a greased 8x8-inch baking dish and let the nougat cool completely before cutting it into squares. 6. serve the nougat as is, or use it as a filling for chocolate bars or other sweets.

title: Oatmeal Creme Pies
text: oatmeal creme pies ingredients - 300ml room temperature butter - 240ml packed dark brown sugar - 120ml granulated sugar - 1 large egg - 10ml vanilla extract - 15ml dark molasses - 360ml all purpose flour - 5ml baking soda - 2ml salt - 4ml cinnamon - 1ml ground cloves, nutmeg, or pumpkin spice - 720ml quick cooking oats - 180ml room temperature butter (for filling) - 720ml sifted confectionery sugar - 8ml vanilla extract (for filling) - up to 45ml heavy cream - salt to taste instructions 1. bring the butter to room temperature, or place it in a warm location to soften if you forgot to do so overnight. 2. in one bowl, cream together the 300ml room temperature butter, 240ml packed dark brown sugar, and 120ml granulated sugar. 3. whip for about a minute and a half until the mixture becomes fluffy and lighter in color. 4. add one large egg, two teaspoons vanilla extract, and 15ml dark molasses to the butter mixture. 5. in another bowl, sift together 360ml all purpose flour, 5ml baking soda, 2ml salt, 4ml cinnamon, and 1ml ground cloves, nutmeg, or pumpkin spice. 6. add 720ml quick cooking oats to the dry ingredients and whisk to combine. 7. add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients a little at a time, mixing by hand and lightly folding until just combined without overworking the dough. 8. form equal 85g balls of dough. 9. bake at 375 degrees for 11 minutes. 10. remove from the oven and leave the cookies on the baking sheet for 3 minutes before transferring to a cooling rack. 11. for the filling, combine 180ml room temperature butter and 720ml of sifted confectionery sugar in a bowl and mix. 12. add 8ml vanilla extract and mix. 13. add up to 45ml heavy cream to reach your preferred consistency. 14. whip the filling for 4 minutes until fluffy. 15. add salt to taste, about a pinch or two. 16. once the cookies are cooled, assemble them into sandwiches with the filling.

title: Old Fashioned Potato Knishes – Kosher From Jerusalem
text: old fashioned potato knishes – kosher from jerusalem <https://kosherfromjerusalem.com/2020/12/14/old-fashioned-potato-knishes/ --- [](https://kosherfromjerusalem.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/img1628-min.jpg "old fashioned potato knishes") growing up in new york, there were certain foods that you associated with your city. knishes were unquestionably one of them. my late father was a huge fan of kasha and potato knishes and my brother avi to this day loves them. the big shocker is that when i made these (a bunch of times, natch) my mom (!) of all people, said, this should become a regular in your repertoire. frankly, i’m still reeling from the shock. but it gives you an idea of how well these went over. don’t worry, i sent some to avi as well. so i checked out many many recipes for knish dough and was disappointed time and again (cookbooks, online etc.) until lo and behold, i spotted a recipe recommended by deb from smitten kitchen and decided to go to the original guy who crafted it. his name is joe and his website is called joe pastry and the guy is awesome. not only do i love his website but he is personable and professional. he also wrote me back and is very encouraging. way to go joe! (sorry, i couldn’t help myself 🙂 ). and so, i finally have an awesome knish recipe. this dough is actually ridiculously easy to make, no yeast, no worries, and all you need is the patience of letting it rest for an hour. yes, yep, nothing to be done about that, ya gotta do it. if you don’t let it rest, the dough will just not be properly workable but if you do (you are relaxing the gluten in the dough), promise! it’s a pleasure. adult playdough if you get me. so you should start with the dough since you need that resting time. it’s done in a bowl, no mixer or processor needed. take your flour, baking powder and salt and whisk briefly in a medium bowl, preferably one with a lid. whisking dry ingredients together then make a well (sorta a little crater in the middle of the flour mixture) and put the egg, oil, water and vinegar in it, and mix it all up till incorporated. mixing wet ingredients with dry stir it up till it looks like so: knish dough if there’s a bit of flour on the bottom of your bowl, no worries, since right in the bowl, using your hands, you should knead the dough about 6 times, (fold and press, 1/4 turn and again) and then take the lid and close it. otherwise, take some plastic wrap and cover. dough resting in bowl with lid set aside (you might want to time it to be sure, 1 hour, no cheating). a note, it might “weep” a little oil. no worries, just stir back in. now if you’ve been doing the sauteeing of onions and storing the extras in your fridge or freezer as i recommend basic sauteed onions, a kitchen staple, you’ve saved a step. otherwise, you need to sautee an onion. no big, do so and on to your potato filling. peel about 5 medium potatoes and chunk or cube them (the faster to cook them, m’dear) put in a pot with salt, cover with boiling water and cook on medium simmer till really truly soft. we are gonna mash ’em. into a bowl and whip out your potato masher (or a fork if you ain’t got one). a note. do not, no no no put potatoes into a food processor or blender. they get a gummy texture and are just gross. mashing will go fast if they are really soft (check with a toothpick to be sure). mashing those suckers next add your sauteed onions and salt and this may seem odd but is not, beat a large egg and put 1/2 (yes, half) the egg into the mixture. you are saving the other half to brush on top of the knish when ready. mix it all about. mixing the potato filling see the other half of the egg? yup for real. okay. your filling is ready to roll, and yuk yuk, so is your dough so now preheat your oven to 177°c. now take the rested dough and divide into four pieces, covering the ones you aren’t working with, sprinkle some flour on parchment paper, take a rolling pin and roll into a rectangle. the dough is soft and will roll nice and thin. roll dough into rectangle now scoop up a quarter of your potato filling and place in a line on the bottom of the dough nearest you. leave a bit of a margin. like so: place filling on dough brush the flour away and roll the first bit of dough over the filling and then, using the parchment paper, lift it up a bit and the dough should just roll over and over covering the filling a number of times. if it doesn’t work for you, just gently roll it up yourself with your hands. your dough should look like this: rolling the dough and then this: dough log now take the dough and sort of pat the filling so it is even and with your fingers, pinch the dough evenly so it looks like this: pinching the dough i didn’t want mammoth size knishes so this was perfect for me. as you wish. next twist the end piece of dough/knish to sort of tie it off from its mates. twisted dough after twisting, cut with a sharp knife to separate. then stand them up on their little bottoms and gently press down and push your index finger lightly into the middle. presto, you’ve made a knish. with a little practice you will become an expert. do this with all the dough (you might have a little filling left over, serve beef or chicken on it, don’t let it go to waste!) and put on parchment lined rimmed baking sheet. remember the 1/2 an egg? now use it and brush the knishes to glaze them. this makes them brown nicely in the oven. bake in the hot oven 30-40 minutes or till golden brown. serve with brown mustard and astound your family! click here to print recipe old fashioned potato knishes dough: 480ml (312 grams) all-purpose flour 5ml baking powder 5ml salt 1 large egg 120ml canola oil 120ml lukewarm water 5ml vinegar filling: 5 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks boiling water to cover pinch of salt one medium onion, peeled and chopped 30ml oil 1 large egg 5ml salt extra flour to sprinkle on parchment paper or silpat ingredients instructions preheat the oven to 177°c/180 c. in a medium bowl (best if it has its own cover, otherwise you will need plastic wrap), whisk together your dry ingredients, make a well in the center of the flour mixture and add the egg, oil, vinegar and water. stir together till all the ingredients are incorporated and then right in the bowl, knead the dough about six times, just pressing and turning to make sure all the ingredients have been properly mixed. cover the bowl with the lid or plastic wrap and let the dough sit for an hour at room temperature. set aside. prepare the filling by boiling the potatoes with the pinch of salt till very soft. put potatoes in a bowl to cool. sautee the onions in the oil till medium brown and add to the potatoes and mash together and add a teaspoon of salt. stir well. when filling is cool, beat the egg and pour half the egg into the potato mixture saving the other half to brush on the finished knishes. divide the rested dough into 4 parts. roll out the dough on a floured piece of parchment paper into a rectangle and along the bottom of the dough (short side) leaving a bit of a margin, place a layer of potato filling. encase the filling with one turn of dough and then using the parchment paper, lift up the edge and gently roll and the dough should fold over itself like a jelly roll. pinch the dough at intervals (i did 4-5 knishes from a rectangle of dough) and twist. cut at the twist, pinch the ends shut and sit on their bottoms, gently poking the top to help seal and make a small indentation. place on parchment paper on rimmed baking sheet, brush with the remaining egg mixture, and do this with the rest of dough and filling. if you have filling left over, serve as a side dish. bake the knishes 30-40 minutes or till golden brown. serve with mustard, of course 🙂 . a note, these reheat beautifully and will keep (ha! try it and see how long they last) at least 5 days in the fridge. <https://joepastry.com/2009/thetradishknish/ ! title: Onion Rings
text: onion rings ingredients - 4 large white onions - 700 ml milk - 2 eggs - 15ml dijon mustard - 500 grams all-purpose flour - 1 level tablespoon salt - 15ml smoked paprika - 15ml garlic powder - 15ml baking powder - panko breadcrumbs - breadcrumbs - oil for frying (170°c) instructions 1. cut four large white onions into thick rings and carefully separate them so they don't break. 2. in a large bowl, combine 500 grams flour, salt, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and baking powder and mix well. 3. in a separate bowl, whisk together 700 ml milk, dijon mustard, and 2 eggs. 4. add the flour mixture to the wet ingredients and mix thoroughly. 5. heat oil to 170°c. 6. dip each onion ring in plain flour, then dip in the batter, and then coat with panko breadcrumbs mixed with breadcrumbs. 7. fry the coated rings in hot oil for approximately 1 minute on each side until golden brown.

title: Overnight Baked Blueberry Muffin Oatmeal
text: overnight baked blueberry muffin oatmeal source: abeautifulmess.com ingredients - 1¾ cups old-fashioned oats - 60ml sugar - 5ml baking powder - 1ml salt - 1½ cups milk - 1 egg - 30ml melted and cooled butter - 5ml vanilla extract - 240ml blueberries - 60ml cold butter - 60ml sugar - 60ml all-purpose flour instructions 1. in a large bowl, stir together the oats, sugar, baking powder, and salt. 2. in a smaller bowl, stir together the milk, egg, melted and cooled butter, and vanilla extract. 3. combine the wet ingredients with the dry in the large bowl and stir to combine, then stir in the blueberries. 4. add this mixture to a pie pan, cover and store overnight in the refrigerator. 5. in a small bowl, cut together the crumb topping ingredients until the mixture is crumbly like small peas you can press together, then store overnight or make in the morning. 6. top the oatmeal with the crumb topping and bake at 177°c for 30-35 minutes, or set under the broiler for a minute or two if the crumb topping doesn't look golden brown and slightly crispy.

title: Overnight Waffle
text: overnight waffle ingredients - 480ml all-purpose flour - 240ml sourdough starter (unfed/discard) - 30ml sugar - 480ml buttermilk - 2 large eggs - 60ml vegetable oil or 60ml melted butter - 4ml salt - 5ml baking soda instructions 1. the night before, combine flour, sourdough starter, sugar, and buttermilk in a large bowl and stir until smooth. 2. cover the bowl loosely and let rest at room temperature overnight for 8–12 hours. 3. in the morning, whisk together eggs, oil or butter, salt, and baking soda in a small bowl. 4. add the egg mixture to the sponge and stir gently until just combined. 5. for waffles, pour batter into a preheated, greased waffle iron and cook according to manufacturer's instructions until golden and crisp. 6. serve immediately and keep finished waffles warm in a 93°c oven while cooking remaining batches.

title: Pickled Artichokes
text: pickled artichokes ingredients - 4 lemons (juice used for prep and brine) - 240ml white vinegar - 120ml olive oil - 4 garlic cloves, thinly sliced - 2 dried chiles - a dozen juniper berries (optional) - 1 bay leaf - 10ml sea salt - 25 baby artichokes instructions 1. prepare an acidulated water bath by filling a large bowl with cold water, squeezing in the juice of 2 lemons, and dropping in the squeezed lemon halves. 2. trim the baby artichokes by removing the tough outer leaves, cutting off the top third, trimming the stem, and halving or quartering them, then immediately drop into the lemon water to prevent browning. 3. make the brine by combining vinegar, olive oil, juice of remaining 2 lemons, garlic, dried chiles, juniper berries, bay leaf, and sea salt in a large saucepan and bringing to a boil. 4. drain the artichokes and add to the boiling brine, then cook for 5–7 minutes until just tender but not mushy. 5. pack artichokes into sterilized mason jars, ladle brine over them, and seal, then process in a water bath for 15 minutes for shelf-stable storage or refrigerate immediately.

title: Paneer
text: paneer ingredients - full fat milk - lemon juice or vinegar - cheesecloth instructions 1. heat milk to 80–85 degrees celsius using a food thermometer, being careful not to let it boil or overflow. 2. add lemon juice or vinegar one teaspoon at a time, stirring for a minute between each addition. 3. use a maximum of 30ml of lemon juice or vinegar per liter of milk. 4. stop adding the acidic agent once the milk has started curdling well. 5. pour the curdled milk through cheesecloth to strain. 6. place the curds in cheesecloth and apply approximately 10 kg of weight on top to press the paneer.

title: Pastila
text: pastila source: atlas obscura ingredients - 6 large apples (granny smith if antonovka unavailable) - 180ml granulated sugar - 2 egg whites - powdered sugar for dusting instructions 1. preheat your oven to 177°c, wash the apples, place them in a shallow oven-safe dish with ¼ inch of water at the bottom, and roast for an hour until golden, saggy, and wrinkly. 2. remove the apples from the oven and allow them to cool completely, then scrape the skins and cores to create soft, seed-free puree and process in a blender until smooth. 3. put the puree, egg whites, and granulated sugar in a stand mixer bowl and whip for 10 minutes, scraping down the sides occasionally. 4. preheat the oven to 82°c or the lowest setting and line a cookie sheet with parchment paper. 5. stop the mixer once the puree has nearly quadrupled in size and formed a thick white foam, then scrape the foam into the pan, reserving about a cup and a half in the fridge. 6. spread the remaining foam in the pan evenly and leave it in the oven for 4 to 6 hours until it is dry to the touch and solid enough to pick up as one sheet without being extremely floppy. 7. remove the pastila from the oven and allow it to cool completely before peeling away the parchment paper. 8. with a knife dipped in hot water, cut the pastila into three identical rectangles and use the reserved puree as glue to stack the three pieces on top of each other, patching any holes or pits. 9. return the stacked pastila to the oven on a parchment-lined baking sheet for an hour and a half until the layers have molded together, then remove and allow to cool. 10. rub the cooled pastila all over with powdered sugar and carefully slice through the layers in inch-long increments, then store in a sealed container.

title: Pecan Pie Cheesecake
text: pecan pie cheesecake source: bakedbyanintrovert.com ingredients for the crust - 480ml graham cracker crumbs, about 18 whole crackers - 240ml pecans, finely ground - 60ml light brown sugar, packed - 120ml unsalted butter, melted for the filling - 454g cream cheese, softened - 120ml granulated sugar - 120ml sour cream, room temperature - 15ml vanilla extract - 1ml salt - 2 large eggs, room temperature, lightly beaten for the topping - 240ml light brown sugar, packed - 160ml dark corn syrup - 15ml dark rum - 60ml unsalted butter - 3 large eggs - 60ml heavy cream - 1ml salt - 600ml coarsely chopped pecans instructions 1. move the oven rack to the middle position and heat the oven to 177°c. 2. line the inside bottom and sides of a 9-inch springform pan with parchment paper or aluminum foil and spray lightly with nonstick spray. 3. wrap foil around the outside bottom and set aside. 4. stir the graham cracker crumbs, ground pecans, brown sugar, and melted butter together until it resembles wet sand. 5. press the crumb mixture into the bottom and up the sides of the prepared pan, making sure it reaches at least ¾ of the way up the sides. 6. bake the crust for 10 minutes and set aside to cool. 7. reduce the oven temperature to 149°c. 8. beat the cream cheese with an electric mixer on medium to medium-high speed until smooth and creamy, about 1 minute. 9. add the sugar, sour cream, vanilla, and salt, and beat on medium speed until well combined. 10. gently stir in the eggs using a silicone spatula just until combined. 11. pour the batter into the prepared crust and spread evenly with an offset spatula. 12. bake the cheesecake for 40 minutes. 13. while the cheesecake is baking, combine the brown sugar, corn syrup, rum, and butter in a medium saucepan. 14. cook over medium heat until it reaches a boil, stirring constantly, then continue to boil for 2 minutes. 15. remove from heat and let cool while the cheesecake is baking. 16. whisk the eggs, salt, and cream together in a small bowl and set aside. 17. once the cheesecake has baked for 40 minutes, remove it from the oven. 18. slowly whisk the egg mixture with the cooled sugar syrup until well combined. 19. stir in the chopped pecans. 20. gently spoon the pecan topping over the cheesecake, adding the pecans first and then just enough syrup to fill the crust. 21. return the cheesecake to the oven and bake for another 40 to 50 minutes until the top is golden brown and crisp, covering the edges with foil if they are over-browning. 22. transfer to a wire rack and cool completely. 23. cover the cheesecake and refrigerate for at least 4 hours before serving. 24. slowly loosen the sides of the springform pan and carefully transfer the cheesecake to a serving platter. 25. freeze the cheesecake for 1 to 2 hours before slicing for neater slices. 26. run a sharp knife under hot water and carefully dry the blade, then make a cut in the cheesecake, repeating this process for each slice. 27. if you froze the cheesecake before slicing, let the slices sit at room temperature for 30 minutes before serving.

title: Perfect Pumpkin Pie
text: perfect pumpkin pie source: allrecipes.com ingredients - 1 (15-ounce) can pumpkin puree - 1 (14-ounce) can eagle brand sweetened condensed milk - 2 large eggs - 5ml ground cinnamon - 2ml ground ginger - 2ml ground nutmeg - 2ml salt - 1 (9-inch) unbaked pie crust instructions 1. gather all ingredients and preheat the oven to 218°c (220 degrees c). 2. whisk pumpkin puree, condensed milk, eggs, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, and salt together in a medium bowl until smooth. 3. pour into crust. bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. 4. reduce oven temperature to 177°c (175 degrees c) and continue baking until a knife inserted 1 inch from the crust comes out clean, 35 to 40 minutes. let cool before serving. 5. enjoy!

title: Pickled Tongue Recipe
text: pickled tongue recipe source: seriouseats.com ingredients - 1 calves or beef tongue - 3 quarts water - 255g brown sugar - 765g coarse sea salt - 5ml black peppercorns - 5ml juniper berries - 2 cloves - 1 bouquet garni - 1 carrot, chopped - 1 onion, chopped - 1 celery stalk, chopped - 1 garlic bulb, halved instructions 1. put all the ingredients from the brine into a large saucepan and stir well over low heat until the sugar and salt have dissolved. 2. bring the brine to a boil, then turn off the heat and leave to cool. 3. place the tongue in a plastic container and pour the brine over the tongue, using something heavy such as a ceramic bowl to weigh down the tongue in the liquid. 4. refrigerate for 4 to 5 days. 5. on the fifth day, remove the tongue from the brine and soak in fresh water overnight in the refrigerator. 6. place the salted tongue in a pot along with the simmering ingredients. 7. bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 3.5 to 5 hours, depending on the kind of tongue and the size. 8. peel away the rubbery lining when the tongue is very soft. 9. serve the tongue, both hot and cold, with horseradish and mustard.

title: Pickling Spice
text: pickling spice ingredients - 30ml black peppercorns - 30ml mustard seeds - 30ml coriander seeds - 30ml crushed red pepper flakes - 30ml allspice berries - 15ml ground mace - 2 small cinnamon sticks, crushed or broken into pieces - 2 to 4 bay leaves, crumbled - 30ml whole cloves - 15ml ground ginger instructions 1. combine all spices together in a container for use in pickling recipes.

title: Pickling Spices
text: pickling spices ingredients - 15ml whole allspice berries - 15ml whole mustard seeds (brown or yellow) - 15ml coriander seeds - 15ml red pepper flakes - 15ml whole black peppercorns - 10ml whole cloves - 9 whole cardamom pods - 6 large bay leaves, crumbled - 10ml ground ginger - 1/2 stick cinnamon instructions mix all spices together and use for pickling vegetables or other foods.

title: Pipitada (Melon Seed Drink)
text: pipitada (melon seed drink) ingredients - 240ml sweet melon seeds - 720ml water - 30ml caster (superfine) sugar - 15ml orange blossom water instructions 1. grind the seeds to a fine powder in a food processor a day before you want to serve. 2. put the ground seeds in cheesecloth, bring the corners together and tie securely. 3. fill a bowl with about 720ml of water and immerse the ground seeds in their cheesecloth bag in the water. 4. leave in the fridge overnight, squeezing the cheesecloth from time to time to release the milky essence from the seeds into the water. 5. squeeze the cloth tightly to extract as much moisture as possible out of the seeds and discard the seeds. 6. add the sugar and orange blossom water to the milky liquid and refrigerate in a pitcher. 7. serve chilled.

title: Polish Cheese Cake
text: polish cheese cake source: null ingredients - 175 grams white sugar - 110 grams butter - 1 egg - 240ml sour cream - 5ml vanilla extract - 375 grams flour - 5ml baking soda - 5ml baking powder - 500 grams 9% white cheese - 100 grams white sugar - 1 egg - 110 grams brown sugar - 42 grams flour - 80 grams butter - 65 grams pecans instructions 1. preheat oven to 175 degrees c. 2. grease a 9x13-inch baking dish. 3. beat 175 grams white sugar, 110 grams butter, and 1 egg in a bowl until smooth. 4. add sour cream and vanilla extract, then mix well. 5. stir in 375 grams flour, baking soda, and baking powder until mixture comes together in a sticky dough. 6. spread half the dough evenly into the prepared baking dish. 7. beat white cheese, 100 grams white sugar, and 1 egg in another bowl until smooth. 8. spoon the cheese mixture into the baking dish over the dough. 9. drop remaining half of dough by spoonfuls over the cheese mixture. 10. mix pecans, brown sugar, 42 grams flour, and 80 grams butter in a bowl until mixture resembles a coarse crumble. 11. sprinkle the crumble mixture over the dough. 12. bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, about 45 minutes.

title: Pot Roast
text: pot roast source: recipetineats.com ingredients - 2 kg / 1.8kg beef chuck roast , rolled ((note 1)) - 5ml each salt and pepper - 30ml olive oil - 1 onion ((large), cut into large dice) - 5 garlic cloves (, peeled and smashed (note 2a)) - 5 carrots (, peeled and cut into 2.5cm/1" pieces) - 3 celery stalks (, cut into 4 cm / 1.5" pieces) - 240ml (250ml) dry red wine ((sub with beef broth)) - 720ml (750ml) beef broth (, salt reduced) - 80ml (50g) flour ((plain / all purpose) (gf - note 2b)) - 5ml dried rosemary - 8ml dried thyme - 750g / 680g potatoes (, peeled and cut into 2.5 cm / 1" pieces) instructions 1. pat beef dry with paper towels. sprinkle generously with salt and pepper all over. 2. heat oil in a skillet over high heat. brown aggressively all over - a deep dark brown crust is essential for flavour base! should take about 7 minutes. 3. transfer beef to slow cooker. 4. in the same skillet, add onion and garlic. cook for 2 minutes until onion is browned. 5. add wine, reduce by half. transfer to slow cooker. 6. mix together flour and about 240ml of the broth. lumps is fine. pour into slow cooker. 7. add remaining broth, carrots, celery, rosemary and thyme into slow cooker. 8. cover and slow cook on low for 5 hours. (45 min pressure cook on high, note 3a for oven and stove) 9. add potato, slow cook on low for 3 hours. (10 min pressure cooker on high, note 3b) 10. remove beef. rest for 5 minutes, then slice thickly. 11. adjust salt and pepper of sauce to taste. 12. serve beef with vegetables and plenty of sauce! bread also terrific for mopping up sauce - try these no knead dinner rolls, no yeast irish soda bread or these fabulous cheese muffins.

title: Pumpkin Roll
text: pumpkin roll source: ohsodelicioso.com ingredients - 240ml sugar - 180ml flour - 5ml baking powder - 5ml ginger - 5ml nutmeg - 2ml cloves - 2ml salt - 10ml cinnamon - 3 eggs - 160ml pumpkin - 720ml powder sugar - 227g cream cheese - 60ml butter - 2ml vanilla - 1-30ml milk or heavy cream instructions 1. sift flour, sugar and seasonings, and baking powder in a large bowl. add eggs and pumpkin. mix until combined. 2. pour and smooth evenly into a standard sized sheet pan lined with parchment paper. 3. bake at 375 degs for 12 mins. 4. while cake is still warm and sprinkle a light layer of powder sugar over. invert on to clean tea towel and roll up. let cool until room temperature or in refrigerator.  5. when cooled spread cream cheese filling evenly over inverted cake. gently roll cake. 6. place on large platter and sprinkle with powder sugar. 7. refrigerate and serve chilled. 8. cream together butter and cream cheese at room temp, add in vanilla and powder sugar. beat all ingredients till creamy and smooth.

title: Pumpkin Scones
text: pumpkin scones ingredients - 250g pumpkin or butternut squash, peeled and seeded - 400g plain flour - 20ml baking powder - 2ml salt - 85g butter - 80g parmesan, grated - 100ml milk - 100ml water - 10ml grain mustard - 1 egg, beaten, for glazing - black pepper to taste instructions 1. cut the pumpkin into large chunks and steam for 7-10 minutes until tender. 2. mix the flour, baking powder and salt in a bowl. 3. cut the butter into small chunks and rub it in with your fingertips until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs. 4. stir in the grated parmesan. 5. roughly crush the cooked pumpkin with a fork or potato masher, taking care not to reduce it to a smooth purée. 6. lightly stir in the grain mustard and a grinding of black pepper to the pumpkin. 7. add the pumpkin mixture to the flour mixture, then pour in the milk and water. 8. stir the liquids into the flour, season with black pepper and mix the ingredients carefully, taking great care not to overmix. 9. turn the dough out onto a floured board and pat it into a circle roughly 3cm thick. 10. using a 5-6cm biscuit cutter, make 12 to 14 scones and place them well apart from one another on a baking sheet. 11. brush the top of each scone with beaten egg, taking care not to let any drip down the sides. 12. bake for 12-14 minutes until they are golden. 13. remove the scones from the oven and let them rest briefly before transferring them to a cooling rack. 14. serve warm, preferably with quince jelly.

title: Quiche Flaky Dough
text: quiche flaky dough ingredients - 180 gr all purpose flour - 1ml kosher salt - 100 gr unsalted butter, cold, cut into cubes - 45ml ice cold water instructions no instructions provided.

title: Quinine-free Tonic Water
text: quinine-free tonic water ingredients - zest of half a lime - zest of half a lemon - 8ml citric acid - 5ml gentian root - 8 juniper berries, crushed - pinch of spice (allspice, chinese five spice, cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, or chili pepper) - 180 ml water - 25ml sugar instructions 1. add zest, citric acid, gentian root, crushed juniper berries, and spice to a small saucepan. 2. bring to the boil and simmer for 20 minutes. 3. strain the mixture through a fine sieve. 4. stir in sugar, ensuring it dissolves completely. 5. allow to cool completely. 6. bottle and keep refrigerated. 7. to drink, mix 3:1 or 4:1 with soda or sparkling water.

title: Ratatouille
text: ratatouille source: tasty ingredients - 2 eggplants - 6 roma tomatoes - 2 yellow squashes - 2 zucchinis - 30ml olive oil - 1 medium white onion, diced - 4 cloves garlic, minced - 1 red bell pepper, seeded and diced - 1 yellow bell pepper, seeded and diced - kosher salt, to taste - freshly ground black pepper, to taste - 794g crushed tomatoes (795 g) - 30ml thinly sliced fresh basil - 30ml thinly sliced fresh basil - 5ml minced garlic - 30ml finely chopped fresh parsley - 10ml fresh thyme leaves - 60ml olive oil instructions 1. preheat the oven to 191°c (190°c). 2. using a sharp knife or a mandoline, slice the eggplant, tomatoes, squash, and zucchini into approximately 1/16-inch (1-mm)-thick rounds, then set aside. 3. heat the olive oil in a 12-inch (30-cm) oven-safe pan over medium-high heat and sauté the onion, garlic, and bell peppers until soft, about 10 minutes. 4. season with salt and pepper, then add the crushed tomatoes and stir until the ingredients are fully incorporated. 5. remove from heat and add the basil, then stir once more and smooth the surface of the sauce with a spatula. 6. arrange the veggies in alternating slices (for example, eggplant, tomato, squash, zucchini) on top of the sauce, working from the outer edge to the center of the pan. 7. season the vegetables with salt and pepper. 8. in a small bowl, mix together the basil, garlic, parsley, thyme, salt, pepper, and olive oil to make the herb seasoning. 9. spoon the herb seasoning over the vegetables. 10. cover the pan with foil and bake for 40 minutes. 11. uncover and bake for another 20 minutes until the vegetables are softened. 12. serve hot as a main dish or side, or cover with foil and reheat in a 177°c (180°c) oven for 15 minutes the next day.

title: Boiled Corn Bread (Puttuckqunnege)
text: boiled corn bread (puttuckqunnege) source: wampanoag ingredients - 1 quart slightly boiled water (this water can be a broth from boiled greens) - 120ml cornmeal - 120ml corn flour - 120ml dried cranberries, blueberries, and/or currants - 120ml crushed nuts or seeds (walnuts, hazelnuts, or sunflower seeds) - maple syrup or sugar to taste (optional) instructions 1. combine all ingredients in large bowl and mix thoroughly. 2. after mixing, slowly add a spoonful at a time of slightly boiled water. 3. when the mix is thick enough to be sticky, shape round patties (about 3 inches in diameter and 1/2 inch thick). 4. return water to slight rolling boil and drop in 1 or 2 patties, carefully making sure they do not stick to the bottom. 5. remove breads when they begin to float.

title: Roasted Sweet Potatoes
text: roasted sweet potatoes source: chelseasmessyapron.com ingredients - 907g sweet potatoes (about 3 large, i like red garnet or jewel sweet potatoes best, peeled and cut into 1/2-inch pieces) - 30ml melted coconut oil - 4ml fine sea salt (use less if using table salt) - 15ml light brown sugar (firmly packed) - 907g sweet potatoes (about 3 large, peeled and cut into 1/2-inch pieces) - 30ml olive oil - 4ml fine sea salt (use less if using table salt) - 1ml pepper - 2ml ground chili powder (see note 1) - 2ml paprika - 2ml ground cumin - 2ml garlic powder instructions 1. plain roasted sweet potatoes: preheat oven to 218°c. peel and cube sweet potatoes into 1/2-inch pieces. add to your largest sheet pan and add the melted coconut oil, salt, and brown sugar on top. toss to coat all the sweet potatoes, then spread out in an even layer. you don’t want any potatoes overlapping or you’ll end up with steamed potatoes instead of roasted potatoes. flip every 10–15 minutes, cooking for a total of 27–35 minutes. (i flip every 10 minutes and bake around 30 minutes.) 2. seasoned roasted sweet potatoes: preheat oven to 218°c. peel and cube sweet potatoes into 1/2-inch pieces. add to your largest sheet pan and add the olive oil, salt, pepper, chili powder, paprika, cumin, and garlic powder on top. toss to coat all the sweet potatoes, then spread out in an even layer. you don’t want any potatoes overlapping or you’ll end up with steamed potatoes instead of roasted potatoes. flip every 10–15 minutes, cooking for a total of 27–35 minutes. (i flip every 10 minutes and bake around 30 minutes.)

title: Root Beer Recipe From Scratch
text: root beer recipe from scratch ingredients - 1l water - 35g fresh ginger, unpeeled and chopped - 5g cinnamon stick - 20g dried sassafras root bark - 10g dried sarsaparilla root - 10g dried liquorice root - 7g dried cherry bark - 2 ml salt - 450g demerara brown sugar - 75g lactose (optional) - 15 ml vanilla extract - 75 ml active ginger bug (for every 2l) or 10ml beer yeast instructions 1. mix 1 part syrup to 3 parts water. 2. mix in active ginger bug or beer yeast. 3. pour into pressure safe bottles, filling to within 2 inches of top but no higher. 4. cap and set aside at room temperature to let ferment for 2 to 3 days. 5. check fermentation and then chill or store in refrigerator.

title: Soft Sourdough Rolls with Tangzhong
text: soft sourdough rolls with tangzhong ingredients - 145 g whole wheat flour - 160 g כפרי flour - 500 g bread flour - 35 g all-purpose flour - 530 g water - 175 g milk - 220 g levain (100% hydration) - 45 g butter - 30 g honey - 16 g salt instructions 1. combine 35 g flour and 175 g milk, then cook until thick pudding consistency and cool completely for the tangzhong. 2. mix the remaining 805 g flour, 355 g water, and all tangzhong until shaggy and rest for 1-4 hours for the autolyse. 3. add 220 g levain, 16 g salt, and 30 g honey to the autolyse and mix until combined and moderately developed. 4. add 45 g butter in pieces during the first fold, then perform 2-3 more folds every 30 minutes and bulk until approximately 40-50% rise. 5. divide dough into 15 portions of approximately 120 g each, shape into balls, and refrigerate overnight covered. 6. bake at 200°c for 15-18 minutes, optionally brushing with egg wash before baking and butter after baking.

title: Spice Squares with Molasses Whipped Cream
text: spice squares with molasses whipped cream ingredients - 600ml sifted cake flour - 2ml baking soda - 10ml baking powder - 1ml allspice - 1ml mace - 1ml nutmeg - 2ml cloves - 10ml cinnamon - 120ml butter or other shortening - 240ml brown sugar, firmly packed - 2 eggs, well beaten - 240ml sour milk or buttermilk - 30ml molasses - 120ml heavy cream, whipped instructions 1. sift flour once, measure, add soda, baking powder, and spices, and sift together three times. 2. cream butter thoroughly, add sugar gradually, and cream together until light and fluffy. 3. add eggs, mixing well. 4. add flour mixture alternately with milk, a small amount at a time, beating after each addition until smooth. 5. bake in a greased 8x8x2 inch pan in a moderate oven at 177°c for 50 minutes. 6. make molasses whipped cream by folding 30ml molasses into 120ml whipped cream. 7. serve cake in squares with molasses whipped cream.

title: Saffron Vanilla Donuts
text: saffron vanilla donuts source: instagram ingredients - 60g sugar - 23g cornstarch - 4 egg yolks - pinch of salt - 360g whole milk - 1 vanilla bean pod - 25g unsalted butter - 150g heavy whipping cream, cold - 0.25g saffron - 10g sugar - 30g whole milk, hot - 445g bread flour - 55g sugar - 7g salt - 185g whole milk, at 27c - 1 whole egg plus 1 yolk - 12g instant dry yeast - 70g unsalted butter, softened and cubed - frying oil - extra sugar instructions 1. whisk together egg yolks, sugar, cornstarch, and salt for the diplomat cream. 2. cut the vanilla pod in half and scrape off the beans. 3. add milk and vanilla to a pot and heat over medium heat until tiny bubbles form. 4. remove from heat and slowly pour the hot milk over the egg mixture a little at a time while whisking. 5. place a strainer over the pot and strain everything back into the pot. 6. heat over medium heat while constantly whisking until the mixture thickens. 7. remove from heat and mix in butter. 8. transfer to a bowl and cover with plastic wrap that touches the surface of the pastry cream, then refrigerate for at least an hour. 9. add saffron threads to a mortar and pestle and grind until they break down. 10. add 10g of sugar and continue grinding into a fine powder. 11. add 30g of hot milk to the saffron mixture and stir, then rest for 15 minutes. 12. add all dough ingredients except butter to the bowl of a stand mixer and knead on low for 10 minutes. 13. add butter one cube at a time to the dough. 14. knead for 10-20 minutes on low-medium until the dough passes the window-pane test. 15. proof the dough for about 90 minutes. 16. divide the dough into 15 pieces of 60g each and roll into balls. 17. arrange the dough balls on parchment paper squares and proof for 30 minutes. 18. fry the donuts at 171°c/170c for 2 minutes on each side. 19. transfer fried donuts to paper towels and toss in sugar. 20. whisk 150g of cold whipping cream to soft peaks and combine with the cooled pastry cream. 21. fill the donuts with the diplomat cream and serve.

title: Scotch Cookies
text: scotch cookies source: cushman's bakery ingredients - 360ml sugar - 240ml butter - 120ml molasses - 1 egg - 840ml flour - 5ml salt - 12ml baking soda - 5ml cinnamon - 5ml mace - 60ml milk instructions 1. cream sugar, shortening, molasses and egg together. 2. sift dry ingredients and beat in along with the milk. 3. drop by tablespoon onto greased sheets. 4. press down lightly with floured glass. 5. bake at 175°c for a maximum of 14 minutes, being careful not to overbake.

title: Scottish Fried Chicken
text: scottish fried chicken source: null ingredients - 480ml apple cider - 120ml salt - 1 (4 1/2 to 5-pound) chicken, cut into 10 pieces - water - 2 eggs - 30ml cayenne pepper - 5ml freshly ground black pepper - 240ml all-purpose flour - 60ml cornstarch - 2 quarts vegetable shortening, for frying instructions 1. in a large bowl, whisk together cider and salt until salt dissolves. 2. add chicken pieces and enough water to coat and soak 1 hour to overnight in the refrigerator until chicken is completely submerged in brine. 3. in a large pot, heat vegetable shortening until a deep-fry thermometer reaches 163 degrees celsius. 4. line a sheet tray with a wire rack. 5. in a large bowl, whisk together eggs, cayenne and black pepper. 6. in a paper bag, shake together flour and cornstarch. 7. drain chicken from brine and dip in batches first in egg mixture then in flour mixture to coat. 8. set coated chicken on wire rack to let coating sit for 10 minutes. 9. in 2 batches, fry chicken until golden brown on both sides and cooked through, 15 to 20 minutes depending on the size of the piece. 10. remove chicken from oil and drain on paper towel-lined plate.

title: Secret Ingredient Sourdough Cornbread
text: secret ingredient sourdough cornbread source: the clever carrot ingredients - 115 g (120ml or 1 stick) unsalted butter - 30 ml (30ml) coconut oil - 2 large eggs - 70 g (80ml) granulated sugar - 5ml pure vanilla extract - 100 g (appx. 120ml) sourdough discard - 125 g (240ml lightly spooned & leveled) all purpose flour - 80 g (120ml) medium grind cornmeal - 10ml baking powder - 2ml baking soda - 5ml fine sea salt - 120 ml (120ml) half & half instructions 1. preheat the oven to 191°c and line an 8×8-inch pan with parchment paper. 2. melt the butter and coconut oil together in a small saucepan over low heat and set aside to cool slightly. 3. whisk the eggs, sugar and vanilla together in a large mixing bowl, then pour in the melted butter mixture and whisk well, then add the sourdough discard and mix again. 4. in a separate bowl, combine the flour and cornmeal, then sift the baking powder, baking soda and salt directly over the top and mix to combine. 5. working in batches, add the flour mixture to the wet ingredients using a wooden spoon to incorporate. 6. gradually pour in the half & half until the liquid is fully absorbed, adjusting the consistency as needed so the batter forms slow ribbons when dropped from a spoon. 7. bake on the center rack for 25–28 minutes until the top is golden brown. 8. cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then remove the cornbread (still on the parchment paper) to finish cooling on a wire rack. 9. serve slightly warm or at room temperature.

title: Seville Orange Marmalade
text: seville orange marmalade source: simplyrecipes.com ingredients - 1.4kg seville or bitter oranges (6 to 12 oranges) - 6 to 1920ml water - 2 lemons (preferably 1 regular lemon and 1 meyer lemon) - 5 to 1440ml sugar (or more to taste) instructions 1. scrub the oranges and discard any that are damaged or soft. 2. cut the oranges in half and juice them, saving the seeds in a separate bowl for making natural pectin. 3. cut the peels into narrow strips by using a spoon to dig out segment membranes from the inside of the rind and putting some with the seeds for pectin. 4. use a sharp chef's knife to thinly julienne the peel and combine the cut peels and juice in a large measuring cup. 5. juice the regular lemon and add this juice to the orange peels and juice, saving the seeds for pectin. 6. cut the meyer lemon into eighths lengthwise, remove the seeds and inner membranes, cut the segments into triangular pieces, and add to the measuring cup with the oranges. 7. add the meyer lemon seeds to the seville orange seeds and membranes. 8. put the citrus seeds and membranes into cheesecloth or a muslin jelly bag and tie tightly. 9. place the orange and lemon juices and cut peels into a large thick-bottomed pot and add 1440ml of water. 10. place the cheesecloth or muslin bag containing the citrus seeds and pulp into the pot, submerging it in the liquid and securing the string to the pot handle. 11. bring mixture to a boil and let boil uncovered for 30 minutes or longer until the peels are completely soft and cooked through. 12. test the orange peels by taking a bite to ensure they are not firm, adding more water if needed to prevent sticking. 13. remove from heat and place the pectin bag in a bowl to cool until comfortable to touch. 14. pour the mixture from the pot into a large measuring cup and measure the amount, then return it to the pan. 15. add 210ml of sugar for every cup of mixture and stir until dissolved, tasting and adjusting sweetness as desired. 16. once the pectin bag has cooled, squeeze it like play-doh to extract extra pectin and add about a tablespoon of pectin to the orange mixture. 17. heat the jelly mixture on medium high and bring it to a rapid boil, stirring occasionally and securing a candy thermometer to the side of the pan. 18. once the mixture reaches 103°c, start testing by placing a small amount on a chilled plate and looking for wrinkling when pushed with a finger tip. 19. put several small plates in the freezer to chill and test the marmalade frequently as it approaches setting point. 20. remove the jelly from heat once it wrinkles on a cold plate. 21. sterilize the canning jars by placing them in a large pot on a steaming rack, covering with water by 1 inch, and boiling for 10 minutes, then wash the lids in hot soapy water and dry them. 22. let the jelly sit in the pot for a couple minutes, then carefully ladle the marmalade into the sterilized jars, leaving 1/4 inch head space at the top. 23. wipe the rim clean with a clean wet paper towel, place the lid on the jar, and secure with a jar ring. 24. optionally process the jars in a hot water bath for 5 minutes to help get a better seal and prevent mold. 25. allow the jars to seal on the kitchen counter as the marmalade cools, turning upside down every 30 minutes to prevent the peels from floating to the top. 26. refrigerate any jars that did not seal and use the marmalade within a few months.

title: Simple Sourdough Focaccia
text: simple sourdough focaccia source: alexandracooks.com ingredients - 50 g – 100 g (1/4 to 120ml) active starter, see notes above - 10 g (about 12ml) kosher salt - 430 – 440 g water (420ml – 420ml + 30ml), room temperature, see notes above - 512 g (about 960ml) bread flour, see notes above - 45ml extra-virgin olive oil, divided, plus more for drizzling - nice, flaky sea salt, such as maldon instructions 1. place the starter, salt, and water in a large bowl. stir with a spatula to combine — it doesn’t have to be uniformly mixed. add the flour. mix again until the flour is completely incorporated. 2. if time permits, perform one “fold”: 30 minutes after you mix the dough, reach into the bowl and pull the dough up and into the center. turn the bowl quarter turns and continue this pulling 8 to 10 times. see video for guidance. 3. drizzle with a splash of olive oil and rub to coat. cover bowl with a tea towel or bowl cover and set aside to rise at room temperature (70ºf/21ºc) for 4 to 18 hours (the time will vary depending on the time of year, the strength of your starter, and the temperature of your kitchen — in summer, for instance, my sourdoughs double in 6 hours; in winter, they double in 18 hours. do not use an oven with the light on for the bulk fermentation — it will be too warm. it is best to rely on visual cues (doubling in volume) as opposed to time to determine when the bulk fermentation is done. a straight-sided vessel makes monitoring the bulk fermentation especially easy because it allows you to see when your dough has truly doubled.). 4. when dough has doubled, place 30ml of olive oil into a 9×13-inch pan. (i have been using this usa pan, which i love. i have had no sticking issues. if you are using a glass pan, you may, as a precaution, want to butter it it first — i have had disasters with bread sticking when i’ve used oil alone with other baking vessels.) 5. drizzle dough with a tablespoon of olive oil. use your hand to gently deflate the dough and release it from the sides of the bowl. gently scoop the dough into the center of the pool of oil in your prepared pan. fold dough envelope style from top to bottom and side to side to create a rough rectangle. turn dough over so seam-side is down. video guidance here. 6. rub top of dough with oil. leave alone for 4 to 6 hours, uncovered, or until puffy and nearly doubled. 7. heat oven to 425ºf. rub hands lightly with oil, and using all ten fingers, press gently into the dough to dimple and stretch the dough to nearly fit the pan. sprinkle generously with sea salt. transfer pan to the oven and bake for about 25 minutes or until golden all around. remove pan from oven and transfer bread to a cooling rack. cool at least 20 minutes before slicing.

title: Simple Whole Roasted Chicken
text: simple whole roasted chicken source: allrecipes.com ingredients - 10ml salt - 5ml white sugar - 1ml ground cloves - 1ml ground allspice - 1ml ground nutmeg - 1ml ground cinnamon - 1 whole chicken (1.8kg) - 5 cloves garlic, crushed instructions 1. in a bowl, mix the salt, sugar, cloves, allspice, nutmeg, and cinnamon. 2. rub the chicken with the mixture. 3. cover chicken and place in the refrigerator for 24 hours. 4. preheat oven to 260°c (260 degrees c). 5. stuff the chicken cavity with the garlic. 6. place the chicken, breast side down, on a rack in a roasting pan. 7. roast 15 minutes in the preheated oven. 8. reduce heat to 232°c (230 degrees c) and continue roasting 15 minutes. 9. baste chicken with pan drippings, reduce heat to 218°c (220 degrees c), and continue roasting 30 minutes to an internal temperature of 82°c (85 degrees c). 10. let stand 20 minutes before serving.

title: Slow-Cooked Beef Bourguignon
text: slow-cooked beef bourguignon source: null ingredients - 227g thick-cut bacon (5 to 6 slices), diced - 2 1/2 to 1.4kg beef chuck roast, round roast, or other similar cut, cut into 1-inch cubes - 480ml good red wine, divided - 2 medium yellow onions, thinly sliced - 3 medium carrots, diced - 3 whole stalks celery, diced - 2 cloves garlic, minced - 15ml tomato paste - 3 to 4 sprigs fresh thyme - 1 bay leaf - 240ml chicken or beef broth, plus more if necessary - 454g white button mushrooms, sliced - salt and pepper to taste - chopped parsley for garnish - cooked pasta or crusty baguette for serving instructions 1. warm a stainless steel or cast iron skillet over medium-high heat and add the bacon, cooking until the fat has rendered and the bacon is golden and crispy, then transfer to a paper towel-lined plate to drain. 2. pour off all but a tablespoon of bacon fat from the pan and return the pan to medium-high to high heat. 3. pat the beef cubes dry, sprinkle with salt and pepper, and sear in a single layer in batches without crowding the pan, allowing 1 to 3 minutes per side until golden-brown. 4. transfer the seared meat to your slow cooker or a clean bowl and deglaze the pan with 60ml of wine, scraping up the dark glaze and crispy bits, then pour the wine over the seared meat. 5. continue searing the remaining meat in batches, deglazing between each batch with additional bacon grease and wine. 6. add bacon grease to the pan, reduce heat to medium, and cook the onions with 1ml salt until soft and browned, then add carrots, celery, garlic, and tomato paste and cook until fragrant. 7. transfer the vegetable mixture to the slow cooker or bowl with the meat. 8. cook the mushrooms in the pan with 1ml salt until they release their liquid, the liquid evaporates, and they are golden brown, then transfer to a separate bowl. 9. for slow cooker method: stir the beef and vegetables together with 5ml salt, tuck in the thyme and bay leaf, pour in the stock and remaining wine until liquid comes 3/4 way up the ingredients, cover and cook on low for 6 to 8 hours until beef falls apart easily with a fork. 10. for oven method: preheat oven to 149°c, transfer beef and vegetables to a dutch oven, stir in 5ml salt, tuck in thyme and bay leaf, pour stock and remaining wine so liquid does not quite cover the ingredients, cover and cook for 2 hours then check every 15 minutes until meat falls apart easily with a fork. 11. once the meat is cooked, stir in the reserved bacon and mushrooms and continue cooking on high or simmering until the mushrooms are warmed through, about 10 minutes. 12. serve in bowls over noodles or with crusty bread on the side and sprinkle with parsley before serving.

title: Slow-Roast Gochujang Chicken
text: slow-roast gochujang chicken source: bon appetit ingredients - 3½–4-lb. whole chicken - 15ml. diamond crystal or 1¾ tsp. morton kosher salt, plus more - freshly ground black pepper - 75ml. gochujang (korean hot pepper paste) - 60ml plus 30ml. extra-virgin olive oil - 2 heads of garlic - 1½" piece fresh ginger - 1½ lb. baby yukon gold potatoes (about 1½" in diameter) - 5 scallions - 2 limes - 10ml. honey instructions 1. place a rack in middle of oven and preheat to 300°. 2. pat chicken dry with paper towels and place on a small rimmed baking sheet. 3. season the chicken all over with salt and freshly ground black pepper, making sure to season the inside cavity. 4. whisk gochujang and 60ml extra-virgin olive oil in a medium bowl until combined. 5. finely grate 3 garlic cloves into the gochujang oil. 6. peel and grate the fresh ginger into the gochujang oil and whisk to combine. 7. cut what's left of both heads of garlic in half crosswise. 8. stuff 2 garlic halves inside the cavity of the chicken and tie the legs together with kitchen twine. 9. brush half of the gochujang oil over the chicken using a pastry brush. 10. toss the potatoes, remaining 2 garlic halves, and 30ml. extra-virgin olive oil in the remaining gochujang oil until well coated, then season lightly with salt and pepper. 11. arrange potatoes in a 12" cast-iron skillet, scooting them toward the edges to make space for the chicken. 12. nestle the garlic halves cut sides down in the center of the skillet and place the chicken over the garlic. 13. roast the chicken and potatoes, turning the potatoes once or twice to coat in juices and oil, until the potatoes are very tender and the chicken skin is deep reddish-golden brown, 2½–3 hours. 14. transfer the chicken to a cutting board and let it rest 10–15 minutes. 15. use the back of a large spoon or a potato masher to gently smash the potatoes in the skillet, exposing some of their flesh. 16. thinly slice the scallions on a long diagonal and cut the limes in half. 17. cut one lime half into wedges and set aside. 18. stir the honey and juice of the remaining lime half into the potatoes, taste, and season with more salt if needed. 19. scatter the sliced scallions over the potatoes. 20. carve the chicken and arrange the pieces over the potatoes and scallions, then serve right out of the skillet with the lime wedges alongside.
