loosely cover and leave to rise until at least doubled in size, taking 1-2.5 hours, until pressing the dough gently leaves an indentation that springs back slowly but remains visible. 13. preheat the oven to 180°c and mix together the maple syrup and water in a small bowl. 14. gently brush the top of the risen loaf with the maple syrup mixture, ensuring none drips down the sides. 15. place the loaf in the preheated oven and bake for 30-50 minutes until a probe thermometer reaches 94°c when poked into the middle, covering the top loosely with foil if it browns too quickly. 16. brush the baked bread with more of the glaze, let it cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then lift it onto a wire rack to cool completely before slicing and store in an airtight container.

title: Sourdough Waffles
text: sourdough waffles source: seriouseats.com ingredients - 142g all-purpose flour (240ml, spooned) - 8ml baking powder - 28g granulated sugar (30ml) - 5ml diamond crystal kosher salt - 2 large eggs - 170g whole milk (180ml) - 227g sourdough starter, unfed or discard (240ml) - 43g unsalted butter, melted (45ml), plus more for serving - maple syrup, for serving instructions 1. in a medium bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt until well combined. 2. in a large bowl, whisk together eggs, milk, starter, and melted butter until well combined. 3. add dry mixture to wet mixture and whisk until just combined, adjusting batter consistency with milk if necessary to reach pancake batter consistency. 4. cook in waffle iron according to the manufacturer's directions and serve right away with butter and maple syrup.

title: Sourdough Chocolate Babka
text: sourdough chocolate babka ingredients starter - 80g white wheat flour (bread flour) - 20g brown sugar - 25g active mother sourdough starter - 35g water dough - 350g white wheat flour (bread flour) - all of the above starter (approximately 160g) - 2 eggs (approximately 100g) - 50g brown sugar - 85g unsalted softened butter - 7g salt - 110g milk chocolate filling - 130g melted dark chocolate (70%) - 120g melted butter - 10g cocoa powder - 10g powdered brown sugar - 50g roughly chopped chocolate or chocolate chips (optional) instructions 1. in the morning, prepare your sourdough starter by mixing the white wheat flour, brown sugar, active mother starter, and water, then leave it to ferment until doubled in volume, which may take 4–12 hours depending on temperature and starter strength. 2. in the late afternoon, mix milk, starter, sugar, eggs, flour, and salt together in a large bowl, adding additional liquid only if necessary to incorporate all the flour, then knead for 3–4 minutes and rest for 15–20 minutes. 3. knead in half of the butter quantity, then add and knead in the other half, kneading for 8–10 minutes until smooth and elastic, then shape into a ball and place in a clean bowl covered with plastic wrap. 4. ferment the dough at room temperature for 2 hours, then place the bowl in the fridge overnight. 5. in the morning, prepare the filling by mixing melted chocolate, melted butter, cocoa powder, and powdered sugar together, then refrigerate for at least half an hour until the mixture thickens to a spreadable consistency. 6. prepare two lined tins and remove the dough from the fridge onto a lightly floured surface. 7. roll the dough into a square measuring approximately 45×45 cm and 4–5 mm thick, then spread the filling across the dough leaving a 1–1.5 cm edge, optionally sprinkle chopped chocolate or chips, and tightly roll into a log. 8. cut the log in half lengthwise, place one half over the other, and braid the two halves together, then cut the braided dough to fit the tins. 9. leave the babkas to rise until approximately doubled in volume, which may take 4–7 hours depending on temperature. 10. preheat the oven to 220°c/220°c and bake the babkas for 10 minutes at this temperature, then decrease to 200°c/200°c and bake for another 30–40 minutes until nicely baked. 11. remove the babkas from the tins and leave them to cool on a cooling rack before serving.

title: Sourdough Pita Bread
text: sourdough pita bread ingredients - 500 g all-purpose flour - 300 g water - 100 g sourdough starter - 30 g olive oil - 30 g sugar - 10 g salt instructions 1. mix all ingredients together. 2. perform stretch and fold every 30 minutes for 4 rounds. 3. rest the dough for 2 hours. 4. divide the dough into 100 g portions. 5. use a rolling pin to flatten each portion. 6. rest the flattened dough for 30 minutes to 1 hour. 7. pan bake on medium-low heat for 3 minutes until the pita puffs up. 8. remove from pan and cover with kitchen towels to prevent drying out and keep the bread soft.

title: Sourdough pita bread recipe | Super easy, the best recipe

title: Sourdough Potato Hamburger Buns
text: sourdough potato hamburger buns source: baking-sense.com ingredients - 1 medium (227g, 224g) russet potato - 360ml (340g, 360ml) whole milk - 30ml (28g, 28g) unsalted butter - 30ml (28g, 28g) granulated sugar - 8ml table salt - 1 large egg - 240ml (227g, 224g) active sourdough starter (100% hydration) - 720ml (425g, 425g) bread flour - 1 egg for brushing - sesame seeds for garnish (optional) instructions 1. peel and chop the potato into 1" dice to yield 1 heaping cup of diced potatoes. 2. in a small saucepan, combine the milk and diced potato, bring to a simmer, and cook until the potato is very tender, stirring frequently and watching for boil overs. 3. remove the pan from the heat and transfer the milk to a large mixing bowl or stand mixer bowl. 4. add butter and use a fork or potato masher to mash the potato into the milk. 5. add the sugar, salt, and egg, then check the temperature and cool if needed until the mixture is about 43°c or slightly warmer than body temperature. 6. add the sourdough starter and 240ml of the bread flour and mix on low speed to form a thick batter. 7. switch to the dough hook or use a wooden spoon or spatula to mix by hand, adding the remaining bread flour until the dough clings to the hook and clears the sides of the bowl. 8. knead for 5 minutes to develop the dough, then dump onto a floured surface and knead to form a smooth ball that is soft, smooth, and slightly sticky. 9. transfer the dough to a lightly oiled bowl, turning once to coat, cover, and set aside at room temperature for 3 hours, folding the dough over itself every hour to redistribute the yeast. 10. after about 3 hours when the dough is lively, elastic, and airy, turn it out onto a lightly floured surface and knead to form a smooth ball. 11. divide the dough into 10 equal portions and roll each portion into a ball. 12. set the balls on a parchment-lined baking sheet, wet your hands, and flatten each ball to a disc about 1" thick. 13. cover the sheet pan and allow the rolls to rise until almost doubled in size, about 1 1/2 hours or longer if the dough is cold, testing readiness by pressing with your finger to see if the dent slowly fills in. 14. preheat the oven to 204°c while the rolls are rising. 15. brush the tops of the buns with egg and sprinkle each bun generously with sesame seeds. 16. bake until the buns are golden brown and feel light when lifted off the sheet pan, about 10-15 minutes. 17. allow the buns to cool completely before slicing.

title: Soft Sourdough Sandwich Bread
text: soft sourdough sandwich bread ingredients - 300 grams sourdough starter - 650 g warm water - 50 g honey - 40 g avocado oil - 20 g salt - 1000 g bread flour instructions 1. combine all ingredients and let rest for one hour. 2. perform four stretch and folds thirty minutes apart. 3. flour the dough, cover it, and place in the refrigerator overnight for eight to twenty-four hours. 4. remove the dough from the refrigerator and let it rest at room temperature for about two hours. 5. prepare two loaf pans and divide the dough in half. 6. roll and flatten the first loaf into a rectangle, then roll it into a log and place it into a pan. 7. repeat with the remaining dough and score the tops. 8. cover the loaves with a damp towel and rest for one hour. 9. preheat the oven to 205°c and spray the tops of the loaves with water. 10. loosely cover the loaves with foil and bake for thirty-five minutes. 11. remove the foil, reduce the oven temperature to 175°c, and bake for another fifteen minutes until the internal temperature reaches 93°c. 12. allow the loaves to cool before serving.

title: Sourdough Tortillas
text: sourdough tortillas source: milk and pop ingredients - 120 g sourdough starter discard - 120 ml olive oil - 160 ml water - 200 g all-purpose flour - 3 g salt instructions 1. in a large bowl, mix the sourdough discard, olive oil, and water and stir to combine. 2. add the all-purpose flour and salt, mixing until the dough is formed. 3. knead for 1 to 2 minutes until everything is well combined and the dough looks homogeneous with no dry spots. 4. if the dough is too sticky, add 15ml more all-purpose flour and knead until absorbed. 5. cover the dough with a damp towel and let it rest for 30 minutes. 6. preheat a large skillet on high heat. 7. lightly flour the surface you will use for rolling the dough. 8. divide the dough into 8 to 10 pieces and flatten each ball with the palm of your hand. 9. roll each piece of dough into a thin circle using a rolling pin or wine bottle, about 1/4 inch thickness. 10. cook each tortilla individually on high heat for about 1 minute on each side, flipping as soon as bubbles appear and the edges look firm. 11. allow the tortillas to cool before storing in an airtight container and serve warm.

title: Spanakopita (Greek Spinach Pie)
text: spanakopita (greek spinach pie) source: delicious.com.au ingredients - 1kg frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry - 180ml olive oil, divided - 1 leek, white and light green parts, finely sliced - 4 green shallots, finely sliced - 400g feta cheese, crumbled - 50g rocket (arugula), roughly chopped - 1 bunch fresh dill, fronds chopped - 1 bunch fresh mint, leaves chopped - ½ bunch fresh flat-leaf parsley, leaves chopped - zest of 1 lemon - 3 eggs, lightly beaten - 15 sheets filo pastry - 5ml sesame seeds - lemon wedges, to serve instructions 1. preheat oven to 200°c (204°c) and heat 30ml olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat, then cook leek and shallots until softened, about 5 minutes. 2. combine squeezed spinach, leek mixture, feta, rocket, dill, mint, parsley, lemon zest, and eggs in a large bowl, mix well, and season with pepper. 3. brush a large round oven-proof pan or springform tin (about 28cm) with olive oil, lay one sheet of filo in the pan letting excess hang over the edge, brush with olive oil, and continue layering 7–8 filo sheets, brushing each with oil and rotating each sheet slightly so overhang covers all sides. 4. spoon the spinach filling into the lined pan and spread evenly. 5. fold overhanging filo back over the filling, layer remaining filo sheets on top brushing each with oil, tuck edges in neatly, score the top lightly with a knife, and sprinkle with sesame seeds. 6. bake for 45 minutes until golden and crisp, rest 10 minutes before slicing, and serve with lemon wedges.

title: Spelt Rolls
text: spelt rolls ingredients בצק - 1 ק"ג קמח כוסמין לבן (או חצי לבן) - 600–650 מ"ל מים פושרים - 25–30 ג' שמרים טריים (או 1 כפית שמרים יבשים) - 2 כפיות סוכר או דבש - ½ כוס שמן זית - 1 כפית מלח לשימון ואפייה - ½ כוס שמן זית - מלח גס למריחת זעתר - 1 כוס עלי זעתר טרי - 10 שיני שום - ½ כוס שמן זית instructions 1. מערבבים שמרים, סוכר ומעט מים חמימים וממתינים 5 דקות עד שמתחיל לבעבע. 2. בקערה גדולה מערבבים קמח ומלח, מוסיפים תערובת השמרים, שמן זית ויתרת המים, וממתינים כ-10 דקות עד לקבלת בצק חלק וגמיש. 3. מכסים ומניחים לתפיחה כשעה–שעה וחצי עד שהבצק מכפיל נפחו. 4. מכינים את ממרח הזעתר בטחינת עלי זעתר, שום ושמן זית בעזרת מעבד מזון עד לקבלת ממרח. 5. מחלקים את הבצק ל-20 כדורים שווים, מרדדים כל כדור, מורחים ממרח זעתר, מקפלים ומעצבים ללחמנייה. 6. מסדרים בתבנית משומנת, מכסים ומניחים לתפיחה שנייה כ-30 דקות. 7. מחממים תנור ל-200°c, מברישים לחמניות בשמן זית ומפזרים מלח גס. 8. אופים 18–22 דקות עד להשחמה ומניחים להתקרר מעט לפני ההגשה.

title: Sticky Shiitake Mushrooms
text: sticky shiitake mushrooms source: bosh.tv ingredients - 60ml groundnut oil - 480ml shiitake mushrooms, thickly sliced and dipped in water - 60ml cornstarch - 15ml sesame oil - 2 cloves garlic, minced - 1 inch ginger, minced - 30ml brown sugar - 30ml rice wine vinegar - 5ml cornstarch mixed with 2ml water - 60ml soy sauce - 5ml sriracha - basmati rice for serving - finely sliced scallions for garnish - sesame seeds for garnish instructions 1. put the shiitake mushrooms in a bowl, pour in the cornstarch and stir them round making sure they're well covered. 2. warm the groundnut oil in a wok until nice and hot, then pour in the mushrooms and fry them for 4-6 minutes until cooked through and slightly crisp on the outside. 3. take the mushrooms out of the wok, put them in a bowl and set aside. 4. turn the heat down slightly and pour in the sesame oil, making sure the wok is clean. 5. add the garlic and ginger and cook them until you release the aromas and they're bubbling in the oil. 6. add the brown sugar to the wok and stir it around until it's caramelised. 7. add the cornstarch, soy sauce and rice wine vinegar, stirring until the sauce has thickened slightly. 8. add the sriracha and stir it into the sauce. 9. pour the cooked mushrooms into the sauce and stir them around so they're warmed through and completely covered. 10. serve the sticky mushrooms over basmati rice and garnish with scallions and sesame seeds.

title: Stuffed Cabbage
text: stuffed cabbage ingredients - 1 large head of cabbage - 680g ground chuck - 120ml raw rice - 1 small onion, grated - 2 eggs - 10ml salt, divided - 4ml freshly ground pepper, divided - 1 large onion, sliced into thin half moons - 15-454g canned tomato sauce - 2 28-ounce cans tomatoes with their juice - 2 medium-large lemons, juiced - 120ml light brown sugar, gently packed instructions 1. boil a large pot of water and cut the core out of the cabbage. 2. when the water is at a rolling boil, add the cabbage and cook covered for about 10 minutes, occasionally rolling the cabbage around so each side is under water. 3. gently lift the cabbage into a colander and pour cool water over it. 4. when cool enough to handle, separate the leaves, and if inner leaves are not pliable, put the remaining cabbage back into boiling water for a few minutes. 5. shave off the thickest part of each leaf near where it was attached to the core. 6. preheat the oven to 191°c. 7. mix the rice, grated onion, eggs, 5ml salt, and 1ml pepper in a medium bowl, then add the beef and combine with your hands. 8. make small meatballs between golf ball and baseball-sized and set them aside on a plate. 9. loosely wrap each meatball in a cabbage leaf and place seam side down on a platter. 10. arrange the leftover leaves on the bottom of one or two heavy oven-safe pots. 11. move the cabbage rolls into the pot(s) seam side down and layer with about half of the thin onion slices. 12. add the tomatoes and their juice, tomato sauce, lemon juice, remaining teaspoon of salt, and 2ml of pepper to the pot(s). 13. if the canned tomatoes are whole, open them with a spoon or knife so their juices flow out. 14. top with the remaining onions. 15. bring the pot(s) to a boil on the stovetop, sprinkle on the brown sugar, and gently mix it in. 16. transfer to the oven and bake covered for 1 hour, then bake uncovered for 1 1/2 to 2 hours.

title: Sweet Potato Sourdough Cinnamon Rolls
text: sweet potato sourdough cinnamon rolls source: instagram.com ingredients dough - 350 g sweet potato blended with milk - 50 g flour for tangzhong - 250 g milk for tangzhong - 2 eggs - 360 g stiff sourdough starter - 950 g bread flour - 225 g sugar - 115 g soft butter - 9 g salt - 80–120 ml milk for dough filling - 345 g butter - 270 g demerara sugar - 45ml pumpkin spice mix - 15ml cinnamon - 10ml nutmeg - 10ml ginger - 10ml cloves frosting - 230 g cream cheese - 230 g mascarpone - 30 g butter - 60 g powdered sugar - 5ml vanilla instructions 1. make tangzhong by heating 50 g flour and 250 g milk to 65°c. 2. blend sweet potato with milk. 3. mix tangzhong, sweet potato, flour, sugar, and eggs together and let autolyse for 30 minutes. 4. add stiff starter and milk, resting for 30 minutes (add more milk only if dough is dry). 5. add salt and butter and knead for 5–10 minutes. 6. perform 3 folds every 40 minutes during a 4-hour bulk fermentation. 7. refrigerate overnight. 8. roll dough to 0.5 cm thickness, spread filling evenly, roll up, and cut into 5 cm pieces. 9. proof for 3–5 hours. 10. bake at 175°c for 25–30 minutes, until internal 85°c. 11. frost the warm rolls with the cream cheese mixture.

title: Sweet Potato Sourdough Cinnamon Rolls — Smaller Batch
text: sweet potato sourdough cinnamon rolls — smaller batch ingredients dough - 120 g sweet potato - 30 g milk - 21 g flour - 105 g milk - 1 egg - 150 g stiff sourdough starter - 400 g bread flour - 80 g sugar - 48 g soft butter - 4 g salt - 35–50 ml milk filling - 145 g butter - 115 g demerara sugar - 30ml pumpkin spice mix - 1¼ tsp cinnamon - 4ml nutmeg - 4ml ginger - 4ml cloves frosting - 95 g cream cheese - 95 g mascarpone - 12 g butter - 25 g powdered sugar - 2ml vanilla instructions 1. blend sweet potato with 30 g milk until smooth. 2. prepare tangzhong by combining 21 g flour with 105 g milk, heating until thickened, then cool. 3. combine blended sweet potato, cooled tangzhong, egg, and stiff sourdough starter in a mixing bowl. 4. add bread flour, sugar, soft butter, salt, and 35–50 ml milk, starting with the lower amount. 5. mix until dough is soft, elastic, and slightly tacky, being conservative with milk as sweet potato varies. 6. develop gluten fully after butter incorporation until the dough reaches proper consistency. 7. mix filling ingredients together, combining butter, demerara sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, and cloves. 8. roll out proofed dough, spread filling evenly, roll into a log, and cut into 8-12 small rolls. 9. proof rolls until puffy, 3–5 hours. 10. bake at 175°c for 25–30 minutes, until internal 85°c. 11. frost the warm rolls with the cream cheese & mascarpone frosting mixture.

title: Swirled Garlic Herb Bread
text: swirled garlic herb bread source: half baked harvest ingredients - 240ml lukewarm milk - 11ml instant yeast - 30ml melted butter - 3 eggs at room temperature - 960ml flour - 5ml salt - 30ml sugar - 90ml butter - 3 minced garlic cloves - 60ml basil chopped finely - 60ml parsley chopped finely - 30ml fresh oregano finely chopped - 120ml grated parmesan cheese - 1 beaten egg for brushing instructions 1. in a large bowl, combine flour, yeast, salt and sugar together. 2. pour in lukewarm milk, melted butter, and eggs and start to combine into flour and form a ball. 3. knead dough for a few minutes until it is smooth. 4. place ball of dough into a well greased bowl, cover and let rest until doubled in size, approximately 1 hour. 5. in a small bowl, mix 90ml butter, 3 minced garlic cloves, 60ml basil chopped finely, 60ml parsley chopped finely, 30ml fresh oregano finely chopped, and 120ml grated parmesan cheese. 6. after dough has risen, press down lightly and transfer to a lightly floured counter. 7. roll it out into a rectangle approximately 13×19 inches, just like cinnamon roll dough. 8. spread garlic butter mixture evenly all over the dough. 9. starting from the longest edge closest to you, roll it up into a log. 10. transfer log onto a prepared baking sheet lined with lightly sprayed parchment or silicone mat. 11. position the log of dough vertically and using a very sharp knife cut down the middle leaving 2 inches at the top end intact. 12. take the left strand and cross it over the right and vice versa, exposing the inside of the strand to show the green mixture. 13. curve the top under itself and do the same with the bottom, almost like you are making an "s". 14. cover with a tea towel and let rise another hour. 15. brush with beaten egg. 16. preheat oven to 191°c and bake for 25 to 35 minutes until golden brown.

title: Switchel (Haymaker's Punch)
text: switchel (haymaker's punch) source: null ingredients - 1.5 liters cold water - 30 ml raw apple cider vinegar with mother - 10-15 grams fresh ginger, grated (or 1-2 grams ground ginger) - 30 ml blackstrap molasses or pure maple syrup or raw honey - juice of ½ lemon or lime, optional (approximately 15 ml) - 1-2 pinches sea salt, optional (for electrolytes) - herbs such as mint or basil, optional - spices such as cinnamon or turmeric, optional instructions 1. boil 125 ml of water and add grated ginger, simmering for 2-5 minutes. 2. let the ginger brew cool slightly and strain if desired. 3. in a large pitcher or bottle, combine 30 ml apple cider vinegar, 30 ml molasses, syrup, or honey, optional lemon or lime juice, optional herbs or spices, optional salt, and the strained ginger tea. 4. add the remaining 1375 ml of cold water to the pitcher. 5. stir or shake the mixture well. 6. refrigerate for at least 1 hour or overnight for full flavor development. 7. shake or stir before pouring and serve cold over ice, or mix with sparkling water if desired.

title: The Best Fudgy Brownies
text: the best fudgy brownies source: tasty ingredients - 227g good-quality semi-sweet chocolate (225 g) - 180ml butter, melted - 300ml sugar (250 g) - 2 eggs - 10ml vanilla extract - 180ml all-purpose flour (95 g) - 60ml cocoa powder (30 g) - 5ml salt instructions 1. preheat the oven to 177°c (180°c) and line an 8-inch (20 cm) square baking dish with parchment paper. 2. chop the chocolate into chunks and melt half of the chocolate in the microwave in 20-second intervals, saving the other half for later. 3. in a large bowl, mix the butter and sugar with an electric hand mixer, then beat in the eggs and vanilla for 1-2 minutes, until the mixture becomes fluffy and light in color. 4. whisk in the melted chocolate (making sure it's not too hot or else the eggs will cook), then sift in the flour, cocoa powder, and salt, folding to incorporate the dry ingredients while being careful not to overmix as this will cause the brownies to be more cake-like in texture. 5. fold in the chocolate chunks, then transfer the batter to the prepared baking dish. 6. bake for 20-25 minutes, depending on how fudgy you like your brownies, then cool completely. 7. slice and serve with a cold glass of milk.

title: The Best Gluten-Free Battered Cauliflower Recipe
text: the best gluten-free battered cauliflower recipe source: glutenfreefoodee.com ingredients - 2 eggs separated - 2ml cream of tarter - 1 c bob’s red mill 1 for 1 gluten-free flour - 15ml baking powder - 2ml xantham gum (optional- i like to add an 2ml extra, even though it is in the bobs red mill 1-1 flour blend) - 5ml salt - 4ml each granulated onion, granulated garlic, and black pepper. - 1 c club soda - 1/3 c milk or non-dairy alternative - 1 medium cauliflower - vegetable oil for frying instructions 1. preparing the cauliflower 2. put a large pot of salted water on the stove to boil. 3. chop cauliflower into bite sized florets. don’t be concerned if some tiny pieces break off keep them, as they can be combined with the batter at the end to make fritters. 4. rinse cauliflower pieces under water. 5. add cauliflower to boiling water. cook until fork tender 6. then drain and leave in a strainer to cool. 7. making the batter 8. separate the whites and yolks of the two eggs into two separate bowls. 9. to the egg yolks, add in gluten-free flour, baking powder, xantham gum (optional), salt, granulated onion, granulated garlic, black pepper, milk, and club soda. 10. beat with a whisk until smooth and combined. 11. know that the batter will have a thin consistency before you add in the egg whites- this is fine. 12. in other bowl, add cream of tarter to the egg whites. 13. using a hand mixer with whisk attachment, beat egg whites to stiff peaks - glossy, thick, and they shouldn’t move when you turn the bowl over. 14. use a silicone spatula to gently fold the whites into the batter, until there are no white streaks. do a figure eight motion while scraping the bottom of the bowl. each pass helps combine this delicate batter. 15. making gluten-free battered cauliflower bites 16. line a cookie sheet with parchment paper or use a wire rack that fits a pan. 17. in a large skillet place about an inch of oil and heat until 350°. 18. to test the batter, use a teaspoon and drop a bit of batter into the oil and fry until golden on both sides. allow to cool slightly and taste. you can now adjust the seasoning after trying the batter. once you are happy with the taste, you can proceed to the next step. 19. drop individual florets of cauliflower into the bowl of batter 20. using you teaspoons scoop out florets, ensuring they are well coated with batter, but not excessively so. that is why we aren’t using a tablespoon. 21. drop the battered cauliflower into the hot oil and cook until golden brown on all sides. we recommend using tongs to turn the cauliflower bites. 22. once they are fried, place them on the parchment paper lined rimmed sheet tray or on the wire rack. 23. after all the cauliflower is fried put the pan in the oven on 200° to keep warm, if necessary.

title: The Best Smoky and Spicy Roasted Chickpeas
text: the best smoky and spicy roasted chickpeas source: foodal.com ingredients - 1 can chickpeas - 1 canned chipotle pepper in adobo sauce ((1 pepper, not 1 can!)) - 5ml olive oil - 1ml crushed red pepper flakes - 1ml cayenne - 1ml fresh ground black pepper - 1ml sea salt instructions 1. preheat the oven to 218°c. 2. drain and rinse garbanzos in cold water until the water runs clear. shake off any excess water, or use a salad spinner. 3. spread beans on a clean dishtowel or paper towel and pat dry, rolling the beans gently to absorb as much water as possible. some of the outer skins will come off. 4. allow the beans to air dry for another 10-30 minutes. 5. finely mince the chipotle pepper, or mash with a mortar and pestle. mix in the olive oil and seasonings. 6. in a medium bowl, add the beans and seasoning mix. toss lightly to coat. 7. spread on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, providing plenty of space for the beans to roast. 8. bake for 30-40 minutes. every 10 minutes, shake the pan, and re-spread the beans. watch the last 10 minutes of baking carefully, as they can quickly burn. at this time, they will be thoroughly browned, but still soft in the center when you break open one of the beans. 9. turn off the oven, open the door slightly, and leave the pan inside as the oven cools for an additional 10-20 minutes to finish drying and creating a crispy outer surface. 10. serve warm or cool. store any leftovers in a paper bag.

title: Sourdough Brioche Bread
text: sourdough brioche bread source: homegrownhappiness.com ingredients - 50 g sourdough starter - 100 g all-purpose flour - 50 g water - 550 g all-purpose flour with around 11% protein - 50 g granulated sugar - 4 large eggs - all the stiff starter - 125 g milk - 9 g salt - 225 g unsalted butter (room temperature but still firm and not melted, cut into cubes) - one egg yolk + 15ml water (whisked together) instructions 1. mix 50g starter with 100g flour and 50g water. knead together into a soft dough ball. 2. place it into a jar or bowl, covered with a damp cloth or plastic wrap. leave to rise for 8 to 10 hours, until doubled. 3. add the flour, sugar, salt, eggs, milk, and stiff starter to the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a dough hook. 4. turn the mixer on low and combine until it forms a thick but slightly sticky dough. mix on low for around 5 minutes to develop the gluten. 5. add the cubed butter a few pieces at a time, on medium speed. wait for each piece to fully incorporate before adding the next. 6. continue mixing on medium speed for around 15 minutes, until the dough is smooth, glossy, and pulls cleanly away from the sides of the bowl. don't be tempted to add more flour. 7. let the dough rest for a few minutes, then check the window pane. stretch a small piece of dough between your fingers. if it stretches thin enough to see light through without tearing, it's ready. 8. you can mix this dough by hand instead, though it takes a long time and requires arm muscle. if you get tired, take a break. the dough will respond well to some relaxation time. don't be tempted to add more flour. 9. place the dough in a greased bowl and cover with plastic wrap or a lid. put it in a warm spot, ideally around 22 to 24°c (72 to 23°c), and let it bulk out by 30 to 40%. this will take around 4 to 6 hours, depending on temperature. 10. once risen, place the dough in the fridge for at least 4 hours, or up to 24 hours. ensure the bowl is covered tightly so the dough doesn't dry out. 11. after the cold proof, the dough will be quite firm. turn it out onto a clean bench and divide into two equal pieces. line two 8 x 5 inch (21 x 13 cm) loaf pans with parchment paper. 12. divide each piece of dough into 8 equal balls, and shape them into tight rounds by rolling on the bench under your cupped hand. fit 8 balls into each lined pan. they will fit snugly with a little room to expand upwards. 13. let the brioche proof in a warm spot until almost doubled and very puffy. this can take 5 to 8 hours, depending on temperature. 14. preheat the oven to 200°c (204°c). 15. brush the tops of the loaves with egg wash. bake for around 25 to 30 minutes, until deep golden brown. if the tops are darkening too quickly, loosely cover with foil. 16. let the loaves cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool to room temperature before slicing.

title: The Guardian: Nigel Slater's recipes for raspberry and apricot shortcake, and apricot and harissa chutney
text: the guardian: nigel slater's recipes for raspberry and apricot shortcake, and apricot and harissa chutney glossy, rich and fleeting, apricots always make summer special. two ways to use a glut of them: a buttery shortcake layered with raspberries, and a glossy chutney spiked with harissa. ingredients raspberry and apricot shortcake (serves 8-10) - 6 apricots - 175 g softened butter - 175 g golden caster sugar - 2 eggs - 80 g ground almonds - 175 g self-raising flour - a few drops vanilla extract - 150 g raspberries - icing sugar, a little to finish for the topping: - 100 g plain flour - 75 g butter - 45 ml jumbo oats - 30 ml demerara sugar - 30 ml flaked almonds apricot and harissa chutney (makes 3 x 400 ml jam jars) - 500 g apricots, fresh - 500 g tomatoes - 1 medium onion - 300 ml white wine vinegar - 250 g golden granulated sugar - 90 g sultanas - zest of 1 small lemon - 5 ml salt - 30 ml harissa - 60 ml honey instructions raspberry and apricot shortcake 1. preheat the oven to 160°c/gas mark 3. line the base of a 22 cm round spring-form cake tin with baking parchment. 2. make the topping: process the flour and butter to coarse crumbs (in a processor or by rubbing between your fingers and thumbs). add the oats, sugar and flaked almonds, then a little water (no more than a tablespoon), and shake the bowl until the mixture comes together in crumbs of different sizes. set aside. 3. halve the apricots and remove their stones. 4. beat the butter and sugar together until light and fluffy. beat the eggs briefly to mix, then add gradually to the mixture with the beater on a slow speed. 5. fold in the ground almonds and flour, then add the vanilla extract. transfer the mixture to the lined tin and smooth the surface. place the halved apricots cut-side down on top, then scatter over the raspberries. 6. scatter the crumble mixture loosely over the fruit and bake for 1 hour and 15 minutes. check with a metal skewer inserted in the centre - it should come out moist but without uncooked mixture attached. bake a further 5 minutes if necessary. remove from the oven and leave to settle for 20 minutes. 7. run a palette knife around the edge to free the cake from its tin, then transfer to a plate and dust lightly with icing sugar. apricot and harissa chutney 1. halve the apricots and discard their stones. put them into a large, deep, heavy-based saucepan. cut the tomatoes in half and add to the pot, then peel and roughly chop the onion and stir it in. 2. add the vinegar, sugar, sultanas, lemon zest and salt and bring to the boil. stir well, lower the heat to a simmer, partially cover, and leave to bubble gently for an hour or so. 3. stir in the harissa and honey and continue cooking for 10 minutes. taste and adjust the seasoning with salt, honey or lemon juice as needed. ladle into sterilised jars, seal, and store in a cool, dark place. source <https://www.theguardian.com/food/2023/jul/16/nigel-slater-recipes-raspberry-and-apricot-shortcake-apricot-and-harissa-chutney

title: Sage Oil
text: sage oil source: the herb gardener if you start making sage oil now, you'll have some prepped and ready to go in two to three weeks. with the holidays coming, sage oil, sage honey and sage vinegar are nice additions to your culinary arsenal, too. they'll all add a savory kick to your recipes with a minimum of fuss, and they make very nice gifts. this is a sage oil "infusion" rather than an essential oil that's distilled like spirits. it's for use as a cooking ingredient. uses for sage oil before you head out to the herb patch, let's take a look at some of the ways this versatile flavored oil can help in the kitchen: add it to olive oil - if the proliferation of olive oils on the market seems a bit confusing to you, you're not alone. the fact that a mild and inexpensive olive oil is great option for general cooking doesn't necessarily make it a good first choice as an at-table spread for your homemade dinner rolls. for that, extra virgin olive oil is probably your best bet and worth the money. to elevate a basic olive oil to standalone status, though, all you have to do is add a little flavor. it's a neat trick that works every time. herbed oils impart the aroma and some of the flavor of their onboard herbs via a cold (or warm) infusion process. adding a little sage olive oil to your potato rolls, for instance, will give them extra savor in a unique and appealing way. it's a personal touch that's easy to produce. as a substitute for minced or rubbed sage - fried sage leaves are delicious, but you don't need to keep a potted sage plant on your windowsill this winter to get those warm, robust flavor notes into your recipes. incorporate sage oil in baked, stewed or slow cooked dishes and you'll pick up a subtle hint of sage without bits of the leaves floating in your sauces or peeking through your piles of carrots. think of it a two-for-one bargain. in sauté - i like to infuse avocado oil with sage. avocado oil has a very high smoke point (when it starts to break down), so it's a practical as well as a heart healthy choice for frying and sautéing. a whisper of sage elevates just about any savory ingredient it's cooked with. on fowl - if you oil the skin on chicken, turkey or cornish game hen before cooking, consider using sage oil. you'll really like the flavor. for an added buttery mouthful, use sage butter under the skin and sage oil on the skin when preparing baked, grilled or rotisserie fowl. in marinades - when you're adding flavor to fowl and even meaty fish using a marinade, sage oil is a good friend to have around. it works quickly, and without making your meat look like you just dragged it through a salad. sage oil recipe ingredients 480ml cooking oil (olive oil is a good first oil to try, but any oil will do) 480ml lightly packed sage leaves large glass jar with tight fitting lid presentation bottle or oil dispenser 30 black peppercorns (whole) instructions wash and dry sage leaves, and place them in a large glass jar with a tight fitting lid. add 20 or so lightly crushed peppercorns to the jar. heat oil (see note below) pour oil into the jar. make sure you add enough to cover the leaves. (compress leaves with a mixing spoon until they're submerged in the oil if you have to.) allow the oil to cool completely and secure the lid on the jar. place the jar in a cool, dark spot for two to three weeks. (test after two weeks to see if the mixture is flavorful enough for your taste. three weeks should be about the maximum.) shake the jar three or four times a week (whenever you think about it) during the infusion process. after two (or three) weeks, pour the oil through a fine mesh strainer and place it in its final container with the 10 additional peppercorns. sage oil - notes and tips: if you don't have enough leaves, you can use sage stems. they produce a stronger and sometimes slightly more resinous flavor, though. harvest sage in the morning after the dew has evaporated but before noon when the sun begins to warm up your herb patch. rinse sage leaves thoroughly and let them dry in a single layer on paper towels. the idea is to heat the oil just enough to encourage the sage leaves to release their native oils into the mixture. too hot, and the oil will cook the leaves -- that's a bad thing. a temperature of around 41°c or slightly warmer works well for me. i like to remove the leaves after infusing because then i'll have a good idea of the flavor going forward. sage can be overpowering in some mild dishes, so recognizing the potency of a tablespoon or two of oil is a good thing. leaves left in the mixture will keep adding flavor intensity over time. i do add back one leaf (and a few pepper corns) to the oil decanter after infusing the oil. this makes it easier to identify the without having to add a label. just a suggestion. oh, if you're wondering if a recipe will taste good with sage oil, my general guideline is that if a savory recipe contains carrots, lots of onions, lemon juice or chicken, a little sage oil couldn't hurt. you can halve or double this recipe as needed, although when increasing it, prefer multiple jars for the infusion.

title: The Real Mushroom Soup
text: the real mushroom soup ingredients - a small handful of dried porcini - olive oil - 600g/454g 170g mixed fresh wild mushrooms (chanterelles, girolles, trompettes de la mort, shitake, oyster), cleaned and sliced - 2 cloves garlic, peeled and finely sliced - 1 red onion, peeled and finely chopped - a knob of butter - a handful of fresh thyme, leaves picked - sea salt and freshly ground black pepper - 1 litre/1 ¾ pints chicken or vegetable stock - a handful of fresh flat-leaf parsley, leaves picked and roughly chopped - 30ml mascarpone cheese - 1 lemon - optional: truffle oil instructions 1. place the porcini in a small dish, add boiling water just to cover, and leave to soak. 2. get a large casserole-type pan nice and hot, then add a good couple of lugs of olive oil and your fresh mushrooms. 3. stir around very quickly for a minute, then add your garlic, onion, butter, thyme, and a small amount of seasoning. 4. after about a minute when moisture cooking out of the mushrooms, add half of your porcini chopped up and the rest left whole. 5. strain the soaking liquid to remove any grit and add it to the pan. 6. carry on cooking for about 20 minutes until most of the moisture disappears. 7. season to taste and add your stock. 8. bring to the boil and simmer for around 20 minutes. 9. remove half the soup from the pan and whizz it up to a purée, then pour it back in. 10. add the parsley and mascarpone, and season carefully to taste. 11. mix together a pinch of salt and pepper with the zest of one lemon and the juice of half of it, then spoon a little of this into the middle of the soup when serving.

title: Tiramisu
text: tiramisu ingredients - 7 large egg yolks - 71 grams (80ml) white sugar - 454 grams (454g) mascarpone cheese, chilled - 1½ cups brewed espresso (or very strong coffee), cooled to room temperature - 1 package (about 200 grams) crisp italian ladyfingers (savoiardi) or petibers / petit beurre biscuits - unsweetened cocoa powder, for dusting - dark chocolate shavings, for garnish (optional) instructions 1. in a stand mixer with the whisk attachment, beat the egg yolks and sugar on high until pale, fluffy, and doubled in volume, about 10 minutes, until the mixture falls in a thick ribbon. 2. reduce speed to low and add mascarpone a spoonful at a time, letting it incorporate gently, then scrape the bowl and beat for 10–20 seconds more until smooth without overmixing. 3. pour the espresso into a wide bowl and quickly dip each ladyfinger, one at a time, into the coffee for 1–2 seconds and place them in a single layer in a 9x13-inch dish. 4. spread half the mascarpone mixture over the layer of dipped ladyfingers and smooth it, then repeat with another layer of dipped ladyfingers and the remaining mascarpone mixture. 5. cover and refrigerate at least 6 hours or overnight. 6. just before serving, sift cocoa powder generously over the top and optionally garnish with chocolate shavings.

title: Tourlou Briam
text: tourlou briam ingredients - 2 potatoes, sliced - 1 large sweet potato, sliced - 1 large eggplant, diced - 1 brown onion, sliced - 1 large zucchini, diced thick - 2 carrots, sliced - 400g crushed tomato - 120ml extra virgin olive oil - 2ml dried oregano - salt and pepper to taste - 180ml water - feta cheese for sprinkling (optional) - fresh parsley to garnish instructions 1. arrange vegetables into a large baking tray. 2. combine all sauce ingredients in a bowl and pour over the vegetables. 3. mix all ingredients through thoroughly and cover with a layer of baking paper then tightly with aluminium foil. 4. bake at 180c fan forced for 40 minutes or until potatoes are cooked. 5. uncover and cook for an additional 15-20 minutes to develop colour. 6. once ready, drizzle extra olive oil over the top, sprinkle with feta cheese, and garnish with fresh parsley.

title: Traditional Greek Galaktoboureko recipe (Greek Custard Pie with Syrup)
text: traditional greek galaktoboureko recipe (greek custard pie with syrup) source: mygreekdish.com ingredients - 450g phyllo pastry (397g/ 12 sheets) - 230g butter (227g) - 160g finely ground (thin) semolina (170g) - 220g sugar (213g) - 500g milk (499g) - 4 eggs (separated into whites and yolks) - 30g butter (28g) - 5ml vanilla extract - 500g double (heavy) cream (499g) - 325g water (323g) - 575g sugar (573g) - 1 large tbsp honey - peel of 1 lemon - a cinnamon stick - 10 drops of the lemon juice instructions 1. to make this galaktoboureko recipe, start by preparing the syrup. into a small pan add the sugar, the water and lemon peel, cinammon stick and lemon and bring to the boil. let it boil just until the sugar has dissolved. remove the pan from the stove, add the honey and stir. leave the syrup aside to cool completely. 2. prepare the custard for the galaktoboureko (steps 3-8). 3. pour into a saucepan the milk, the cream and 120g of the sugar, and bring to the boil. (don’t whisk the mixture. the sugar at the bottom of the pan protects the milk from burning.) as soon as it comes to the boil and heats up slowly add the semolina and the vanilla extract, whilst whisking. turn the heat down to medium heat and whisk constantly until the mixture becomes creamy. remove the pan from the stove, add a knob of butter and fold. let it cool down while you are preparing the remaining steps, until warm (50c / 49°c), else your mix will curdle when you fold in the eggs. just remember to whisk it once in a while. 4. . in most traditional greek recipes, the eggs are added whole towards the end, but with this galaktoboureko recipe the eggs are beaten into meringues and combined in the semolina based cream. this is the secret to a more fluffy and creamy custard and to avoid the egg-y smell, which can ruin the flavour of your galaktoboureko. 5. . make sure your egg whites, bowl and whisk attachment/s are free of any water. use an electric mixer or electric hand beaters to whisk the egg whites and sugar until the mixture is very thick and glossy, all the sugar has dissolved and a long trailing peak forms when the whisk is lifted (meringues). set aside. 6. in another bowl, whisk the yolks and 50g of sugar, until the mixture is thick and foamy. this should take about 5 minutes. 7. with a spatula add 1/4 of the meringues into the egg yolks-sugar mixture and blend with light circular movement from the bottom up. gradually add all the meringues into the mixture and fold. 8. , from step 3 and step 7 and set aside. 9. for this galaktoboureko recipe, you need a large baking tray, approx. 25x32cm. melt 230g of butter (low heat) and butter the bottom and sides of the tray. remove the phyllo roll from the plastic sleeve. you will use 6 sheets of phyllo for the bottom of the galaktoboureko. 10. begin by layering the sheets one by one on the bottom of the tray, making sure to sprinkle each one thoroughly with melted butter. layer four sheets of phyllo so that they extend half in the pan and half out of the pan horizontally and vertically and two more in the middle. 11. , smoothing the surface with a spatula and fold the phyllo sheet flaps over the custard. sprinkle with melted butter. 12. , sprinkling each sheet with melted butter. with a knife trim some of the excessive phyllo and use your pastry brush to help you turn the phyllo inwards, towards the bottom of the pan to seal the galaktoboureko. 13. of the galaktoboureko in pieces with a sharp knife. cut down until the knife reaches the cream. 14. sprinkle with a little bit of water. 15. until the phyllo is crisp and golden. 16. as soon as the galaktoboureko is ready, ladle slowly the cold syrup over the pastry. (hot galaktoboureko, cold syrup) 17. serve after the syrup is absorbed. enjoy!

title: Triple Chocolate Mousse Torte
text: triple chocolate mousse torte source: abajillianrecipes.com ingredients - 120ml boiling water - 4ml instant espresso powder - 43g semi-sweet chocolate, (chopped or chips) - 180ml + 15ml all-purpose flour - 180ml granulated sugar - 30ml brown sugar - 105ml unsweetened cocoa powder - 2ml baking soda - 2ml baking powder - 2ml salt - 1 large egg - 120ml buttermilk - 60ml vegetable oil - 5ml vanilla - 170g semi-sweet chocolate, (chips or chopped) - 720ml heavy cream, (divided) - 20ml unflavored gelatin, (divided) - 30ml cold water, (divided) - 170g white chocolate, (chips or chopped) - 113g semi-sweet chocolate, (chips or chopped) - 120ml heavy cream - white, milk, and dark chocolate curls instructions 1. preheat the oven to 350ºf. line an 8-inch springform pan with parchment paper and grease with butter or nonstick cooking spray; set aside. 2. in a medium bowl, stir together the boiling water, espresso powder, and semi-sweet chocolate until chocolate has dissolved and mixture is smooth. set aside to cool. 3. in a large mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, granulated sugar, brown sugar, cocoa powder, baking soda, baking powder, and salt until combined. 4. in another bowl, whisk together the egg, buttermilk, vegetable oil, and vanilla. pour wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until smooth. add the cooled espresso-chocolate mixture, stirring until just combined. 5. pour batter into prepared pan and bake in the oven for 31-33 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted in the center of the cake comes out with few crumbs attached. remove from the oven and allow to cool completely. 6. once completely cool, wrap either acetate or parchment paper (about 6 inches wide) around the edges of the cake to create a "wall". secure cake with the sides of the springform pan or an adjustable cake ring. 7. in the chilled bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a whisk attachment, beat 480ml of the heavy cream until stiff peaks form. set aside in the refrigerator. 8. place semi-sweet chocolate into a medium bowl; set aside. pour 120ml of the heavy cream into a saucepan and heat until it begins to simmer. immediately pour hot cream over the semi-sweet chocolate and cover with plastic wrap. let sit for 5 minutes. remove plastic wrap and stir until completely smooth. 9. in a small bowl, sprinkle 10ml gelatin over 15ml cold water; let stand 1 minute. heat in the microwave for 10-15 seconds until gelatin is completely dissolved and liquified. stir gelatin liquid into semi-sweet chocolate mixture; allow to cool completely. 10. place white chocolate into a medium bowl; set aside. pour 120ml of the heavy cream into a saucepan and heat until it begins to simmer. immediately pour hot cream over the white chocolate and cover with plastic wrap. let sit for 5 minutes. remove plastic wrap and stir until completely smooth. 11. in a small bowl, sprinkle 10ml gelatin over 15ml cold water; let stand 1 minute. heat in the microwave for 10-15 seconds until gelatin is completely dissolved and liquified. stir gelatin liquid into white chocolate mixture; allow to cool completely. 12. fold 480ml of the whipped cream (about half) into the cooled semi-sweet chocolate mixture; spread evenly over cake. chill in the freezer until set, about 15-20 minutes. 13. fold the remaining 480ml of the whipped cream into the cooled white chocolate mixture; spread evenly over semi-sweet chocolate mousse layer. 14. refrigerate torte, covered, until set, about 4 hours. 15. place semi-sweet chocolate into a medium bowl. pour heavy cream into a small saucepan on the stove and heat over medium-high heat until it begins to boil. immediately pour hot cream over the chocolate, cover bowl in plastic wrap, then allow to sit for 4-5 minutes. remove plastic wrap and stir until smooth. set aside to cool and thicken slightly. 16. pour ganache over the cake, using an offset spatula to evenly smooth out the top. refrigerate for 20 minutes to allow ganache layer to set up. 17. if desired, sprinkle chocolate curls along the border of the cake. slice, serve and enjoy! cake will keep covered in the refrigerator for up to 5 days.
