title: Vanilla Diplomat Cream
text: vanilla diplomat cream ingredients - 480ml (480ml) whole milk - 75g (80ml) sugar - pinch of salt - 35g (60ml) cornstarch - 15ml vanilla extract - 3 egg yolks - 43g (45ml) unsalted butter - 5ml unflavored gelatin powder - 30ml cold water - 30ml heavy cream - 240ml heavy cream - 28g (3½ tbsp) confectioner's sugar instructions 1. heat milk with half the sugar and salt in a saucepan over medium heat until steaming. 2. whisk egg yolks with remaining sugar, cornstarch, and vanilla until pale, then slowly temper in the hot milk while whisking constantly. 3. return mixture to saucepan and cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, until thick and bubbling, then remove from heat and stir in butter. 4. press plastic wrap directly on the surface and refrigerate until completely cold, at least 2 hours or overnight. 5. sprinkle gelatin over cold water and let bloom for 5 minutes, then melt gently by microwave or over hot water and stir in 30ml heavy cream to cool slightly. 6. whip 240ml heavy cream with confectioner's sugar to soft peaks, then drizzle in the gelatin mixture and continue whipping to medium-firm peaks. 7. whisk the chilled pastry cream until smooth and gently fold in the whipped cream in thirds until fully incorporated and fluffy. 8. use immediately or refrigerate up to 2 days.

title: Vanilla Cake in a Mug
text: vanilla cake in a mug ingredients - 62.5 grams all-purpose flour - 30 grams sugar - 1ml baking powder - dash of salt - 30 grams butter, melted - 45 grams milk - 2ml vanilla extract - 5ml sprinkles instructions 1. mix together the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt in a mug. 2. stir in the melted butter, milk, and vanilla extract until just combined. 3. top with sprinkles. 4. microwave for about 3 minutes until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.

title: Vegan Bechamel Sauce
text: vegan bechamel sauce ingredients - 3 heaped tbsp vegan butter - 45ml all-purpose flour - 30ml nutritional yeast - 600ml almond milk - 2ml nutmeg, grated - salt and pepper to taste instructions 1. melt the vegan butter on low heat in a medium-sized pot. 2. once melted, add the flour and stir until a ball or lumpy consistency appears. 3. add the nutritional yeast and stir well. 4. slowly add the almond milk while whisking aggressively over medium-high heat for about 20 minutes. 5. stir until all the milk is incorporated and a silky smooth sauce forms. 6. add the nutmeg and stir thoroughly. 7. season to taste with salt and pepper, then remove from heat and set aside.

title: Vegan Gluten-Free Black Bean Brownies
text: vegan gluten-free black bean brownies source: minimalistbaker.com ingredients - 2 heaping tbsp flaxseed meal - 90ml water - 1 15-oz. can black beans ((well rinsed and drained // 1 can yields 420ml)) - 45ml coconut oil ((melted // or sub other oil of choice)) - 180ml cocoa powder - 1ml sea salt - 5ml pure vanilla extract - 1/2 heaping cup organic cane sugar ((slightly ground or pulsed in a food processor or coffee grinder for refined texture)) - 8ml baking powder - crushed walnuts - pecans - dairy-free semisweet chocolate chips instructions 1. preheat oven to 177°c (176 c). 2. lightly grease a 12-slot standard size muffin pan (not mini // adjust pan size if altering batch size). make sure you've rinsed and thoroughly drained your black beans at this point. 3. prepare flax egg by combining flax and water in the bowl of the food processor. pulse a couple times and then let rest for a few minutes. 4. add remaining ingredients (besides walnuts or other toppings) and puree - about 3 minutes - scraping down sides as needed. you want it pretty smooth. 5. if the batter appears too thick, add a tbsp or two of water and pulse again. it should be slightly less thick than chocolate frosting but nowhere close to runny. 6. evenly distribute the batter into the muffin tin and smooth the tops with a spoon or your finger. 7. optional: sprinkle with crushed walnuts, pecans or chocolate chips. 8. bake for 20-26 minutes or until the tops are dry and the edges start to pull away from the sides. i found mine took about 25. 9. remove from oven and let cool for 30 minutes before removing from pan. they will be tender, so remove gently with a fork. the insides are meant to be very fudgy, so don't be concerned if they seem too moist - that's the point. plus, they're vegan so it doesn't really matter. 10. store in an airtight container for up to a few days. refrigerate to keep longer.

title: Vegan Hokkaido Milk Bread
text: vegan hokkaido milk bread source: domesticgothess.com ingredients - 30 g (60ml) bread flour - 150 ml (scant 160ml) unsweetened soy milk - 7 g (10ml) instant/fast action or active dry yeast - 5 g (5ml) sugar - 150 ml (scant 160ml) lukewarm unsweetened soy milk - 400 g (3 + 80ml) white bread flour (plus extra as needed) - 55 g (60ml) caster sugar - 5ml salt - 45ml aquafaba ((or more milk)) - 40 g (30ml + 10ml) vegan block butter (softened) - 8ml maple syrup - 15ml water instructions 1. start by making the tangzhong; whisk together the 30g bread flour and 150ml milk in a pan until no lumps remain. 2. place the pan over a medium/low heat and whisk constantly until the mixture has thickened to a pudding-like consistency (think wallpaper paste...). scrape it into a small bowl, cover with baking parchment directly on the surface to prevent a skin from forming and set aside to cool to room temperature. 3. once the tangzhong has cooled (it will become much thicker as it cools, don't worry.), mix together the yeast with the other 150ml of the (lukewarm) soy milk and the 5g sugar. set it aside for about 10 minutes until it goes foamy. 4. mix together the 400g bread flour, 55g sugar and tsp salt in the bowl of a stand mixer. add the cooled tangzhong, the yeast mixture and the aquafaba and mix until it forms a rough dough. 5. set the mixer to a medium speed and leave it to knead for about 10 minutes until the dough is stretchy. it should be soft and sticky but if it seems too wet you can add in a little extra flour, a tablespoon at a time. conversely if it is too dry add in a drop more milk. 6. next, add the softened vegan butter and knead for a further 5-10 minutes until it is well incorporated and the dough is smooth, elastic and no longer feels greasy. 7. place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover and place in the fridge to rise overnight (or in a warm spot until doubled in size, 1-2 hours). 8. the following day (or once the dough has doubled in size at room temperature), knock back the dough and give it a brief 30 second knead to knock out the air bubbles. 9. divide it into 3 or 4 even pieces and roll each one into a ball. (use 4 pieces for a loaf as pictured, with 4 'humps', or 3 for a loaf with 3 'humps'). line an approx 11.5 x 21.5 cm / 4.5 x 8.5 inch loaf tin with baking parchment. 10. roll each ball out into a long oval, fold one third of the oval over the middle (from the side, not the top), then the other third over the top to form a long, narrow packet. 11. roll over the seam to flatten it, then roll it up tightly from one end to make a fat sausage. repeat with the other balls of dough then arrange them in the loaf tin, seam side down. 12. loosely cover and leave to rise until at least doubled in size, it should rise above the top of the tin. this can take 1-2.5 hours (mine took 1 1/2). if you press the dough gently with a finger the indentation should spring back slowly but remain visible. if it springs back quickly it needs to prove for a little longer. 13. while the dough is rising, preheat the oven to 180°c/177°c/gas mark 4. mix together the maple syrup and water in a small bowl. 14. once the loaf has risen, gently brush the top with the maple syrup mixture, making sure that none drips down the sides as that can make the bread stick to the tin. if you don't want a sweet glaze then you can brush it with milk or aquafaba instead. 15. place the loaf in the preheated oven and bake for 30-50 minutes, until a probe thermometer reaches 94°c/94°c when poked into the middle of the loaf. you may need to cover the top loosely with tin foil part way through baking if it starts to colour too much. 16. if you want the loaf to have a shinier crust, brush it with some more of the maple syrup water halfway through baking. 17. once the bread is baked, remove it from the oven and brush with some more of the glaze. let it cool in the tin for 10 minutes then lift it out onto a wire rack to cool completely before slicing. store in an airtight container.

title: Vegan Hu Tieu Recipe
text: vegan hu tieu recipe source: vo uy vegetarian restaurant ingredients - 500g hu tieu noodles (dried or fresh) - 2 carrots (200g) - 1 daikon radish (200g) - 100g shiitake mushrooms - 100g straw mushrooms - 200g tofu - 50g dried bean curd sheets - 100g vegan ham (cha chay) - 100g bean sprouts - 50g fresh herbs (cilantro, chives) - soy sauce to taste - vegan bouillon to taste - rock sugar to taste - salt to taste - pepper to taste - olive oil - fried shallots for garnish - chili sate for serving instructions 1. cut carrot and daikon into 3-4cm chunks, soak dried mushrooms for 10-15 minutes and halve them, cube tofu, slice vegan ham, and rinse herbs and bean sprouts. 2. boil 2.5 liters of water and add carrots, daikon, and mushrooms, then simmer on low heat for 30-45 minutes while skimming foam constantly. 3. season the broth with 15ml vegetable seasoning, 5ml salt, and 15ml rock sugar, and optionally add an apple or loofah for natural sweetness. 4. fry tofu and bean curd sheets until golden, blanch bean sprouts and chives for 20 seconds, and lightly fry vegan ham. 5. soak noodles for 30 minutes, blanch them for 30-40 seconds, rinse with cold water, and toss with 5ml olive oil. 6. layer noodles, tofu, bean curd, vegan ham, sprouts, and chives in a bowl, then ladle hot broth over the top. 7. garnish with fried shallots, cilantro, and pepper, and serve with soy sauce and chili sate on the side.

title: Vegan Whipped Cream (NO Coconut!)
text: vegan whipped cream (no coconut!) source: nora cooks ingredients - 120ml aquafaba (liquid from 1 can of chickpeas, low or no sodium added) - 1ml cream of tartar - 1/2 to 180ml powdered sugar - 5ml pure vanilla extract instructions 1. drain the liquid from a can of chickpeas into a large bowl and reserve the chickpeas for another use, aiming for about 120ml of liquid. 2. add the cream of tartar to help with the whipping process. 3. with a hand mixer, start mixing on medium speed until foamy, then increase to high speed and beat for about 3 to 4 minutes until stiff peaks form. 4. add the powdered sugar and vanilla extract and continue beating for about 1 more minute until fluffy and smooth. 5. serve immediately for best results, or store leftover whipped cream in the freezer.

title: Vegetarian Cauliflower Buffalo Bites
text: vegetarian cauliflower buffalo bites ingredients - 1 whole head of cauliflower - 120ml all purpose flour - 120ml cornstarch - 120ml rice flour - 2ml baking powder - 10ml salt - 240ml water - 45ml buffalo sauce - 45ml melted butter - 1 clove of garlic, diced instructions 1. soak the cauliflower head in salted water to season it and rinse out any debris. 2. mix together the all purpose flour, cornstarch, rice flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. 3. add water to the dry ingredients and stir until a batter forms. 4. cut the cauliflower into bite-sized florets. 5. dip the cauliflower florets into the batter to coat evenly. 6. fry the battered cauliflower until golden and crispy. 7. combine the buffalo sauce, melted butter, and diced garlic in a bowl. 8. toss the fried cauliflower bites in the buffalo sauce mixture until well coated.

title: Venetian Charoset
text: venetian charoset source: joan nathan ingredients - 360ml chestnut paste - 284g dates, chopped - 340g figs, chopped - 30ml poppy seeds - 120ml chopped walnuts - 120ml chopped almonds - 120ml pine nuts - grated rind of 1 orange - 120ml white raisins - 60ml chopped dried apricot - 120ml brandy - honey to bind instructions 1. combine all the ingredients, adding just enough brandy and honey to make the mixture bind.

title: Walnut Cranberry Sourdough Bread Recipe | Super Easy and Delicious
text: walnut cranberry sourdough bread recipe | super easy and delicious source: foodgeek.dk

title: Walnut Cranberry Sourdough
text: walnut cranberry sourdough ingredients dough - 489 g bread flour - 61 g dark rye flour - 61 g spelt flour - 122 g sourdough starter - 444 g water - 93 g toasted walnuts - 23 g walnut oil - 13 g salt soaker - 93 g dried sweet cranberries - 80 g bourbon instructions 1. add bread flour, dark rye flour, spelt flour, sourdough starter, water, and walnut oil to a bowl, then mix with your hands until no dry flour remains. 2. leave the dough covered for an hour to develop the gluten. 3. add cranberries and bourbon to a small bowl and leave them to infuse until needed, or use warm water for an alcohol-free version. 4. heat the oven to 180°c/177°c with fan assist and line a baking sheet with baking paper. 5. toast the walnuts in the oven until fragrant and light brown, then chop them coarsely. 6. over the next 1½ hours, stretch and fold the dough every 30 minutes. 7. during the second set of stretch and folds, include a quarter of the drained cranberries and a quarter of the walnuts, repeating this with each fold and using rubaud mixing after the second set to ensure they are properly mixed in. 8. after the third set, check gluten development using the windowpane test and add another set after 30 minutes if needed. 9. add the entire dough to a see-through container with straight sides and level the top. 10. mark the top of the dough on the outside of the container and mark where the dough will have increased by 25%. 11. let the dough grow by 25% at 30°c/30°c. 12. when the dough has grown, divide it into two equally sized pieces. 13. shape the balls into bâtards or boules and place them in floured bannetons. 14. place the shaped bread in the fridge for at least 8 hours but up to 48 hours at 2°c/2°c. 15. preheat the oven to 260°c/260°c with a baking steel and dutch oven inside for one hour. 16. flour the bottom of the first dough with rice flour, flip it onto a peel, and score it with a lame or sharp knife. 17. put the dough into the bottom of the dutch oven, cover with the lid, and bake for 20 minutes. 18. remove the lid, turn down the oven to 230°c/232°c, and bake for another 25 minutes until golden and crispy. 19. remove the bread from the oven and cool on a wire rack for a couple of hours until it reaches room temperature. 20. bake the second loaf the same way.

title: Walnut Toffee
text: walnut toffee ingredients - xylitol, erythritol, and stevia blend (or xylitol or erythritol alone) - heavy cream or heavy whipping cream - salted butter - walnuts (or any nuts) - sugar-free milk, semisweet, or dark chocolate (or 85% dark chocolate) instructions no instructions provided in source text.

title: Wasabi Roasted Chickpeas
text: wasabi roasted chickpeas source: glueandglitter.com ingredients - 425g can chickpeas (drain, but save the liquid from the can.) - 45ml aquafaba - 30ml wasabi powder - 5ml salt - 5ml sugar - 10ml cornstarch (or potato starch) instructions 1. preheat the oven to 204°c. 2. line a baking sheet with parchment paper or a silpat, and spread the chickpeas onto the sheet in a single layer. bake for 35 minutes. remove from the oven, set aside, and reduce the oven temp to 93°c. 3. when the chickpeas are done baking at 204°c, whisk the chickpea liquid with a fork in a large bowl until it becomes foamy. add chickpeas and toss to coat with the whipped chickpea liquid, then drain off the excess liquid in a colander. 4. stir together wasabi powder, salt, sugar, and cornstarch in a small bowl. 5. transfer the chickpeas back to the large bowl, and toss to coat with the wasabi mixture. 6. spread chickpeas on baking sheet in a single layer, and bake for 20 more minutes.

title: West Coast Onions
text: west coast onions ingredients - 240ml water - 240ml white vinegar - 15ml sugar - 2 large onions, sliced - 240ml mayo - 30ml sour cream - 15ml celery salt instructions 1. combine water, white vinegar, sugar, and sliced onions in a jar and let sit overnight. 2. drain the onions. 3. mix the drained onions with mayo, sour cream, and celery salt.

title: White House Pecan Pie
text: white house pecan pie ingredients - 120ml (115g) unsalted butter, softened - 240ml sugar - 240ml dark corn syrup - 2ml salt - 1½ tsp vanilla extract - 3 large eggs - 480ml chopped pecans - 1 unbaked 9-inch pastry shell instructions 1. preheat oven to 191°c (190°c). 2. in a large bowl, beat softened butter until creamy. 3. add sugar and beat until light and fluffy. 4. mix in dark corn syrup, salt, and vanilla extract. 5. add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition. 6. fold in the chopped pecans. 7. pour the filling into the unbaked pastry shell. 8. bake for 40–50 minutes, until the center is set and the top is golden, with a toothpick coming out mostly clean. 9. cool completely before slicing.

title: Whole Wheat Pizza
text: whole wheat pizza ingredients - 60g crimson turkey whole wheat flour - 240g ka 00 pizza flour - 200g water - 50g levain - 6g salt instructions 1. combine flour, water, levain, and salt together. 2. knead with a stand mixer for approximately 5 minutes. 3. perform 3 stretch and folds during bulk fermentation over 4 hours. 4. chill overnight for 14 hours. 5. allow the dough to rise at room temperature for 5 hours. 6. bake at 288°c for 7 minutes.

title: Whole Wheat Sourdough
text: whole wheat sourdough ingredients - 400g king arthur whole wheat flour - 340g water - 40g rye starter - 8g salt instructions 1. mix flour and water together for 10 minutes, then rest covered for 10 minutes. 2. perform slap and fold on counter for 10 minutes, then rest for 5 minutes. 3. laminate the dough and rest covered. 4. perform coil folds at 3 hours and 6 hours. 5. at 9 hours, shape and refrigerate overnight in a baneton. 6. preheat a pizza stone for 1 hour at 260°c, then reduce to 249°c. 7. spritz the dough with water and bake for 25 minutes on the pizza stone using a tray of water underneath and an upside-down baking sheet above for steam. 8. add an ice cube to the stone and spritz with water a few more times throughout baking. 9. lower heat to 232°c, remove the steam catcher system, and bake for 25 minutes more. 10. rest the loaf for at least 6 hours before slicing.

title: Wild Mushroom Flatbread with Basil Oil Drizzle
text: wild mushroom flatbread with basil oil drizzle ingredients - 120ml loosely packed basil leaves - 1 clove garlic - 30ml extra-virgin olive oil - 1ml sea salt - 1ml ground pepper - 15ml water - 30ml extra-virgin olive oil, divided - 1 small red onion, thinly sliced - 2ml sea salt, divided - 2ml ground black pepper, divided - 454g mixed wild mushrooms (cremini, oyster, shiitake), roughly chopped - 1 large whole-grain or whole-wheat flatbread pizza crust - 113g fresh mozzarella, torn into pieces - arugula, for garnish instructions 1. place basil, garlic, olive oil, salt, pepper and water into a mini food processor and blend until smooth. 2. preheat oven to 204°c and line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper. 3. heat 15ml oil in a large skillet over medium, add onions and cook, stirring frequently, until soft and translucent, 3 to 4 minutes. 4. reduce heat to low, season with half of the salt and pepper, and continue cooking, stirring occasionally, until onions are very soft and begin to stick to the pan, 7 to 9 minutes longer. 5. transfer onions to a bowl and wipe out the skillet. 6. heat remaining 15ml oil on medium-high, add mushrooms and remaining salt and pepper, and cook, stirring frequently, until softened slightly, 3 to 4 minutes. 7. place flatbread on prepared sheet and bake until it begins to brown, 5 to 7 minutes. 8. top with mushrooms, onions and cheese and bake until cheese has melted, about 5 minutes longer. 9. transfer flatbread to a cutting board, drizzle with basil oil, and garnish with arugula. 10. cut flatbread into 16 squares.

title: World's Best Pumpkin Soup
text: world's best pumpkin soup a tried-and-tested favorite from new zealand, where pumpkin soup is an everyday staple — incredibly easy and fast, and great in an extra-large batch (freeze the extra for an instant meal later). ingredients - 45 ml butter - 1 onion, roughly chopped - 2 cloves garlic, chopped - 2 tsp cumin - 1/2 tsp cayenne pepper - 1/2 of a small pumpkin, peeled & chopped into large cubes - 1 sweet potato or kumara, peeled & cubed - 2 stalks celery, chopped - 4 cups chicken stock instructions 1. melt butter in the bottom of a big stock pot. add onion and cook over low heat until soft, about 5 minutes. add garlic and cumin and stir continuously for another minute or so. 2. add pumpkin, sweet potato, celery, and stock, and bring to a simmer. cover partially and cook on the stovetop about 20 minutes, until the veggies are soft. 3. let it cool slightly, then puree in batches in a blender or with an immersion blender. return to the pot and season to taste. source <http://www.laurelofleaves.com/2011/10/worlds-best-pumpkin-soup/

title: You can cook THIS brisket!
text: you can cook this brisket! source: getyumskull.com ingredients - well-marbled brisket - dry rub - light brown sugar - spritz liquid (apple cider vinegar, water, beer, fruit juice, worcestershire, wine, or cola) - butcher paper instructions 1. choose a well-marbled brisket in your desired size range 2. trim external fat on the fat side to about 1/4" thick and remove hard dense fat 3. trim protruding bits to optimize airflow and shape 4. apply dry rub in 2-3 light coats, patting each in before the next, covering all sides and surfaces 5. finish with a very light dusting of light brown sugar 6. place brisket on a small baking rack and refrigerate until ready to cook 7. fill pellet hopper completely and set target temperature to 210-104°c (99-104°c) with cook time set to maximum 8. wait 10 minutes for smoke to transition from thick white to transparent clean smoke before placing meat on cooker 9. place brisket on cooker fat-side up on the rack with temperature probe inserted in thickest part of leanest section 10. let cook for about two hours, checking hourly and spritzing surface if dry 11. at 66°c (65°c) internal temperature, verify probe placement by checking multiple locations 12. wrap brisket in dampened butcher paper once reaching 150-71°c (65-71°c), or leave unwrapped based on preference 13. return wrapped brisket to cooker and continue cooking until reaching 203-99°c (95-99°c) with butter-like resistance when probed 14. remove brisket from cooker and let cool naturally to 60°c (60°c) on counter or in cool oven 15. slice across the grain, using toothpick marks as grain indicator if needed 16. for larger briskets with both flat and point muscle, adjust slicing angle as grain direction changes 17. slice with fat side up for stability, making thinner slices in lean flat and thicker slices toward point

title: Zucchini Cauliflower Summer Gratin
text: zucchini cauliflower summer gratin source: relishing it ingredients - 1 large head cauliflower - kosher salt - 1¼ lbs zucchini, coarsely grated - 30ml olive oil - 180ml chopped onion - 2 garlic cloves, minced - 2ml finely ground black pepper - 30ml all-purpose flour (or gluten-free) - 60ml milk - 80ml heavy cream - 160ml grated parmesan, divided - 15ml chopped fresh rosemary - 45ml chopped fresh parsley instructions 1. core and break cauliflower into pieces, then pulse in food processor in batches to rice-grain size, yielding about 3½ cups. 2. preheat oven to 191°c and lightly oil a shallow baking dish. 3. mix zucchini with 5ml salt and place in a colander over a bowl, then squeeze to remove water (about 160ml shreds) and reserve the liquid. 4. heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat, add onion with a pinch of salt, and cook for 4-5 minutes. 5. reduce heat to medium, add cauliflower, garlic, drained zucchini, 2ml salt, and pepper, then cook for 7-8 minutes. 6. sprinkle flour and stir, then gradually add the reserved zucchini water, milk, and cream over medium heat, stirring for 2-3 minutes to prevent curdling. 7. remove from heat and stir in 80ml parmesan, rosemary, and parsley, then pour the mixture into the prepared baking dish and bake for 20 minutes. 8. add the remaining parmesan and bake for 10 more minutes until golden, with optional broiling to brown the top further.

title: Amazake Drink
text: amazake drink source: justonecookbook.com ingredients - 150 g uncooked japanese short-grain white rice - water for cooking the rice porridge - 240 ml water for cooling the porridge - 200 g rice koji - 960 ml water - 120 g sake lees (sake kasu) - 50 g sugar - 1 pinch diamond crystal kosher salt instructions 1. rinse and drain 150 g uncooked japanese short-grain white rice and add to the inner pot of a rice cooker, filling water to the porridge water line or white rice 960ml line. 2. select the porridge menu on your rice cooker and press start, or cook the porridge according to your rice cooker's instructions. 3. once the porridge is cooked at around 175ºf (79ºc), take out the inner pot from the rice cooker. 4. gradually add 240 ml water, 30ml at a time, to the porridge, stirring thoroughly after each addition and measuring the temperature with an instant-read thermometer. 5. cool the porridge down to 140ºf (60ºc) as koji mold cannot live above that temperature. 6. crumble and add 200 g rice koji to the cooled porridge and stir thoroughly to incorporate. 7. ensure there is enough water to cover the porridge and rice koji so they are sufficiently soaked, adding warm water if needed to maintain 140ºf (60ºc). 8. put the inner pot back into the rice cooker and turn on the keep warm setting, covering the opening with a cloth towel and leaving the rice cooker lid fully open. 9. allow the mixture to cook for 8–10 hours, stirring occasionally and checking the temperature every hour for the first 2–3 hours, keeping it between 125ºf and 140ºf (50–60ºc) at all times. 10. turn off the rice cooker when the mixture smells sweet and transfer the inner pot to a large bowl of ice water to cool and stop the cooking. 11. transfer the cooled amazake to a large sterilized container for storage. 12. to serve, take out the portion needed, dilute with hot or iced water to your preferred consistency, and serve chilled or warm. 13. to make amazake with sake lees, tear 120 g sake lees into small pieces. 14. bring 960 ml water to a boil in a large pot. 15. using a mesh sieve, dissolve the sake lees into the boiling water, softening them so they dissolve more easily. 16. once dissolved, add 50 g sugar and 1 pinch diamond crystal kosher salt. 17. let the mixture cook and reduce for approximately 15 minutes to your preferred consistency. 18. serve the amazake hot or warm and enjoy.

title: Apple Strudel
text: apple strudel ingredients - 5 תפוחים ירוקים חמוצים - 25 גרם חמאה או מרגרינה - 2 כפות מיץ לימון - 2 כפות סוכר - 1 כף קינמון - 1 כוס אגוזי מלך קצוצים - 3 דפים של בצק - חלמון ביצה - שומשום instructions 1. קלפו ותחתכו לקוביות קטנות 5 תפוחים ירוקים חמוצים. 2. המיסו 25 גרם חמאה או מרגרינה והכניסו את התפוחים. 3. הוסיפו 2 כפות מיץ לימון ובשלו עד לריכוך. 4. סננו את הנוזלים וקררו. 5. הוסיפו 2 כפות סוכר וכף קינמון וערבבו. 6. הוסיפו כוס אגוזי מלך קצוצים. 7. חלקו את הדפים לשלוש חלקים והכינו 3 מאפים. 8. הברישו בחלמון וזרעו שומשום. 9. אפו ב-180 מעלות ללא מצב טורבו למשך חצי שעה. 10. הגישו את ה-strudel.

title: Arroz Rojo
text: arroz rojo ingredients - 200g long-grain rice - 30ml olive oil - 1 medium onion - 4 cloves of garlic - 1 large carrot - 1 red bell pepper - 4 tomatoes - 240ml peas - 2 red chilies - 250ml vegetable broth - 2ml salt - 2ml pepper - 2ml cumin - 5ml chili powder instructions no instructions provided.

title: Sourdough Bread
text: sourdough bread source: jamieoliver.com ingredients - 50g mature sourdough starter - 50g strong white bread flour - 100g levain starter - 400g organic strong white bread flour - 100g organic whole wheat flour - 8ml fine salt - fine semolina flour, for dusting - semolina, for dusting instructions 1. the night before you want to bake, make the levain starter by pouring 50ml of tepid water into a large mixing bowl and gently stirring in the mature sourdough starter until fully dissolved, then repeat with the flour until smooth and combined. 2. leave the levain covered in a warm place for at least 8 hours until lots of bubbles appear on the surface and the dough has a milky-sweet aroma. 3. the next day, pour 325ml of tepid water into a large mixing bowl and add 100g of the levain, which should float, then gently stir it into the water until fully dissolved, and repeat with both flours, covering with a damp cloth and resting in a warm place for 1 hour. 4. add the salt and 25ml of tepid water, scrunching them into the dough until fully combined, then set aside covered in a warm place for 30 minutes. 5. wet your hand slightly and give the dough four folds in the bowl, one at each corner, and repeat this process another three times at 30-minute intervals, turning the dough four times in total across 2 hours, then cover and leave to rise in a warm place for another 2 hours. 6. tip the dough onto a clean surface and gently dust the top with a handful of semolina flour, then roughly shape into a round while keeping as much air in the dough as possible, and rest covered for 30 minutes. 7. dust a basket or cane banneton with semolina flour or use a medium bowl lined with a clean floured tea towel, then lightly flour the dough and flip it over so the flour side is on the worktop, gently shape into a round, and place it in your floured basket, banneton or tea towel-lined bowl. 8. cover the dough with a shower cap or oiled cling film and allow to rest for 1 to 2 hours until increased in size by a quarter and looking bubbly, then transfer your dough in its basket or bowl to the fridge to rise for another 12 to 16 hours until bubbly and risen by another quarter. 9. place a heavy lidded casserole pot on the bottom shelf of the oven and preheat to 240°c/240°c/gas 9. 10. bring your loaf out of the fridge and scatter semolina over the top, then carefully remove the hot pot from the oven, take off the lid and gently tip your dough out into the pot so the pattern is the right way up, score it with a sharp knife held at a 40 degree angle to the surface of the dough, and carefully cover and return to the oven. 11. reduce the temperature to 230°c/230°c/gas 8 and bake for 30 minutes, then carefully remove the lid and bake for a final 20 minutes until a malted golden brown, and remove to a wire rack to cool.

title: Basic Sourdough
text: basic sourdough source: null ingredients - 530g water - 160g rustic flour - 160g all grain flour - 400g bread flour - 40g mixed grains (flax, sesame, pumpkin, sunflower) - 220g 100% levin (sourdough starter) - 16g salt instructions 1. perform a 30-minute autolyse with water and flour. 2. add the remaining ingredients and mix for 5 minutes. 3. perform lamination and let rest for 30 minutes. 4. bulk ferment outside for 5 hours. 5. place in the refrigerator overnight. 6. shape the dough and bake in a hot oven, optionally allowing an additional hour rise before baking if desired.

title: Best Fries
text: best fries ingredients - 907g russet potatoes (about 4 large), peeled and cut into 1/4-inch by 1/4-inch fries - 30ml distilled white vinegar - kosher salt - 2 quarts peanut oil instructions 1. place potatoes and vinegar in a saucepan and add 2 quarts of water and 30ml of salt. 2. bring to a boil over high heat and boil for 10 minutes until potatoes are fully tender but not falling apart. 3. drain potatoes and spread on a paper towel-lined rimmed baking sheet to dry for five minutes. 4. heat oil in a 5-quart dutch oven or large wok over high heat to 204°c. 5. add 1/3 of fries to oil and cook for 50 seconds while agitating occasionally with a wire mesh spider, then remove to a second paper towel-lined rimmed baking sheet. 6. repeat with remaining potatoes in two more batches, allowing oil to return to 204°c after each addition. 7. allow potatoes to cool to room temperature, about 30 minutes, or freeze at least overnight or up to 2 months for best results. 8. return oil to 204°c over high heat and fry half of potatoes until crisp and light golden brown, about 3 1/2 minutes, adjusting heat to maintain around 182°c. 9. drain fries in a bowl lined with paper towels and season immediately with kosher salt. 10. keep cooked fries hot and crisp on a wire rack set on a sheet tray in a 93°c oven while the second batch is cooked. 11. serve immediately.

title: Artisan Bread
text: artisan bread ingredients - 330g bread flour - 330g shogun whole flour - 150g starter (started 4 hours earlier) - 750ml water - 20g salt - 40ml olive oil instructions 1. mix dough in mixer for 13 minutes. 2. after 2 hours, perform 100 folds. 3. let dough rest overnight in fridge. 4. divide dough into 4 bowls and fold three times, then flour. 5. proof in poika for 15 minutes. 6. proof outside of poika for 30 minutes.

title: Cabbage Salads Collection
text: cabbage salads collection burmese lethok with cabbage and ginger ingredients - 454g green cabbage, in slivers (about half a small to medium cabbage) - 8ml salt - juice of 1/2 lime - 10ml fish sauce (or soy sauce) - 45ml shallot oil - 1 plum tomato, deseeded and sliced into slivers - 30ml sushi-style pickled ginger (gari) - 45ml fried shallots - 15ml toasted sesame seeds - 120ml peanuts, crushed instructions 1. hand crush the green cabbage and salt it with 8ml salt, then let it sit for 45 minutes. 2. combine the salted cabbage with lime juice and fish sauce. 3. drizzle with shallot oil and toss to combine. 4. top with sliced plum tomato, pickled ginger, fried shallots, sesame seeds, and crushed peanuts. lebanese malfouf salad ingredients - 454g green cabbage, in slivers (about half a small to medium cabbage) - 8ml salt - 30ml tahini - juice of 1/2 lemon - 2-45ml olive oil - black pepper to taste - 120ml chopped parsley - 5ml garlic powder - 8ml mint powder instructions 1. hand crush the green cabbage and salt it with 8ml salt, then let it sit for 45 minutes. 2. in a bowl, whisk together tahini, lemon juice, and olive oil. 3. toss the salted cabbage with the tahini dressing. 4. season with black pepper, garlic powder, and mint powder. 5. fold in the chopped parsley and serve. american southern style coleslaw (kfc style) ingredients - 454g green cabbage, in slivers (about half a small to medium cabbage) - 8ml salt - 1 large carrot, julienned or grated - 1/2 white onion, sliced - 30ml distilled vinegar - 60ml mayonnaise - 15ml white sugar - 2ml celery seeds - black pepper to taste instructions 1. hand crush the green cabbage and salt it with 8ml salt, then let it sit for 45 minutes. 2. combine the salted cabbage with julienned carrot and sliced onion. 3. in a separate bowl, whisk together vinegar, mayonnaise, sugar, and celery seeds. 4. pour the dressing over the cabbage mixture and toss to combine. 5. season with black pepper to taste and serve.

title: Chicken Breast on a Ninja Woodfire Electric Grill
text: chicken breast on a ninja woodfire electric grill ingredients - chicken breasts (boneless, skinless) - olive oil - salt and pepper - optional: marinade or dry rub of your choice instructions 1. turn on your ninja woodfire grill and set it to the grill setting, preheating to about 204°c (205°c). 2. pound the chicken breasts to an even thickness if they are thick for even cooking. 3. lightly coat the chicken breasts with olive oil to prevent sticking and add moisture. 4. season both sides of the chicken with salt, pepper, or your preferred seasoning blend, and let it sit for at least 30 minutes (or overnight in the fridge) if using a marinade. 5. once the grill is preheated, place the chicken breasts on the grill grates. 6. cook for about 6 to 8 minutes on each side, avoiding pressing down on the chicken while it cooks. 7. use a meat thermometer to ensure the internal temperature reaches 74°c (75°c). 8. remove the chicken from the grill and let it rest for 5 minutes to allow the juices to redistribute throughout the meat. 9. slice and serve the chicken breast with your favorite sides or use it in salads, sandwiches, or other dishes.

title: Chilli Peanut Brownies
text: chilli peanut brownies source: mobkitchen.co.uk ingredients - 5 eggs - 350g dark chocolate (70%) - 300g unsalted butter - 400g caster sugar - 215g self rising flour - 90g cocoa powder - 52ml dried chilli flakes - 100g roasted peanuts (salted or roasted) - salt - 1 lime (to serve) - 5ml chilli flakes (to serve) - 5ml salt (to serve) instructions 1. preheat the oven to 185°c/185°c. 2. whisk all the eggs in a large mixing bowl and break in the dark chocolate, then set aside. 3. on medium heat, melt all the butter in a large saucepan, watching closely to ensure it doesn't brown, then add the caster sugar and stir frequently until you have a thick, golden consistency. 4. remove the butter mixture from the heat and pour it into the egg and chocolate mix, stirring consistently until the chocolate has melted and you have a rich batter. 5. sieve in the flour and cocoa powder and mix until you get a smooth texture. 6. add the chilli flakes and peanuts and give it a final stir. 7. line your baking tin with greaseproof paper by scrunching it up and flattening it across the tin. 8. pour the mixture in and bang the kitchen surface to bring air bubbles to the top, then use the back of a spoon to even out the brownie surface and sprinkle with salt. 9. bake for 25 minutes until the brownies develop a very thin crust with a slight wobble. 10. transfer the brownies to a cooling rack and leave to cool to room temperature, then chill in the fridge overnight or in the freezer for a couple of hours. 11. serve with a generous handful of lime zest, salt, and chilli flakes for the ultimate flavour kick.

title: Chilli Con Carne
text: chilli con carne ingredients - 500g pack of beef chopmeat - 1-2 large onions, peeled and chopped - 1 red pepper - 2 garlic cloves, finely chopped - 1-15ml sweet paprika - 5ml hot chili powder - 1-15ml dried cumin - 400g or 2 tins of chopped tomatoes - 240ml beef stock - 30ml tomato puree - 180ml dry soaked and cooked beans or 1 tin of black or red beans, rinsed and drained - 2ml dried marjoram or dried oregano - salt and freshly cracked black pepper instructions no instructions provided.

title: Chocolate Cake Base
text: chocolate cake base ingredients - 118.3 ml boiling water - 2.8 grams instant espresso powder - 42.5 grams semi-sweet chocolate - 118.3 grams all-purpose flour - 183.3 grams granulated sugar - 33.3 grams unsweetened cocoa powder - 2.4 grams baking soda - 2.4 grams baking powder - 2.4 grams salt - 1 large egg - 120 ml buttermilk - 58.3 ml vegetable oil - 3.3 ml vanilla extract instructions 1. preheat the oven to 177°c and line three 8-inch round cake pans with parchment paper and grease with butter or nonstick cooking spray. 2. in a medium bowl, stir together the boiling water, espresso powder, and semi-sweet chocolate until the chocolate has dissolved and the mixture is smooth, then set aside to cool. 3. in a large mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, cocoa powder, sugar, baking soda, baking powder, and salt until combined. 4. in another bowl, whisk together the eggs, buttermilk, vegetable oil, and vanilla, then pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until smooth. 5. add the cooled espresso-chocolate mixture to the batter and stir until just combined. 6. divide the batter evenly among the three pans and bake in the oven for 31-33 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out with few crumbs attached. 7. remove the cakes from the oven and allow to cool.

title: chocolate cream cake
text: chocolate cream cake ingredients instructions nana’s devil’s food cake \240ml cake flour 2ml salt 2ml baking powder 5ml baking soda 90ml cup cocoa 240ml sugar 120ml oil 120ml milk 120ml coffee – room temp 1 egg 2ml vanilla whisk all dry ingredients together. beat wet ingredients until foamy. slowly fold dry into wet ingredients. pour into greased \& floured tube pan. bake at 191°c until done, 25\-30 mins/96°c

title: Cinnamon Roll in a Mug
text: cinnamon roll in a mug ingredients - 50g self-raising flour - 60g greek yoghurt - 10g butter, melted - 15ml granulated sugar - 2ml cinnamon - 45ml powdered sugar - 10ml milk instructions 1. mix together the self-raising flour, greek yoghurt, and melted butter. 2. combine the granulated sugar and cinnamon in a small bowl. 3. swirl the cinnamon sugar mixture into the dough. 4. place the mixture in a mug and microwave on high for about 50 seconds at 750w, being careful not to overcook as the dough will become chewy. 5. mix the powdered sugar with milk to create a glaze and drizzle over the warm cinnamon roll.

title: Classic Moussaka Without Potatoes
text: classic moussaka without potatoes ingredients - 500g ground lamb or beef - 1 large onion, finely chopped - 2-3 garlic cloves, minced - 1 can (400g) crushed tomatoes - 30ml tomato paste - 120ml red wine (optional) - 5ml ground cinnamon - 2ml ground allspice - 2ml ground cumin - salt and pepper to taste - 45ml olive oil - 1 bay leaf - 30ml chopped fresh parsley - 2-3 large eggplants (aubergines), sliced into 1 cm thick rounds - olive oil for frying or roasting - 60ml butter - 60ml flour - 720ml milk, warmed - 2 egg yolks - 120ml grated parmesan or kefalotyri cheese - nutmeg, grated (optional) instructions 1. salt the eggplant slices and let them sit for about 30 minutes to release excess moisture, then rinse and pat them dry. 2. brush the eggplant with olive oil and either roast in a preheated oven at 200°c (204°c) for 20-25 minutes until golden, or fry them in olive oil until soft and browned, then set aside. 3. heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat and sauté the onions and garlic until softened. 4. add the ground meat and cook until browned. 5. stir in the tomato paste, crushed tomatoes, red wine (if using), cinnamon, allspice, cumin, bay leaf, salt, and pepper, and let it simmer for 20-30 minutes until the sauce thickens. 6. remove from heat and stir in chopped parsley, then discard the bay leaf. 7. in a medium saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat and whisk in the flour, cooking for 2-3 minutes to make a roux. 8. gradually add warm milk, whisking constantly to avoid lumps, and continue stirring until the sauce thickens. 9. remove from heat, then whisk in the egg yolks, cheese, salt, pepper, and nutmeg. 10. preheat the oven to 180°c (177°c) and layer half of the roasted eggplant slices on the bottom of a greased baking dish. 11. spread the meat sauce evenly over the eggplants. 12. layer the remaining eggplants on top of the meat sauce. 13. pour the béchamel sauce over the top, spreading it evenly. 14. bake in the preheated oven for 45-50 minutes until the top is golden and bubbly. 15. let it cool for about 10-15 minutes before serving.

title: Coffee Cake Muffins
text: coffee cake muffins source: damndelicious.net ingredients - 360ml all-purpose flour - 120ml brown sugar - 10ml baking powder - 5ml ground cinnamon - 1ml baking soda - 1ml salt - 180ml milk - 80ml canola oil - 2 large eggs - 80ml sugar - 80ml brown sugar - 5ml ground cinnamon - 1ml salt - 120ml unsalted butter (melted) - 360ml all-purpose flour - 60ml confectioners’ sugar - 2ml vanilla extract - 5ml milk instructions 1. preheat oven to 191°c. line a 12-cup standard muffin tin with paper liners or coat with nonstick spray; set aside. 2. in a large bowl, combine flour, sugar, baking powder, cinnamon, baking soda and salt. 3. in a large glass measuring cup or another bowl, whisk together milk, canola oil and eggs. pour mixture over dry ingredients and stir using a rubber spatula just until moist. 4. scoop the batter evenly into the muffin tray. sprinkle with crumb topping, using your fingertips to gently press the crumbs into the batter. place into oven and bake for 15-17 minutes, or until a tester inserted in the center comes out clean. 5. when the muffins are done, cool for 10 minutes and drizzle the glaze on each muffin. 6. allow glaze to set before serving. 7. in a medium bowl, combine sugars, cinnamon and salt. stir in melted butter. add flour and stir using a rubber spatula just until moist. spread out mixture on parchment paper to dry until ready to use. 8. in a small bowl, whisk together confectioners’ sugar, vanilla and milk until smooth. if the glaze is too thin, add more confectioners’ sugar as needed.

title: Coffee Butter Muffins
text: coffee butter muffins ingredients - flour - brown sugar - baking powder - baking soda - cinnamon - salt - milk - butter - eggs - vanilla - sugar - melted butter note: specific quantities not provided in source text instructions 1. preheat oven to 375 degrees and line muffin tin with paper liners. 2. in a large bowl, whisk together flour, brown sugar, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon and salt, then make a well in the center. 3. in a smaller bowl or large measuring cup, whisk together milk, butter, eggs and vanilla until smooth. 4. pour the wet mixture into the dry bowl and mix with a hand blender or by hand until you have a thick but smooth batter. 5. for the crumb topping, stir together flour, sugars, and cinnamon in a medium bowl, then add melted butter and stir with a fork until the mixture is crumbly and resembles wet sand. 6. for the cinnamon swirl, combine sugar and cinnamon in a small bowl. 7. scoop 30ml of batter into each muffin cavity, place a teaspoon of cinnamon sugar mixture on top, swirl quickly, and top with more batter, filling the tin ¾ to the top. 8. sprinkle about a heaping tablespoon of crumb topping on top of each muffin, covering the tops. 9. bake for 15-17 minutes until the crumbly tops are golden and a toothpick inserted in the middle comes out clean. 10. remove from oven and allow muffins to cool to room temperature in the pan, then transfer to a wire rack. 11. once cooled, drizzle a little glaze over the cooled muffins.

title: Coffee Cake
text: coffee cake ingredients - 600ml all-purpose flour - 240ml packed brown sugar - 120ml plus 15ml granulated sugar - 5ml salt - 5ml nutmeg - 180ml canola oil - 5ml cinnamon - 5ml baking soda - 5ml baking powder - 1 large egg - 240ml buttermilk instructions no instructions provided.

title: Cookies
text: cookies ingredients - 240ml white sugar - 240ml brown sugar - 240ml oleo (margarine) - 240ml oil - 1 egg - 5ml vanilla - 5ml cream of tartar - 5ml baking soda - 240ml rice crispies - 240ml quick oatmeal - 5ml salt - 240ml flaked coconut - 240ml chopped nuts - 840ml flour instructions 1. mix all ingredients in order. 2. drop mixture by the tablespoonful onto a baking sheet. 3. press down with fingers. 4. bake at 350 degrees for 13 minutes.

title: Cream Cheese Coffee Cake
text: cream cheese coffee cake ingredients - 2½ cups all-purpose flour - 240ml sugar - 5ml baking soda - 2ml baking powder - 1ml salt - 240ml (225g) unsalted butter, softened - 3 large eggs - 10ml vanilla extract - 240ml buttermilk - 90ml unsalted butter, softened - 30ml cinnamon - 240ml all-purpose flour - 240ml brown sugar - 2 packages (450g total) cream cheese, softened - 120ml sugar - 2 large eggs - 5ml vanilla extract - 240ml brown sugar - 15ml cinnamon - 1ml salt - 120ml (115g) unsalted butter, melted - 480ml all-purpose flour - 240ml powdered sugar - 2–45ml milk - 5ml vanilla extract instructions 1. preheat oven to 177°c (175°c) and grease a 9x13 baking pan. 2. beat butter and sugar until fluffy, add eggs one at a time, then vanilla, and alternately mix in the flour mixture and buttermilk, beginning and ending with flour. 3. mix butter, cinnamon, flour, and brown sugar until crumbly to make the cinnamon filling. 4. beat cream cheese and sugar until smooth, add eggs and vanilla, and mix until combined for the cheesecake layer. 5. combine brown sugar, cinnamon, salt, melted butter, and flour until crumbly to make the streusel. 6. spread half the cake batter in the pan, scatter cinnamon filling, spread cheesecake layer, add remaining cake batter, and top with streusel. 7. bake for 45–50 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean and cool completely. 8. whisk together powdered sugar, milk, and vanilla extract and drizzle the glaze over the cooled cake.

title: Re: curd meat basturma בסטרומה
text: re: curd meat basturma בסטרומה ingredients instructions to make a traditional curd meat basturma, you generally want to let the meat hang in the refrigerator to dry and cure for around 10 to 14 days before cold smoking. here’s a more detailed timeline and tips for each phase: 1\. dry curing phase (10\-14 days) goal: remove excess moisture and allow the flavors of the spices to penetrate the meat. process: hang the meat in the refrigerator (ideally on a wire rack to allow airflow) at temperatures between 34\-4°c (1\-4°c). check for firmness, which indicates it’s drying well. duration: 10 to 14 days, or until the surface is dry, and the meat feels firmer to the touch. 2\. cold smoking phase timing: once the meat has fully cured and dried in the refrigerator, cold smoke it at around 70\-32°c (21\-32°c) for 12\-24 hours depending on the smokiness you prefer. keep the smoking chamber's temperature low to avoid cooking the meat while infusing it with smoke. tips air circulation: ensure the meat hangs freely with good air circulation on all sides. weight monitoring: weighing the meat before and after curing can help you check for moisture loss (ideal is about a 30% weight reduction). patience for flavor: the longer the curing phase, the more intense the flavor. let me know if you'd like help with the spice blend or any further steps for basturma!

title: Danish Rye Bread (Rugbrød)
text: danish rye bread (rugbrød) source: nordicfoodliving.com ingredients - 2 dl cracked rye kernels - 2 dl cracked wheat - 2 dl flax seed/linseeds - 2 dl sunflower seeds - 15ml malt syrup ((or dark syrup)) - 4 dl sour dough - 8 dl water - 4 dl all-purpose flour - 4 dl rye flour - 15ml salt - 30ml gravy browning ((can be omitted)) instructions 1. in a large bowl; add the cracked rye kernels, cracked wheat, flax seeds, sunflower seeds, water, malt syrup and the sour dough. let it all soak for minimum 8 hours. this can with advantage be done in the evening, so that you can continue the morning after. 2. after about 8 hours; add the rest of the ingredients and let the rye bread dough rise for about 1.5 hours. 3. divide the dough into two portions and pour it into two normal bread pans. cover the bread pans with some plastic wrap (or a damp dishtowel). let the dough rise for about 1-2 hours or until the bread pan is full of dough. 4. bake the rye breads at 180 c (182°c) for about 1 hour. 5. when done; remove the breads for the bread pans and let them cool off. when the breads are cooled off; keep them in an air tight container or a plastic bag.

title: Authentic Niter Kibbeh (Ethiopian Spiced Clarified Butter)
text: authentic niter kibbeh (ethiopian spiced clarified butter) source: daringgourmet.com ingredients - 454g unsalted butter, cubed - 60ml chopped yellow onion - 45ml minced fresh garlic - 30ml minced fresh ginger - 1 2-inch cinnamon stick - 5ml whole black peppercorns - 3 black cardamom pods ((not the green cardamom variety)) - 3 whole cloves - 5ml fenugreek seeds - 5ml coriander seeds - 5ml dried oregano - 2ml cumin seeds - 1ml ground nutmeg - 1ml ground turmeric - 15ml besobela (,if you can find it, otherwise omit (see blog post)) - 15ml kosseret (,if you can find it, otherwise omit (see blog post)) instructions 1. toast the whole spices over medium heat in a dry skillet for a few minutes until very fragrant.  be careful not to scorch the spices or they will become bitter.  set aside. 2. place all the ingredients in a medium saucepan and bring it to an extremely low simmer.  continue to simmer over low for at least one hour or up to 90 minutes.  be very careful not to burn the butter.  if it burns it will be bitter and there is no salvaging it. 3. pour everything through a fine-mesh cheesecloth. (no need to skim off the foam, everything will be removed during straining.) pour the niter kibbeh into a jar, let it cool, and cover so that it is airtight. it will keep at room temperature for several weeks, in the fridge for a few months, and even longer in the freezer (it will be hard in the fridge and freezer, let it come to room temp for easy scooping). makes about 480ml.

title: Falafel
text: falafel source: the cooking foodie ingredients - 480ml (400g) dried chickpeas - 1 small onion - 3-5 garlic cloves - 1/3 bunch parsley - 1/2 bunch cilantro - 60ml (30g) flour, breadcrumbs, or chickpea flour for gluten free version - 1¼ teaspoon salt - 1ml pepper - 5ml cumin - 5ml paprika - 10ml baking soda - oil for frying instructions 1. put the chickpeas in a large bowl and cover them with 2-3 inches of cold water, then let soak overnight and wash and drain. 2. put the washed and drained chickpeas into a food processor with garlic cloves, onion, parsley, cilantro, baking soda, and spices, then process until smooth but crumbly. 3. transfer the mixture to a large bowl, add breadcrumbs, and mix until combined. 4. cover the mixture and refrigerate for 1 hour. 5. heat oil to 360˚f (180˚c). 6. remove falafel mixture from the fridge and using wet hands shape into 1-inch balls. 7. fry the falafels in batches of 4-6 at a time until golden brown and crispy, about 3-4 minutes, then transfer to a paper towel. 8. serve as is or in a pita bread with salad and tahini sauce.

title: Fire Cider
text: fire cider ingredients - 18 cm piece of freshly peeled and grated ginger root - 18 cm piece of freshly grated horseradish root - 18 cm piece of freshly grated turmeric root - 1 medium onion, chopped - 10 cloves or 1 head of garlic, crushed or chopped - 2 organic jalapeño peppers, chopped - 1 whole lemon with zest and juice - 1ml cayenne powder - 1 cinnamon stick - a few allspice berries - a few whole cloves - 1 whole orange with zest and juice - 30ml chopped rosemary and/or thyme and/or oregano and/or sage leaves - 2ml black peppercorns - organic unfiltered apple cider vinegar - 60ml raw honey, or to taste instructions 1. add ginger, horseradish, onion, garlic, jalapeño peppers, lemon zest and juice, rosemary, turmeric, cayenne powder, and about 25 cranks of fresh black pepper into a food processor and pulse until all vegetables are in small, semi-uniform pieces similar to the texture of sauerkraut. 2. put all the processed ingredients into a quart-sized glass jar. 3. pour apple cider vinegar into the jar until all ingredients are fully covered and the vinegar reaches the top of the jar, ensuring all ingredients are submerged to prevent spoilage. 4. use a piece of natural parchment paper under the lid to keep the vinegar from touching the metal, or use a plastic lid if available. 5. shake the jar to combine all ingredients and store in a dark, cool place for 4-6 weeks, shaking the jar for a few seconds every day. 6. after one month, use a mesh strainer or cheesecloth to strain out the solids, pouring the vinegar into a clean jar and squeezing out as much liquid as possible. 7. add honey to the liquid and stir until incorporated. 8. taste the fire cider and add more honey if needed until desired sweetness is reached. 9. store in a sealed container in the refrigerator or in a cold, dark place. 10. drink 1-30ml when needed.

title: Garlic Ginger Chicken Potstickers
text: garlic ginger chicken potstickers ingredients - 450g (454g) ground chicken - 180ml shiitake mushrooms, finely diced - 60ml fresh cilantro, chopped - 3 green onions, thinly sliced - 3 garlic cloves, minced - 30ml soy sauce - 15ml sesame oil - 15ml fresh ginger, grated - 15ml rice wine vinegar - 2ml black pepper - 1ml red pepper flakes - 36 round wonton (gyoza) wrappers - 60ml vegetable oil instructions 1. in a large bowl, combine ground chicken, shiitake mushrooms, cilantro, green onions, garlic, soy sauce, sesame oil, ginger, rice wine vinegar, black pepper, and red pepper flakes, and mix well. 2. place a wonton wrapper on a clean surface, place 1 heaping teaspoon of filling in the center, moisten the edges with water, fold over, and press to seal, then pleat the edges to form a dumpling shape and repeat with remaining wrappers and filling. 3. heat 15ml vegetable oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, working in batches, add dumplings flat-side down and cook until the bottoms are golden, 2–3 minutes. 4. add 2–45ml water to the pan, cover immediately, and steam until cooked through, about 3–4 minutes, then remove lid and let any remaining water evaporate and repeat with remaining dumplings.

title: Garlic Pickle (Lahsun Achar)
text: garlic pickle (lahsun achar) source: tarladalal.com ingredients - 120ml garlic cloves, peeled - 45ml mustard oil - 1ml turmeric powder - 30ml lemon juice - 15ml chilli powder - 5ml finely chopped jaggery - 2ml salt - 10ml split mustard seeds - 1ml split fenugreek seeds - 1ml cumin seeds - 1ml crushed coriander seeds - 1ml asafoetida instructions 1. transfer split mustard seeds, split fenugreek seeds, cumin seeds, crushed coriander seeds, and asafoetida to a small mixer jar. 2. without using any water, blend them in a mixer jar to a smooth powder and keep aside. 3. heat the oil in a non-stick kadhai and add the garlic cloves. 4. add turmeric powder and sauté on a slow flame for 3 to 4 minutes or until the garlic cloves are soft, stirring continuously. 5. add the lemon juice and cook on a slow flame for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring occasionally. 6. add the chilli powder, jaggery, and salt and cook on a slow flame for another 2 to 3 minutes or until the jaggery has dissolved, stirring occasionally. 7. add the prepared masala powder, mix well, and cook for another minute. 8. remove from the flame, cool completely, and store in a sterilized glass jar. 9. store the garlic pickle in a cool dry place and stir it with a clean and dry spoon once a day after storing in the glass jar. 10. the garlic pickle is ready to serve after 1 week, though it tastes better the longer it is preserved.

title: icecream for espresso
text: icecream for espresso james hoffmann the ultimate espresso affogato ingredients • 110g sugar • 60g skimmed milk powder • 550g milk (divided into 250g and 300g) • 165g double/heavy cream (divided into 65g and 100g) • 0.5g xanthan • 0.5g locust bean gum • 0.1g kappa carageenan • 1g vanilla bean pulp about work weird coffee science the ultimate series contact • 5g vanilla bean paste instructions 1. thoroughly mix the sugar, xanthan, locust bean gum and carageenan together in a bowl with a whisk. 2. pour 250g of milk and 65g of double cream into a pan 3. add the sugar mixture to the pan and heat 4. whisk to combine as the pan heats, and once it begins to simmer reduce the heat. it should nearly boil, and hold it there, whisking vigorously for 60 seconds 5. in a separate mixing bowl, or blender, combine the hot, thickened cream mixture with 60g of skimmed milk powder, the remaining 100g of cream and 300g of milk and the vanilla pulp and paste. whisk/blend until completely combined. 6. chill in an ice bath. 7. churn in your ice cream machine. 8. once churned and ice cream, then transfer to a container and put in the freezer to further firm up. 9. make sure your serving vessel (cups/bowls etc) are frozen before use. 10. before scooping, allow to come to -10c. 11. per serving, allow approximately 50g of ice cream per single shot (16-20g) of liquid espresso 12. pull the shot directly onto the ice cream in the frozen vessel. 13. serve immediately!

title: Greek Meatballs recipe (Keftedes/ Keftethes)
text: greek meatballs recipe (keftedes/ keftethes) source: mygreekdish.com ingredients - 500g ground beef (510g) - 200g ground pork (198g) - 1 medium red onion, grated - 1 medium clove of garlic, minced - 150g stale bread (142g), soaked in water and squeezed to remove the excess water - 1 large egg - 22ml fresh parsley, chopped (optional) - 22ml fresh spearmint (chopped) and a pinch dried. or 11ml fresh regular mint - 30ml olive oil - 22ml red wine vinegar - 5ml oregano - 5ml salt - 5ml pepper - oil for frying - flour for dredging instructions 1. to prepare this traditional greek meatballs recipe (keftedes), add all the ingredients into a large bowl and mix well (for about 5-10 minutes), squeezing with your hands, to allow the flavours to blend. cover the bowl with some plastic wrap and let it rest in the fridge for 1 hour. 2. turn the mixture for the keftedes out of the fridge and roll into meatballs the size of a walnut (or bigger if you prefer). if you’re frying them, dredge the rolled meatballs lightly in flour making sure to shake off any excess. fry until nicely browned on all sides. 3. the traditional way of cooking greek meatballs (keftedes) is frying them. fry the keftedes in batches of 10-15 at a time, until nicely browned on all sides. 4. instead of frying you can bake / grill the keftedes in the oven. preheat the oven at 200c, place the un-floured keftedes on greased baking sheet about an inch apart. bake for about 20 minutes, turning the meatballs upside down midway through cooking time. the grilled version is much lighter than the fried so theres not excuse to not trying it now! 5. keftedes (greek meatballs) are ideally served as an appetizer (meze) with some creamy tzatziki sauce and pita breads or as a main course with some basmati rice and a greek salad. enjoy!

title: Keto Brownies
text: keto brownies ingredients - 130g unsalted butter - 200g erythritol - 80g cocoa powder - 2ml salt - 2 eggs at room temperature - 70g almond flour - 40g peanut butter instructions 1. position a rack in the lower third of your oven and preheat to 177°c/180°c. 2. line the bottom and sides of an 8x8-inch baking pan with parchment paper and set aside. 3. add butter, sweetener, cocoa powder and salt to a medium heatproof bowl and melt over a water bath or using the microwave until all the butter and sweetener has melted and the mixture is well incorporated. 4. remove from heat and allow the mixture to cool slightly. 5. add one egg at a time, stirring well after each one until completely incorporated. 6. add almond flour and stir vigorously until fully blended, about a minute. 7. pour the batter into the prepared pan. 8. divide peanut butter into 9 equal amounts and place on top of the brownie batter. 9. swirl the peanut butter into the batter. 10. bake for 15-25 minutes, or until the center is just set and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out slightly moist. 11. cut into 16 equally sized squares.

title: Khachapuri Georgian Cheese Bread
text: khachapuri georgian cheese bread ingredients for the dough: - 5ml salt - 5ml dry active yeast - 15ml granulated sugar - 840ml all-purpose flour - 240ml water - 120ml milk - 15ml olive oil for the filling: - 360ml farmers cheese - 360ml shredded mozzarella - 360ml feta cheese - 5 eggs - unsalted butter (optional) instructions 1. in the bowl of a stand mixer, combine the salt, yeast, sugar, and flour. 2. heat water and milk to about 46°c, then pour it into the bowl of dry ingredients. 3. begin kneading the dough with the hook attachment until it is close to being smooth and elastic. 4. add the oil into the dough and knead for another minute. 5. drizzle a little bit of olive oil onto the bottom and sides of a deep bowl, place the dough inside, and cover with plastic wrap. 6. set the bowl in a warm place until the dough doubles in size, about 1 hour. 7. remove the plastic wrap and press into the dough a few times with your hands, then cover with plastic wrap once more and let it sit in a warm place for another 30 minutes. 8. meanwhile, combine the farmers cheese, feta, and mozzarella in a bowl. 9. remove the dough from the bowl and place it onto a floured surface, then cut it into 4 equal pieces. 10. spread each piece of the dough into a circle about 9 inches in diameter, then roll 2 opposite sides of the circle towards the center so it ends up in a boat-like shape and pinch the corners together. 11. transfer the khachapuri onto a baking sheet lined with greased parchment paper. 12. stuff each khachapuri with the cheese mixture, beat 1 egg with a teaspoon of water, then brush the dough with egg wash. 13. bake in a preheated 450 degrees oven for about 15 minutes or until the crust becomes golden brown. 14. make a well in the center of each khachapuri with the back of a spoon (about 3 inches in diameter) and drop 1 egg into each well, then stick a few small pieces of butter into the cheese. 15. return the khachapuri back into the oven and bake for another 5-6 minutes, then serve immediately with the cheese and egg mixed together with a fork.

title: Mac and Cheese
text: mac and cheese ingredients - 60ml butter - 45ml flour - 480ml milk (low-fat is ok) - 2ml smoked paprika - 2ml garlic powder - 5ml hot sauce (optional) - 5ml yellow mustard, or 2ml mustard powder - ground black pepper to taste - salt to taste - 2¼ cups water - 227g elbow macaroni, uncooked - 480ml (227g) shredded cheddar cheese - 180ml (85g) shredded mozzarella cheese instructions 1. melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. 2. add the flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring frequently, until the flour is lightly cooked. 3. whisk about half of the milk into the flour mixture until it becomes a thick roux. 4. add the remaining milk and whisk until smooth. 5. add the smoked paprika, garlic powder, hot sauce (if using), yellow mustard or mustard powder, pepper, and salt, and stir to combine. 6. add the elbow macaroni and stir occasionally until the mixture comes to a simmer. 7. cook the pasta at a simmer, stirring often, for 8-11 minutes or until the sauce thickens and the macaroni is just cooked al dente. 8. turn off the heat and stir in the cheddar and mozzarella cheeses. 9. taste and adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper to taste.

title: pickled beets סלק כבוש
text: pickled beets סלק כבוש ingredients instructions סלק כבוש הזה מוסיף מתיקות חריפה וצבע תוסס לכל ארוחה. תהנו מהם ישר מהצנצנת או במתכונים האהובים עליך. כך תשפרו את המנות שלכם עם סלק כבוש תוצרת בית! רכיבים: \- 4\-5 סלקים בינוניים, קלופים ופרוסים \- 1 כוס חומץ תפוחים \- 1 כוס מים \- 1/2 כוס סוכר \- 1 כפית מלח \- 1 כפית גרגירי פלפל שלמים \- 1 כפית זרעי חרדל \- 2 שיני שום, כתושות \- עלה דפנה אחד הוראות הכנה: 1\. מערבבים בסיר בינוני חומץ תפוחים, מים, סוכר, מלח, גרגירי פלפל שלמים, זרעי חרדל, שום ועלה דפנה. מביאים את התערובת לרתיחה, מנמיכים את האש ונותנים לה להתבשל במשך 5 דקות. 2\. מוסיפים לסיר את הסלקים הפרוסים ומבשלים עוד 5\-7 דקות עד שהסלק רך אך עדיין יש לו פריך קל. 3\. מסירים את הסיר מהאש ונותנים לסלק הכבוש להתקרר לטמפרטורת החדר. 4\. לאחר התקררות מעבירים את הסלק הכבוש ואת נוזל הכבישה לצנצנת או לכלי זכוכית. 5\. מכסים את הצנצנת ומקררים את הסלק הכבוש ל\-24 שעות לפחות כדי לאפשר לטעמים להתפתח. 6\. מגישים את הסלקים הכבושים כתוספת, על סלטים, בסנדוויצ'ים, או תהנו מהם לבד כנשנוש טעים. מקור:

title: Polish Cream Cheese Coffee Cake
text: polish cream cheese coffee cake ingredients - 240ml sugar - 120ml (115g) unsalted butter, softened - 1 large egg - 240ml sour cream - 5ml vanilla extract - 720ml all-purpose flour - 5ml baking soda - 5ml baking powder - 2 packages (450g total) cream cheese, softened - 120ml sugar - 1 large egg - 120ml chopped pecans - 120ml brown sugar - 80ml all-purpose flour - 80ml (75g) unsalted butter, cold and cubed instructions 1. preheat oven to 177°c (175°c) and grease a 9x13 baking pan. 2. beat butter and sugar until light, then add egg, sour cream, and vanilla; mix until combined. 3. stir in flour, baking soda, and baking powder until a soft dough forms. 4. beat cream cheese and sugar until smooth, then mix in egg. 5. combine pecans, brown sugar, flour, and cold butter, then mix with fingertips until crumbly. 6. press two-thirds of the cake dough into the prepared pan. 7. spread cream cheese filling evenly over the dough. 8. drop spoonfuls of remaining dough over the filling. 9. sprinkle streusel over the top. 10. bake for 45 minutes until golden and set, then cool before slicing.

title: Best Baked Potatoes
text: best baked potatoes source: splendid table ingredients - potatoes - salt - water - oil instructions 1. prepare a saltwater brine solution. 2. submerge potatoes in the brine to season the skins. 3. place potatoes on a wire rack set in a baking sheet to allow air circulation. 4. bake potatoes at 232°c until the internal temperature reaches 96°c. 5. brush oil on the potatoes near the end of cooking. 6. continue baking until the outside is crispy like a potato chip.

title: Pretzel
text: pretzel ingredients - 255g warm water - 13g brown sugar - 4g active dry yeast - 200g sourdough discard - 567g all-purpose flour - 12g salt - 56g unsalted butter, softened - 2kg water - 192g baking soda - 1 egg, beaten - flaky sea salt instructions 1. in a large bowl or stand mixer, combine warm water, brown sugar, and yeast and let sit 5 minutes until foamy. 2. add sourdough discard, flour, and salt, mix until a shaggy dough forms, then add softened butter and knead for 8–10 minutes until smooth and elastic. 3. cover and let rise at room temperature for 1 hour, or until noticeably puffed. 4. preheat oven to 232°c and line two baking sheets with parchment. 5. bring water and baking soda to a boil in a large pot. 6. divide dough into 8 equal pieces, roll each into a long rope about 50cm, then shape into a pretzel. 7. working in batches, boil pretzels in the baking soda bath for 30 seconds per side and transfer to prepared baking sheets. 8. brush each pretzel with egg wash and sprinkle with flaky sea salt. 9. bake for 13–15 minutes until deep mahogany brown.
